# API reference

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/pdf/api-reference

PdfReaderState, PdfPage, PdfThumbnail, PdfReader, and the supporting data types.

The public API lives under `dev.nucleusframework.pdfium`. Coordinates in text-layout results are in PDF page points (1 pt = 1/72 inch), with the origin at the bottom-left of the page.

## PdfReaderState

The state holder tied to a single document. Hoist it with `rememberPdfReaderState()`.

```kotlin
@Stable
class PdfReaderState {
    // Snapshot state
    val pageCount: Int        // 0 until a document is open
    val isLoading: Boolean    // true during open()
    val error: PdfError?      // last open() error, if any
    val metadata: PdfMetadata
    var renderScale: Float    // 1.0 = fit-to-width

    // Intents
    suspend fun open(bytes: ByteArray, password: String? = null)
    suspend fun pageSize(pageIndex: Int): PageSize?
    suspend fun pageText(pageIndex: Int): String
    suspend fun pageTextLayout(pageIndex: Int): PageTextLayout?

    // Render ahead-of-display; best-effort, populates the cache
    fun prefetch(pageIndex: Int, widthPx: Int, quality: RenderQuality = RenderQuality.FULL)

    // Release native handles + cached bitmaps (called by rememberPdfReaderState)
    fun dispose()

    companion object {
        const val DEFAULT_CACHE_BYTES: Long = 64L * 1024 * 1024
        const val DEFAULT_THUMBNAIL_CACHE_BYTES: Long = 12L * 1024 * 1024
    }
}

@Composable
fun rememberPdfReaderState(
    cacheBytes: Long = PdfReaderState.DEFAULT_CACHE_BYTES,
    thumbnailCacheBytes: Long = PdfReaderState.DEFAULT_THUMBNAIL_CACHE_BYTES,
): PdfReaderState
```

Bitmaps are keyed by `(pageIndex, quantized_width)`. Both cache budgets are tunable on `rememberPdfReaderState(...)`.

## PdfPage

Renders a single page. Handles progressive rendering (low-res preview to full quality on settle) and debounces size changes internally.

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PdfPage(
    state: PdfReaderState,
    pageIndex: Int,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    contentScale: ContentScale = ContentScale.Fit,
    background: Color = Color.White,
    selectableText: Boolean = false,
    linksEnabled: Boolean = true,
    onLinkClick: ((PdfLink) -> Boolean)? = null,
)
```

- `modifier` controls the layout width; the composable derives the aspect ratio from the PDF page and sets its own height.
- `selectableText = true` enables the pointer-driven selection overlay.
- A standalone `PdfPage` has no list to scroll, so internal GoTo links are only actionable through `onLinkClick`.

## PdfThumbnail

A low-resolution preview of a single page. Renders at `RenderQuality.PREVIEW`, shares the `PdfReaderState` cache, and sizes itself to the modifier-provided width.

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PdfThumbnail(
    state: PdfReaderState,
    pageIndex: Int,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    background: Color = Color.White,
)
```

## PdfReader

A convenience composable — a vertical `LazyColumn` that stacks every page of the document.

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PdfReader(
    state: PdfReaderState,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    contentPadding: PaddingValues = PaddingValues(12.dp),
    pageSpacing: Dp = 16.dp,
)
```

## RenderQuality

```kotlin
enum class RenderQuality {
    // No annotations, no LCD text. Used for thumbnails and progressive previews.
    PREVIEW,

    // Annotations on, no LCD text. Balanced default for on-screen viewing.
    FULL,
}
```

## PageSize, PdfMetadata, PdfError

```kotlin
data class PageSize(val widthPoints: Float, val heightPoints: Float) {
    val aspectRatio: Float // widthPoints / heightPoints, or 1f for degenerate pages
}

data class PdfMetadata(
    val title: String? = null,
    val author: String? = null,
    val subject: String? = null,
    val keywords: String? = null,
    val creator: String? = null,
    val producer: String? = null,
)

sealed class PdfError(open val message: String, open val cause: Throwable? = null) {
    data class InvalidFormat(...) : PdfError(...)
    data class PasswordRequired(...) : PdfError(...)
    data class NativeFailure(...) : PdfError(...)
    data class Io(...) : PdfError(...)
}
```

## PageTextLayout

Returned by `PdfReaderState.pageTextLayout(...)` for building custom text overlays and highlighting tools.

```kotlin
@Immutable
class PageTextLayout {
    val pageIndex: Int
    val pageSize: PageSize
    val rectCount: Int
    val charCount: Int

    // Rect-level (line-level runs from FPDFText_GetRect)
    fun left(i: Int): Float       // in PDF points, origin bottom-left
    fun bottom(i: Int): Float
    fun right(i: Int): Float
    fun top(i: Int): Float
    fun text(i: Int): String      // UTF-8 Unicode

    // Char-level (FPDFText_GetCharBox / FPDFText_GetUnicode)
    fun codepoint(i: Int): Int
    fun charLeft(i: Int): Float
    fun charBottom(i: Int): Float
    fun charRight(i: Int): Float
    fun charTop(i: Int): Float
}
```

To map a rectangle to a rendered bitmap of pixel dimensions `W × H`:

```
scaleX = W / pageSize.widthPoints
scaleY = H / pageSize.heightPoints

screenX = left × scaleX
screenY = H - top × scaleY       // flip Y (PDF is bottom-up)
screenW = (right - left)   × scaleX
screenH = (top   - bottom) × scaleY
```

## What's next

- [Getting started](/docs/pdf/getting-started) — the same API used across a full reader screen.
- [PDF reader overview](/docs/pdf) — supported targets and the render path.

---

# WebView

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/webview

Embed a native web engine in Compose with one API across Android, iOS, web, and desktop.

The WebView library embeds each platform's native web engine in Compose. You write against `WebView`, `WebViewState`, and `WebViewNavigator` once; the library binds to Android WebView, WKWebView, WebView2, WebKit2GTK, or an iframe underneath.

The public API and the Android/iOS implementations follow [compose-webview-multiplatform](https://github.com/KevinnZou/compose-webview-multiplatform). ComposeNativeWebView adds a WasmJs target and a desktop path built on [`NativeView`](/docs/native-content/native-views).

WebView ships from [`NucleusFramework/ComposeNativeWebview`](https://github.com/NucleusFramework/ComposeNativeWebview) with its own release cycle, like the [system tray](/docs/os/tray) and the [PDF reader](/docs/pdf). Its version number is **independent of Nucleus** — pin it separately. The artifact is `dev.nucleusframework:composewebview`, published to Maven Central.

## One API instead of one per platform

| Platform | Native web engine |
| -------- | ----------------- |
| Android  | `android.webkit.WebView` |
| iOS      | WKWebView |
| WasmJs   | `HTMLIFrameElement` |
| Desktop (Linux) | WebKit2GTK via `NativeView` |
| Desktop (macOS) | WKWebView via `NativeView` |
| Desktop (Windows) | WebView2 CompositionController via `NativeView` |

Without a shared layer, a multiplatform app integrates and maintains each engine separately. ComposeNativeWebView replaces that with a single Compose surface and the same navigation, cookie, and JavaScript model on every target.

## Add the dependency

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
kotlin {
    sourceSets {
        commonMain.dependencies {
            implementation("dev.nucleusframework:composewebview:<version>")
        }
    }
}
```

The same artifact covers Android, iOS, Desktop (JVM), and WasmJs.

## Show a page

Hoist a `WebViewState` and drop `WebView` into your layout:

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxSize
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import dev.nucleusframework.webview.web.WebView
import dev.nucleusframework.webview.web.rememberWebViewState

@Composable
fun HelloWeb() {
    val state = rememberWebViewState("https://example.com")
    WebView(state = state, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize()) {
        // Optional Compose overlay on top of the native surface
    }
}
```

The trailing `content` lambda draws Compose UI over the embedded engine — the same role as the content slot of [`NativeView`](/docs/native-content/native-views).

## Supported targets

| Target  | Engine |
| ------- | ------- |
| Android | `android.webkit.WebView` |
| iOS     | WKWebView |
| WasmJs  | IFrame |
| JVM desktop | Platform engine through `NativeView` |

Desktop requires a Nucleus window (`nucleusApplication` and `DecoratedWindow`). Windows also needs the [WebView2 Runtime](https://developer.microsoft.com/microsoft-edge/webview2/) (or Edge). Native libraries ship inside the artifact under `nucleus/native/…`.

## What the library covers

- Content loading: URL (with headers), inline HTML, and HTML from app resources.
- Navigation: back, forward, reload, stop, with `canGoBack` / `canGoForward` as Compose state.
- Observable state: `isLoading`, `loadingState`, `lastLoadedUrl`, `pageTitle`, and per-request errors.
- A unified cookie manager across platforms.
- `evaluateJavaScript` and a callback-based JS ↔ Kotlin bridge (`window.kmpJsBridge`).
- A `RequestInterceptor` for navigator-initiated main-frame navigations.

## Limitations

- `RequestInterceptor` does not intercept sub-resources (images, XHR, scripts).
- **Desktop** needs a Nucleus window. The library does not embed a browser in a Compose Desktop `Window`.
- **WasmJs**: history back/forward is unavailable in the iframe; CORS must allow embedding; JavaScript runs only on the same origin; cookies apply only when the iframe destination matches the parent origin.

## What's next

- [Getting started](/docs/webview/getting-started) — load URLs and HTML, navigate, evaluate JS, intercept requests.
- [API reference](/docs/webview/api-reference) — every public type, its parameters, and defaults.
- [PDF reader](/docs/pdf) — another Nucleus component shipped from its own repository.
- [Native views](/docs/native-content/native-views) — the desktop embedding primitive used under the hood.

---

# Getting started

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/webview/getting-started

Load URLs and HTML, navigate the history stack, evaluate JavaScript, and intercept requests from Compose.

In this tutorial, you'll open a URL in a multiplatform WebView, react to loading state, navigate the history stack, evaluate JavaScript, and intercept navigations. Every snippet drops into a Compose Multiplatform `commonMain` source set.

## Before you start

Add the dependency described in the [WebView overview](/docs/webview):

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
commonMain.dependencies {
    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:composewebview:<version>")
}
```

On **desktop**, open the window with `nucleusApplication` and `DecoratedWindow`. The WebView embeds through [`NativeView`](/docs/native-content/native-views) and needs a Nucleus window: it does not run in a Compose Desktop `Window`.

## Load a URL

Hoist a `WebViewState` with `rememberWebViewState` and place `WebView` in the layout:

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxSize
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import dev.nucleusframework.webview.web.WebView
import dev.nucleusframework.webview.web.rememberWebViewState

@Composable
fun Browser(url: String) {
    val state = rememberWebViewState(url) {
        customUserAgentString = "MyApp/1.0"
    }
    WebView(state = state, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize())
}
```

The trailing lambda on `rememberWebViewState` is a `WebSettings` receiver — set user agent, zoom, JavaScript, and platform-specific options there.

## Load HTML

For inline HTML, use `rememberWebViewStateWithHTMLData`. For a file packaged with the app, use `rememberWebViewStateWithHTMLFile`:

```kotlin
val htmlState = rememberWebViewStateWithHTMLData(
    data = """
        <html><body><h1>Hello</h1></body></html>
    """.trimIndent(),
    baseUrl = null,
)

val fileState = rememberWebViewStateWithHTMLFile(
    fileName = "index.html",
    readType = WebViewFileReadType.ASSET_RESOURCES,
)
```

`WebViewFileReadType.ASSET_RESOURCES` reads platform asset roots; `COMPOSE_RESOURCE_FILES` reads Compose Multiplatform resources.

## React to loading state

`WebViewState` exposes snapshot state you can read in any composable — `isLoading`, `loadingState`, `lastLoadedUrl`, `pageTitle`, and `errorsForCurrentRequest`:

```kotlin
Box(Modifier.fillMaxSize()) {
    WebView(state = state, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize())
    if (state.isLoading) {
        LinearProgressIndicator(
            progress = {
                (state.loadingState as? LoadingState.Loading)?.progress ?: 0f
            },
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().align(Alignment.TopCenter),
        )
    }
    state.pageTitle?.let { title ->
        Text(title, Modifier.align(Alignment.BottomCenter))
    }
}
```

`LoadingState` is a sealed class: `Initializing`, `Loading(progress)`, or `Finished`.

## Navigate with a navigator

Hoist a `WebViewNavigator` when you need toolbar actions or programmatic loads:

```kotlin
val state = rememberWebViewState("https://example.com")
val navigator = rememberWebViewNavigator()

Column(Modifier.fillMaxSize()) {
    Row {
        IconButton(
            onClick = { navigator.navigateBack() },
            enabled = navigator.canGoBack,
        ) { Icon(Icons.Default.ArrowBack, contentDescription = "Back") }
        IconButton(
            onClick = { navigator.navigateForward() },
            enabled = navigator.canGoForward,
        ) { Icon(Icons.Default.ArrowForward, contentDescription = "Forward") }
        IconButton(onClick = { navigator.reload() }) {
            Icon(Icons.Default.Refresh, contentDescription = "Reload")
        }
        IconButton(onClick = {
            navigator.loadUrl("https://kotlinlang.org")
        }) { Text("Kotlin") }
    }
    WebView(state = state, navigator = navigator, modifier = Modifier.weight(1f))
}
```

Navigator commands include `loadUrl`, `loadHtml`, `loadHtmlFile`, `evaluateJavaScript`, `navigateBack`, `navigateForward`, `reload`, and `stopLoading`.

## Evaluate JavaScript

```kotlin
navigator.evaluateJavaScript("document.title") { title ->
    println("Page title: $title")
}
```

## Bridge JavaScript to Kotlin

Pass a `WebViewJsBridge` to `WebView`. Handlers register under a method name; the page calls `window.kmpJsBridge.callNative(...)` after load:

```kotlin
val navigator = rememberWebViewNavigator()
val bridge = rememberWebViewJsBridge(navigator)

LaunchedEffect(bridge) {
    bridge.register(object : IJsMessageHandler {
        override fun methodName() = "echo"
        override fun handle(
            message: JsMessage,
            navigator: WebViewNavigator?,
            callback: (String) -> Unit,
        ) {
            callback(message.params)
        }
    })
}

WebView(
    state = state,
    navigator = navigator,
    webViewJsBridge = bridge,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize(),
)
```

From the page:

```js
window.kmpJsBridge.callNative("echo", JSON.stringify({ hello: "world" }), function (result) {
  console.log(result);
});
```

## Intercept navigations

Attach a `RequestInterceptor` when creating the navigator. It runs only for **navigator-initiated** main-frame loads — not for sub-resources:

```kotlin
val navigator = rememberWebViewNavigator(
    requestInterceptor = object : RequestInterceptor {
        override fun onInterceptUrlRequest(
            request: WebRequest,
            navigator: WebViewNavigator,
        ): WebRequestInterceptResult {
            if (request.url.contains("blocked.example")) {
                return WebRequestInterceptResult.Reject
            }
            return WebRequestInterceptResult.Allow
        }
    },
)
```

Return `Allow`, `Reject`, or `Modify(request)` to rewrite the URL or headers.

## Manage cookies

```kotlin
scope.launch {
    state.cookieManager.setCookie(
        url = "https://example.com",
        cookie = Cookie(name = "session", value = "abc", domain = "example.com"),
    )
    val cookies = state.cookieManager.getCookies("https://example.com")
    state.cookieManager.removeCookies("https://example.com")
    state.cookieManager.removeAllCookies()
}
```

## Desktop notes

- Linux needs WebKit2GTK available on the system (`libwebkit2gtk`).
- Windows needs the WebView2 Runtime or a recent Edge install.
- macOS uses the system WKWebView; no extra runtime package is required.
- Open the host window with `DecoratedWindow`. See [Windows](/docs/windows).

The repository's e2e hosts (`e2e-desktop`, `e2e-android`, `e2e-wasmJs`, `iosApp`) run the same visual suite against a real WebView on each platform. Use them as a complete reference for wiring.

- [WebView overview](/docs/webview) — supported targets and platform engines.
- [Native views](/docs/native-content/native-views) — how desktop embeds the native surface.

# API reference

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/webview/api-reference

WebView, WebViewState, WebViewNavigator, settings, cookies, JS bridge, and request interception.

The public API lives under `dev.nucleusframework.webview`. Platform packages re-export the same types from `commonMain`.

## WebView

The multiplatform composable. Draws the native engine and an optional Compose overlay.

```kotlin
@Composable
fun WebView(
    state: WebViewState,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    navigator: WebViewNavigator = rememberWebViewNavigator(),
    webViewJsBridge: WebViewJsBridge? = null,
    onCreated: (NativeWebView) -> Unit = {},
    onDispose: (NativeWebView) -> Unit = {},
    content: @Composable () -> Unit = {},
)
```

- `content` is Compose UI drawn **over** the native surface (`NativeView` content slot on desktop; a layered sibling elsewhere).
- `onCreated` / `onDispose` receive the platform `NativeWebView` handle when the engine is attached or released.

## WebViewState

State holder for one embedded engine. Create it with the `rememberWebViewState*` helpers.

```kotlin
@Stable
class WebViewState(webContent: WebContent) {
    var lastLoadedUrl: String?           // last committed URL
    var content: WebContent              // drives loads when reassigned
    var loadingState: LoadingState       // Initializing | Loading | Finished
    val isLoading: Boolean               // true until Finished
    var pageTitle: String?
    val errorsForCurrentRequest: SnapshotStateList<WebViewError>
    val webSettings: WebSettings
    val cookieManager: CookieManager
    var webView: IWebView?               // set after the platform view attaches
}
```

```kotlin
@Composable
fun rememberWebViewState(
    url: String,
    additionalHttpHeaders: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
    extraSettings: WebSettings.() -> Unit = {},
): WebViewState

@Composable
fun rememberWebViewStateWithHTMLData(
    data: String,
    baseUrl: String? = null,
    encoding: String = "utf-8",
    mimeType: String? = null,
    historyUrl: String? = null,
): WebViewState

@Composable
fun rememberWebViewStateWithHTMLFile(
    fileName: String,
    readType: WebViewFileReadType,
): WebViewState
```

## WebContent

```kotlin
sealed class WebContent {
    data class Url(
        val url: String,
        val additionalHttpHeaders: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
    ) : WebContent()

    data class Data(
        val data: String,
        val baseUrl: String? = null,
        val encoding: String = "utf-8",
        val mimeType: String? = null,
        val historyUrl: String? = null,
    ) : WebContent()

    data class File(
        val fileName: String,
        val readType: WebViewFileReadType,
    ) : WebContent()

    data object NavigatorOnly : WebContent()
}

enum class WebViewFileReadType {
    ASSET_RESOURCES,
    COMPOSE_RESOURCE_FILES,
}
```

## LoadingState and WebViewError

```kotlin
sealed class LoadingState {
    data object Initializing : LoadingState()
    data class Loading(val progress: Float) : LoadingState()
    data object Finished : LoadingState()
}

@Immutable
data class WebViewError(
    val code: Int,
    val description: String,
    val isFromMainFrame: Boolean,
)
```

## WebViewNavigator

Programmatic navigation and script evaluation. Hoist with `rememberWebViewNavigator`.

```kotlin
@Stable
class WebViewNavigator(
    val coroutineScope: CoroutineScope,
    val requestInterceptor: RequestInterceptor? = null,
) {
    var canGoBack: Boolean
    var canGoForward: Boolean

    fun loadUrl(url: String, additionalHttpHeaders: Map<String, String> = emptyMap())
    fun loadHtml(
        html: String,
        baseUrl: String? = null,
        mimeType: String? = null,
        encoding: String? = "utf-8",
        historyUrl: String? = null,
    )
    fun loadHtmlFile(
        fileName: String,
        readType: WebViewFileReadType = WebViewFileReadType.ASSET_RESOURCES,
    )
    fun evaluateJavaScript(script: String, callback: ((String) -> Unit)? = null)
    fun navigateBack()
    fun navigateForward()
    fun reload()
    fun stopLoading()
}

@Composable
fun rememberWebViewNavigator(
    coroutineScope: CoroutineScope = rememberCoroutineScope(),
    requestInterceptor: RequestInterceptor? = null,
): WebViewNavigator
```

Bare HTTP(S) host URLs without a path gain a trailing slash before load (browser-style normalization).

## WebSettings

```kotlin
@Stable
class WebSettings {
    var isJavaScriptEnabled: Boolean          // default true
    var customUserAgentString: String?
    var zoomLevel: Double                     // default 1.0
    var supportZoom: Boolean                  // default true
    var allowFileAccessFromFileURLs: Boolean  // default false
    var allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs: Boolean // default false
    var logSeverity: KLogSeverity             // default None
    var backgroundColor: Color                // default Transparent

    val androidWebSettings: PlatformWebSettings.AndroidWebSettings
    val desktopWebSettings: PlatformWebSettings.DesktopWebSettings
    val iOSWebSettings: PlatformWebSettings.IOSWebSettings
    val wasmJSWebSettings: PlatformWebSettings.WasmJSWebSettings
}
```

Each platform applies the subset it supports. Use the nested `*WebSettings` objects for engine-specific knobs.

## Cookies

```kotlin
interface CookieManager {
    suspend fun setCookie(url: String, cookie: Cookie)
    suspend fun getCookies(url: String): List<Cookie>
    suspend fun removeAllCookies()
    suspend fun removeCookies(url: String)
}

data class Cookie(
    val name: String,
    val value: String,
    val domain: String? = null,
    val path: String? = null,
    val expiresDate: Long? = null,
    val isSessionOnly: Boolean = false,
    val sameSite: Cookie.HTTPCookieSameSitePolicy? = null,
    val isSecure: Boolean? = null,
    val isHttpOnly: Boolean? = null,
    val maxAge: Long? = null,
)
```

Access the manager through `state.cookieManager`.

## Request interception

```kotlin
interface RequestInterceptor {
    fun onInterceptUrlRequest(
        request: WebRequest,
        navigator: WebViewNavigator,
    ): WebRequestInterceptResult
}

data class WebRequest(
    val url: String,
    val headers: MutableMap<String, String> = mutableMapOf(),
    val isForMainFrame: Boolean = false,
    val isRedirect: Boolean = false,
    val method: String = "GET",
)

sealed interface WebRequestInterceptResult {
    data object Allow : WebRequestInterceptResult
    data object Reject : WebRequestInterceptResult
    class Modify(val request: WebRequest) : WebRequestInterceptResult
}
```

Interception applies to navigator-driven main-frame navigations only.

## JS bridge

```kotlin
@Immutable
open class WebViewJsBridge(
    val navigator: WebViewNavigator? = null,
    val jsBridgeName: String = "kmpJsBridge",
) {
    fun register(handler: IJsMessageHandler)
    fun unregister(handler: IJsMessageHandler)
    fun clear()
}

interface IJsMessageHandler {
    fun methodName(): String
    fun handle(
        message: JsMessage,
        navigator: WebViewNavigator?,
        callback: (String) -> Unit,
    )
}

@Composable
fun rememberWebViewJsBridge(navigator: WebViewNavigator? = null): WebViewJsBridge
```

After each finished load (or URL change), the library injects `window.<jsBridgeName>` with `callNative(methodName, params, callback)`. Register handlers before or after attach; clear happens when `WebView` leaves composition.

# OS integration

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os

Kotlin modules for native desktop features on macOS, Windows, and Linux, such as notifications, the system tray, global hotkeys, media controls, dark mode, and accent color.

The OS integration modules give you native desktop features from Kotlin: notifications, the
system tray, global hotkeys, media controls, dark mode, accent color, and more. Each feature ships
as its own Gradle artifact, so you add only the modules you use.

## Coverage

| Feature | Module | macOS | Windows | Linux |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cross-platform notifications | `notification-common` | yes | yes | yes |
| Native notifications | `notification-macos`, `notification-windows`, `notification-linux` | yes | yes | yes |
| System tray | `composenativetray` | yes | yes | yes |
| Tray popup apps | `composenativetray-app` | yes | yes | yes |
| Global hotkeys | `global-hotkey` | yes | yes | yes |
| Media controls | `media-control` | yes | yes | yes |
| Dark mode | `darkmode-detector` | yes | yes | yes |
| Accent color and high contrast | `system-color` | yes | yes | yes |
| Hardware and OS info | `system-info` | yes | yes | yes |
| macOS menu bar | `menu-macos` | yes | no | no |
| Spell check | `spellcheck` | yes | yes | yes |
| SF Symbols names | `sf-symbols` | yes | no | no |
| FreeDesktop icon names | `freedesktop-icons` | no | no | yes |

Modules use the group `dev.nucleusframework` and the artifact name `nucleus.<module-name>`. The
two tray modules drop the `nucleus.` prefix: `composenativetray` holds the icon and menu,
`composenativetray-app` holds `TrayApp`.

`nucleus-application` already includes `darkmode-detector` and `spellcheck`. For notifications,
start with `notification-common`; add a platform module when you need a feature it leaves out,
such as Windows toast progress bars, macOS scheduled delivery, or Linux urgency hints.

## Callback threads

`notification-common`, `notification-linux`, `notification-windows`, `media-control`, and
`menu-macos` call your code on the UI thread. `global-hotkey` listeners and the
`notification-macos` delegate run on native threads: move the work to `Dispatchers.Main` before
you touch UI state.

In 2.x, `notification-linux`, `notification-windows`, and `media-control` called back on the AWT
event dispatch thread. See [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

## What's next

- [Cross-platform notifications](/docs/os/notifications): send a notification with one API on all three systems.
- [System tray](/docs/os/tray): draw a tray icon and its menu from Compose.
- [Dark mode](/docs/os/theme/dark-mode): read the system theme and follow its changes.
- [Threading](/docs/concepts/threading): the threads Nucleus runs your code on.

# Cross-platform notifications

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/notifications

Send desktop notifications on macOS, Windows, and Linux from a single Kotlin API.

`notification-common` sends a desktop notification with one API on macOS, Windows, and Linux:
title, body, images, up to five buttons, and lifecycle callbacks. Add
`dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.notification-common`; it pulls in the three platform modules.

## Send a notification

```kotlin
NotificationManager.initialize() // optional: otherwise setup runs on the first send()

val n = notification(
    title = "Download complete",
    message = "report.pdf has been saved",
    onActivated = { openFile() },
    onDismissed = { reason -> log.info("dismissed: $reason") },
) {
    button("Open") { openFile() }
    button("Show in folder") { showInFolder() }
}

when (val result = n.send()) {
    is NotificationResult.Success -> saveHandle(result.handle) // handle.dismiss() closes it
    is NotificationResult.Failure -> log.warn(result.reason)
}
```

Each `send()` shows a new notification, so you can send the same instance twice. Callbacks run on
the UI thread. `onFailed` can run on the calling thread, because a send can fail before it
reaches the OS.

In 2.x, callbacks on Linux and Windows ran on the AWT event dispatch thread. See
[Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

## Platform-specific options

The `linux { }`, `macos { }`, and `windows { }` blocks apply only on that OS, so you can keep them
in shared code.

```kotlin
notification(title = "Build failed", message = "See the logs") {
    linux { urgency = Urgency.CRITICAL; transient = true; category = "device.error" }
    macos { interruptionLevel = InterruptionLevel.TIME_SENSITIVE; subtitle = "CI" }
    windows { scenario = ToastScenario.URGENT; duration = ToastDuration.LONG }
}
```

| Block | Properties |
| --- | --- |
| `linux { }` | `urgency`, `category`, `transient`, `resident`, `expireTimeout` (ms; `0` never expires, unset or `-1` uses the server default) |
| `macos { }` | `interruptionLevel`, `relevanceScore` (`0.0..1.0`), `subtitle` |
| `windows { }` | `scenario` (`ToastScenario`), `duration` (`ToastDuration`) |

- macOS needs the matching Apple entitlement for `TIME_SENSITIVE` and `CRITICAL`, or falls back
  to `ACTIVE`.
- `ToastScenario.URGENT` breaks through Focus Assist on Windows 11 and later.

## macOS setup

macOS delivers notifications only to a bundled app the user has authorized. Request authorization
with `NotificationCenter.requestAuthorization` and test with `./gradlew runDistributable`. Do not
call `NotificationCenter.setDelegate`: the common layer installs its own delegate.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- `NotificationManager` picks the platform module for the host OS on first use. Only that module
  loads.
- On Windows, `initialize()` calls `WindowsNotificationCenter.initialize()`.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `String` | Required title. |
| `message` | `String` | Body text. Defaults to `""`. |
| `largeImage` | `String?` | Image URI: hero image on Windows, image hint on Linux, attachment on macOS. |
| `smallIcon` | `String?` | Icon URI: app logo on Windows, app icon on Linux, ignored on macOS. |
| `onActivated` | `(() -> Unit)?` | The user clicked the body. |
| `onDismissed` | `((DismissReason) -> Unit)?` | `USER_DISMISSED`, `TIMED_OUT`, `APPLICATION`, or `UNKNOWN`. |
| `onFailed` | `(() -> Unit)?` | The notification could not be shown. |

A sixth `button(...)` throws. `NotificationManager.isAvailable()` returns `false` when the OS has
no notification backend or the native library did not load.

## What's next

- [Notifications on macOS](/docs/os/notifications/macos): authorization, scheduling, categories, and attachments.
- [Notifications on Windows](/docs/os/notifications/windows): toast layouts, progress bars, and history.
- [Notifications on Linux](/docs/os/notifications/linux): urgency, actions, and server capabilities.

# Notifications on macOS

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/notifications/macos

Kotlin bindings for Apple's UserNotifications framework, with authorization, categories, attachments, text input, triggers, and interruption levels.

`notification-macos` gives you Apple's UserNotifications framework from Kotlin: authorization,
scheduled requests, action categories with text input, attachments, and the Dock badge. Add
`dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.notification-macos`.

## Send a notification

```kotlin
NotificationCenter.requestAuthorization(
    setOf(AuthorizationOption.ALERT, AuthorizationOption.SOUND, AuthorizationOption.BADGE),
) { granted, error ->
    if (!granted) return@requestAuthorization
    NotificationCenter.add(
        NotificationRequest(
            identifier = "greeting",
            content = NotificationContent(
                title = "Hello",
                body = "Welcome to Nucleus",
                sound = NotificationSound.Default,
                interruptionLevel = InterruptionLevel.TIME_SENSITIVE,
                attachments = listOf(
                    NotificationAttachment(identifier = "img", url = imageFile.absolutePath),
                ),
            ),
            trigger = NotificationTrigger.TimeInterval(interval = 5.0), // null delivers now
        ),
    )
}
```

macOS delivers notifications only to a bundled app. Run `./gradlew runDistributable` or
`./gradlew runGraalvmNative` during development: a plain `./gradlew run` has no bundle, and the
system drops its notifications without an error.

Delegate methods and result callbacks run on a worker thread. Switch to `Dispatchers.Main` before
you touch Compose state.

## Add actions and text input

Register categories once, then reference one from `NotificationContent.categoryIdentifier`:

```kotlin
NotificationCenter.setNotificationCategories(setOf(
    NotificationCategory(
        identifier = "MESSAGE",
        actions = listOf(
            TextInputNotificationAction(
                identifier = "REPLY",
                title = "Reply",
                textInputButtonTitle = "Send",
                textInputPlaceholder = "Type a reply…",
            ),
        ),
        options = setOf(CategoryOption.CUSTOM_DISMISS_ACTION),
    ),
))

NotificationCenter.setDelegate(object : NotificationCenterDelegate {
    override fun willPresent(notification: DeliveredNotification) =
        setOf(PresentationOption.BANNER, PresentationOption.SOUND)

    override fun didReceive(response: NotificationResponse) {
        handle(response.actionIdentifier, response.userText)
    }
})
```

`willPresent` decides how a notification shows while your app is in front. It runs synchronously,
so return fast; an empty set hides the notification. Override `openSettings` to react to the
notification settings button. If you also use `notification-common`, skip `setDelegate`: it
installs its own.

## Notes

- Sandboxed apps need the notifications entitlement: point `macOS { entitlementsFile }` at an
  `.entitlements` file that declares it.
- To bypass Focus modes, set `InterruptionLevel.CRITICAL` and request
  `AuthorizationOption.CRITICAL_ALERT`. Critical sounds need the same entitlement.
- A bundle identifier mismatch causes most silent failures. Check that `NucleusApp.appId`
  matches the bundle id of the packaged `.app`.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Each call wraps the matching `UNUserNotificationCenter` method through a JNI bridge.
- Callbacks run on a Nucleus thread named `NucleusNotificationCallback-N`.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Symbol | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `NotificationCenter.isAvailable` | `false` off macOS, without the native library, or without an app bundle. Calls then do nothing; error callbacks receive the reason. |
| `AuthorizationOption` | `BADGE`, `SOUND`, `ALERT`, `CRITICAL_ALERT`, `PROVIDES_APP_NOTIFICATION_SETTINGS`, `PROVISIONAL`, `TIME_SENSITIVE` |
| `getNotificationSettings { }` | Current `authorizationStatus` and per-feature settings |
| `NotificationTrigger.TimeInterval(interval, repeats)` | Seconds. Repeating needs `interval >= 60`. |
| `NotificationTrigger.Calendar(dateComponents, repeats)` | A date from `DateComponents`, such as every Monday at 9:00 |
| `NotificationSound` | `Default`, `Named(name)`, `DefaultCritical`, `CriticalNamed(name, volume)`, `DefaultCriticalWithVolume(volume)` |
| `ActionOption` | `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`, `DESTRUCTIVE`, `FOREGROUND` |
| `setBadgeCount(n)` / `getBadgeCount { }` | Dock badge |
| `getPendingNotifications { }` / `getDeliveredNotifications { }` | Queued or on-screen requests |
| `removePendingNotifications(ids)` / `removeDeliveredNotifications(ids)` | Remove entries; `removeAll…()` variants clear everything |

## What's next

- [Cross-platform notifications](/docs/os/notifications): the shared `NotificationManager` API.
- [Notifications on Windows](/docs/os/notifications/windows): toasts through `WindowsNotificationCenter`.
- [Notifications on Linux](/docs/os/notifications/linux): freedesktop notifications through `LinuxNotificationCenter`.
- [Code signing](/docs/packaging/code-signing): sign and bundle the app so macOS delivers its notifications.

# Notifications on Windows

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/notifications/windows

Send Windows toast notifications from Kotlin with adaptive text, images, buttons, inputs, headers, and progress bars.

`notification-windows` sends Windows 10 and 11 toasts from Kotlin, with adaptive text, images,
progress bars, inputs, and headers. It works for MSIX apps and for unpackaged EXE and MSI
installs. Add `dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.notification-windows`.

## Send a toast

```kotlin
WindowsNotificationCenter.initialize()

WindowsNotificationCenter.show(
    toast {
        visual {
            text("Build finished")
            text("artifact.zip uploaded")
            heroImage("file:///C:/Users/me/hero.png")
        }
        actions {
            button("Open", arguments = "open")
            button("Cancel", arguments = "cancel", activationType = ActivationType.BACKGROUND)
        }
        scenario = ToastScenario.REMINDER
    },
)

WindowsNotificationCenter.addListener(object : ToastNotificationListener {
    override fun onActivated(
        tag: String, group: String, arguments: String, userInputs: Map<String, String>,
    ) { handle(arguments, userInputs) }
    override fun onDismissed(tag: String, group: String, reason: DismissalReason) {}
    override fun onFailed(tag: String, group: String, errorCode: Int) {}
})
```

Every method does nothing off Windows. `arguments` carries the `launch` string or the clicked
button's `arguments`; `userInputs` maps each input id to its value. Listener callbacks run on the
UI thread.

`ToastNotificationListener` callbacks ran on the AWT event dispatch thread in 2.x. See
[Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

## Set the app identity

Windows identifies the sender by its AUMID. MSIX apps use the package identity; unpackaged apps
use `NucleusApp.aumid`, which the Gradle plugin sets. Pass `initialize(aumid = "Vendor.App")` to
override it.

An unpackaged app also needs a Start Menu shortcut with the same AUMID, or toasts can fail to show
or vanish from Action Center. The Windows installers create it, so install the app once to see
toasts from a dev run. `shortcutPolicy` sets what `initialize` does with it:

| `ShortcutPolicy` | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `REQUIRE_CREATE` | Create or update the shortcut. Default for installed apps. |
| `REQUIRE_NO_CREATE` | Require an existing shortcut and never touch it. Default in dev runs, with a logged warning. |
| `IGNORE` | Skip shortcut handling. |

## Update a toast in place

Show the toast with a `tag`, a `group`, `{key}` placeholders, and `initialData`, then push new
values:

```kotlin
WindowsNotificationCenter.show(
    toast { visual { progressBar(status = "{status}", value = 0.0) } },
    tag = "upload",
    group = "transfers",
    initialData = ToastNotificationData(sequenceNumber = 1, values = mapOf("status" to "Starting")),
)

WindowsNotificationCenter.update(
    tag = "upload",
    group = "transfers",
    data = ToastNotificationData(sequenceNumber = 2, values = mapOf("status" to "Almost done")),
)
```

Increase `sequenceNumber` with each update so Windows drops stale ones. To bind the bar's value,
build an `AdaptiveProgressBar(valueBind = "progressValue", status = …)` and send
`"progressValue"` in `values`.

## Notes

- Keep one AUMID across the shortcut, your Gradle configuration, and run time. A mismatch
  produces a toast that shows once and never again.
- `tag` and `group` hold 16 characters at most.
- Unpackaged apps can load `http(s)://` images when the server answers fast. For offline use,
  ship a local file and use `file:///` (unpackaged) or `ms-appx:///` (MSIX).

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- The module wraps the WinRT `ToastNotificationManager` API.
- For unpackaged apps, `initialize` registers the AUMID on the process.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Symbol | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `toast { visual { } }` | `text`, `image`, `appLogo`, `heroImage`, `attribution`, `progressBar`, `group` (columns) |
| `toast { actions { } }` | `textBox`, `selectionBox`, `button`, `contextMenuItem` |
| `audio(source, customSource, loop, silent)` / `silentAudio()` | Sound |
| `header(id, title, arguments)` | Group toasts in Action Center |
| `launch`, `activationType`, `scenario`, `duration`, `displayTimestamp` | Toast properties |
| `ToastScenario` | `DEFAULT`, `REMINDER`, `ALARM`, `INCOMING_CALL`, `URGENT` |
| `ToastDuration` | `DEFAULT`, `SHORT`, `LONG` |
| `DismissalReason` | `USER_CANCELED`, `APPLICATION_HIDDEN`, `TIMED_OUT` |
| `showSimple(title, body, body2)` / `showFromXml` | Text-only toast / raw toast XML |
| `getHistory { entries, error -> }` | Action Center entries |
| `remove(tag, group)` / `removeGroup(group)` / `clearAll()` | Remove toasts |
| `removeListener(listener)` / `uninitialize()` | Remove a listener / release native resources at shutdown |

## What's next

- [Cross-platform notifications](/docs/os/notifications): the shared notification DSL.
- [Notifications on macOS](/docs/os/notifications/macos): `UNUserNotificationCenter` from Kotlin.
- [Notifications on Linux](/docs/os/notifications/linux): freedesktop notifications over D-Bus.
- [Windows packaging](/docs/packaging/windows): the installers that create the Start Menu shortcut.

# Notifications on Linux

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/notifications/linux

Send freedesktop desktop notifications over D-Bus from Kotlin, with urgency, hints, sounds, images, and action callbacks.

`notification-linux` sends freedesktop desktop notifications on GNOME, KDE, Cinnamon, Xfce, and
other desktops. Add `dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.notification-linux`; it brings the typed icon
names of [`freedesktop-icons`](/docs/os/icons/freedesktop).

## Send a notification

```kotlin
val id: Int = LinuxNotificationCenter.notify(
    Notification(
        appName = "MyApp",
        summary = "Build finished",
        body = "myapp.zip is ready",
        appIcon = FreedesktopIcon.Status.DIALOG_INFORMATION,
        hints = NotificationHints(
            urgency = Urgency.NORMAL,
            soundName = NotificationSound.Notification.DIALOG_INFORMATION,
        ),
        actions = listOf(
            NotificationAction(NotificationAction.DEFAULT_KEY, "Open"), // body click
            NotificationAction("archive", "Archive"),
        ),
    ),
)
```

`notify` returns the server-assigned ID, or `0` on failure. Pass it as `replacesId` to replace a
notification in place, or to `closeNotification(id)`. `expireTimeout` is in milliseconds: `-1`
(the default) lets the server decide, `0` keeps the notification until the user closes it.

## Receive callbacks

```kotlin
LinuxNotificationCenter.addListener(object : LinuxNotificationListener {
    override fun onActionInvoked(notificationId: Int, actionKey: String) { /* … */ }
    override fun onClosed(notificationId: Int, reason: CloseReason) { /* … */ }
    override fun onActivationToken(notificationId: Int, token: String) { /* … */ }
})
```

All three methods have empty defaults. `onActivationToken` delivers the X11 or Wayland token you
use to request window focus. Callbacks run on the UI thread.

Listener callbacks ran on the AWT event dispatch thread in 2.x. See
[Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

## Notes

- Servers render the specification differently. GNOME Shell often ignores `appIcon`; set
  `hints.imagePath` for a consistent icon. `getServerInformation()` and `getCapabilities()`
  tell you which server runs and what it supports.
- Most servers show `Urgency.CRITICAL` notifications through Do Not Disturb and never expire them.
- Under Xvfb or on a headless CI runner, `notify` returns without error but nothing shows.
- In a Flatpak build, the manifest must grant access to `org.freedesktop.Notifications`.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Each `notify` call invokes the `Notify` method of the `org.freedesktop.Notifications` D-Bus
  service through a GDBus bridge, with no JNA or Java D-Bus library.
- Actions and close events arrive as D-Bus signals. Monitoring starts with the first listener and
  stops when you remove the last one.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Symbol | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `LinuxNotificationCenter.isAvailable` | `false` off Linux or when the native library did not load |
| `Urgency` | `LOW`, `NORMAL`, `CRITICAL` |
| `NotificationHints` | All optional: `urgency`, `category`, `desktopEntry`, `imageData`, `imagePath`, `actionIcons`, `soundFile`, `soundName`, `suppressSound`, `resident`, `transient`, `x`, `y` |
| `ImageData(width, height, rowstride, hasAlpha, data)` | Raw RGB or RGBA pixels. `channels` defaults to `4` with alpha, `3` without; `bitsPerSample` to `8`. |
| `NotificationSound` | Theme names in `Alert`, `Notification`, `Action`, `InputFeedback`, `Game`; `Custom("x-myapp-…")` for others |
| `CloseReason` | `EXPIRED`, `DISMISSED`, `CLOSED`, `UNDEFINED` |
| `closeNotification(id)` / `removeListener(listener)` | Close a notification / remove a listener |

## What's next

- [FreeDesktop icon names](/docs/os/icons/freedesktop): typed names for `appIcon` and `imagePath`.
- [Cross-platform notifications](/docs/os/notifications): the shared notification API.
- [Linux launcher](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/linux): badges and quicklists on the Linux dock.

# System tray

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/tray

Draw a tray icon and its native menu from Compose on macOS, Windows, and Linux without AWT.

`Tray` draws a system tray icon and its native menu from Compose on macOS, Windows, and Linux.
The icon and the menu update when the state they read changes.

The tray ships from [`NucleusFramework/ComposeNativeTray`](https://github.com/NucleusFramework/ComposeNativeTray)
with its own version. Add `dev.nucleusframework:composenativetray` for `Tray` and the menu DSL,
and `dev.nucleusframework:composenativetray-app` for [tray apps](/docs/os/tray/tray-app).

## Add a tray icon

```kotlin
import dev.nucleusframework.composenativetray.tray.api.Tray

fun main() = nucleusApplication {
    Tray(
        icon = Icons.Default.Favorite,
        tooltip = "My App",
        primaryAction = { showWindow() },
        onMenuOpened = { refreshStatus() },
    ) {
        Item(label = "Show window") { showWindow() }
        Divider()
        Item(label = "Quit") { exitApplication() }
    }
}
```

The icon stays while `Tray` is in the composition, so wrap it in an `if` to hide it. Pass
`menuContent = null` for an icon without a menu.

Compose Desktop's `androidx.compose.ui.window.Tray` relies on AWT and does not work under
`nucleusApplication`. Use `dev.nucleusframework.composenativetray.tray.api.Tray`. See
[Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

## Handle clicks

`primaryAction` runs on a left click on macOS and Windows. On Linux, KDE fires it on a single
click and GNOME on a double click. Without `primaryAction`, a click opens the menu.
`onMenuOpened` runs each time the menu opens, so you can refresh data first.

## Set the icon

`icon` accepts an `ImageVector` (with an optional `tint`), a `Painter`, or a `DrawableResource`.
`iconContent` takes any composable, such as a badge:

```kotlin
Tray(
    iconContent = {
        Box(Modifier.size(24.dp).background(Color.Red, CircleShape)) {
            Text("3", color = Color.White, modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.Center))
        }
    },
    tooltip = "3 notifications",
) { /* … */ }
```

- Without `tint`, an `ImageVector` renders white on a dark tray and black on a light one.
- For a hand-drawn `.ico` on Windows, pass `windowsIcon` and `macLinuxIcon` instead of `icon`.
- `iconRenderProperties` sets the render sizes. The default targets 44 px on macOS, 32 px on
  Windows, and 24 px on Linux.
- Stock GNOME shows the icon only with the AppIndicator extension. KDE Plasma and Ubuntu show it
  by default.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Compose renders the icon offscreen when its state changes and hands the pixels to the native
  tray API. The library records the menu items during composition and rebuilds the native menu
  when they change. It does not use AWT.
- macOS uses an `NSStatusItem`, with light and dark variants of an untinted vector rendered ahead
  of time. Windows uses `Shell_NotifyIcon`. Linux uses a StatusNotifierItem with a DBusMenu menu.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's next

- [Tray menu DSL](/docs/os/tray/menu): items, checkable items, submenus, shortcuts, and reactive menus.
- [Tray apps](/docs/os/tray/tray-app): open a Compose popup from the tray icon.
- [Application entry point](/docs/lifecycle/application): `nucleusApplication` and `exitApplication`.

---

# Tray menu DSL

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/tray/menu

Build the tray context menu in Kotlin with items, checkable items, submenus, dividers, shortcut hints, and state-driven content.

The trailing lambda of `Tray` builds its native context menu. The lambda is `@Composable`: it
reads state, calls `painterResource`, and branches with `if`, and the native menu follows each
change.

## Build a menu

```kotlin
var connected by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
var advanced by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }

Tray(icon = Icons.Default.Wifi, tooltip = "Network") {
    Item(label = if (connected) "Disconnect" else "Connect") { connected = !connected }
    Item(label = "Export", icon = Icons.Default.Upload) { export() }
    Item(label = "Disabled", isEnabled = false)
    CheckableItem(
        label = "Advanced options",
        checked = advanced,
        onCheckedChange = { advanced = it },
    )
    if (advanced) {
        SubMenu(label = "Advanced", icon = Icons.Default.Build) {
            Item(label = "DNS settings") { openDns() }
            SubMenu(label = "More") { Item(label = "Proxy") { openProxy() } }
        }
    }
    Divider()
    Item(label = "Quit") { exitApplication() }
}
```

- `icon` accepts an `ImageVector` (with an optional `iconTint`), a `Painter`, or a
  `DrawableResource`. Menu icons render at 16 px.
- `SubMenu` nests to any depth.
- `TrayApp` takes its `menu` as a plain `TrayMenuBuilder` lambda. It offers the same functions,
  but they are not `@Composable`.

## Show shortcut hints

`shortcut` displays a key combination next to an item. It registers no hotkey; use
[global hotkeys](/docs/os/global-hotkey) for that.

```kotlin
import dev.nucleusframework.composenativetray.menu.api.Key
import dev.nucleusframework.composenativetray.menu.api.KeyShortcut

Item(label = "New note", shortcut = KeyShortcut(Key.N, meta = true)) { newNote() }
```

macOS draws the native glyphs (⌘N), Windows shows right-aligned text (`Win+N`), and the Linux
desktop renders its own.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- The DSL records each call into a flat list of menu operations. The library rebuilds the native
  menu only when a fingerprint of that list changes, so a recomposition that leaves the menu
  identical makes no native call.
- Linux sends shortcuts as the DBusMenu `shortcut` property.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's next

- [System tray](/docs/os/tray): icon sources, clicks, and platform behavior.
- [Tray apps](/docs/os/tray/tray-app): open a popup window from the icon.
- [macOS menu bar](/docs/os/menus/menu-bar): the application menu bar on macOS.

# Tray-anchored apps

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/tray/tray-app

TrayApp opens a Compose popup window next to a system tray icon, for menu bar and tray utilities written in Kotlin.

`TrayApp` anchors a Compose popup to a system tray icon. A left click on the icon opens the popup
next to it, a right click opens its menu, and a click elsewhere closes the popup. Add
`dev.nucleusframework:composenativetray-app`; it brings [`composenativetray`](/docs/os/tray).

`composenativetray-app` builds for Nucleus 2.x call `NucleusApplicationScope.backend`, which
Nucleus 3.0 removes. Use a release built against Nucleus 3.0. See
[Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

## Create a tray app

Call `TrayApp` inside `nucleusApplication { }`. Hold a `TrayAppState` to show, hide, or resize
the popup from code:

```kotlin
import dev.nucleusframework.composenativetray.trayapp.TrayApp
import dev.nucleusframework.composenativetray.trayapp.rememberTrayAppState

fun main() = nucleusApplication {
    val state = rememberTrayAppState(
        initialWindowSize = DpSize(300.dp, 400.dp),
        initialDismissMode = TrayWindowDismissMode.AUTO,
    )

    TrayApp(
        icon = Icons.Default.Dashboard,
        tooltip = "Quick dashboard",
        state = state,
        menu = {
            Item(label = "Settings") { openSettings() }
            Divider()
            Item(label = "Quit") { exitApplication() }
        },
    ) {
        Column(Modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(16.dp)) {
            Text("CPU: 42%")
            Button(onClick = { state.hide() }) { Text("Close") }
        }
    }
}
```

`menu` takes the functions of the [tray menu DSL](/docs/os/tray/menu), without
`@Composable`.

## Hide the Dock icon on macOS

Pass `dockIconFollowsWindows = true` to `nucleusApplication` instead of setting `LSUIElement` in
`Info.plist`:

```kotlin
fun main() = nucleusApplication(dockIconFollowsWindows = true) {
    TrayApp(icon = Icons.Default.Dashboard, tooltip = "Dashboard") { Text("Popup content") }
}
```

A Dock tile appears only while a `DecoratedWindow` with `hiddenFromDock = false` is visible.
`TrayApp` popups never count, so a tray-only app stays out of the Dock. Other systems ignore the
flag. See [Hide a window from the taskbar or Dock](/docs/windows#hide-a-window-from-the-taskbar-or-dock).

## Notes

- The popup has no title bar and does not appear in the taskbar, the Dock, or Alt+Tab.
- In `AUTO` dismiss mode, the popup hides when it loses focus. Clicks on the tray icon and its
  menu do not count as outside clicks. In `MANUAL`, only `hide()` or a click on the icon closes it.
- On macOS the popup joins every Space and stays when you click the wallpaper.
- The popup keeps its composition while hidden, so its state survives a hide and show.
- On Linux the popup needs X11 or XWayland. A Wayland session without XWayland gets an opaque
  undecorated window instead: the "fallback window only" parameters below apply to it.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- The popup is a transparent, non-activating native panel, not a `DecoratedWindow`.
- The library reads the tray icon's screen position and places the popup beside it, with an
  offset tuned for each OS and Linux desktop.
- About 1.5 s after the popup hides, the library requests a garbage collection to trim the heap.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

### TrayApp parameters

| Parameter | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` / `windowsIcon` + `macLinuxIcon` | required | `ImageVector`, `Painter`, or `DrawableResource`, as in `Tray`. |
| `tooltip` | required | Tray icon tooltip. |
| `state` | `null` | A `TrayAppState`; without it `TrayApp` keeps its own. |
| `windowSize` | `null` | Initial size; falls back to the state's size, `DpSize(300.dp, 200.dp)` by default. |
| `visibleOnStart` | `false` | Show the popup at launch. |
| `enterTransition` / `exitTransition` | fade | Popup animations. |
| `undecorated`, `resizable`, `windowsTitle`, `windowIcon` | `true`, `false`, `""`, `null` | Fallback window only. |
| `horizontalOffset` / `verticalOffset` | `0` / per OS | Nudge the popup away from the tray anchor, in pixels. |
| `onPreviewKeyEvent` / `onKeyEvent` | `{ false }` | Key handlers for the popup. |
| `menu` | `null` | Right-click menu. |

### TrayAppState

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `isVisible`, `windowSize`, `dismissMode` | `StateFlow`s of the current values. |
| `show()`, `hide()`, `toggle()` | Change visibility. |
| `setWindowSize(size)`, `setWindowSize(width, height)` | Resize the popup. |
| `setDismissMode(mode)` | `AUTO` or `MANUAL`. |
| `onVisibilityChanged(callback)` | Observe visibility changes. |

`getTrayPosition()` returns the `TrayPosition` (`TOP_LEFT`, `TOP_RIGHT`, `BOTTOM_LEFT`,
`BOTTOM_RIGHT`) of the screen corner that holds the tray.

## What's next

- [System tray](/docs/os/tray): the `Tray` API that `TrayApp` builds on.
- [Tray menu DSL](/docs/os/tray/menu): the right-click menu functions.
- [Single instance](/docs/lifecycle/single-instance): keep one running copy of a tray app.

# Dock and taskbar

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/dock-taskbar

Progress, badges and menus on the macOS Dock, the Windows taskbar and the Linux launcher.

Each OS gives your app an icon outside its windows: the Dock on macOS, the taskbar button on
Windows, the launcher entry on Linux. Nucleus lets you draw on it and add menus to it.

| You want to | macOS | Windows | Linux |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Show progress or request attention | [Progress](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/progress) | [Progress](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/progress) | [Progress](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/progress) |
| Add items to the icon's right-click menu | [Dock menu](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/macos) | [Jump list](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/windows#build-a-jump-list) | [Quicklist](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/linux#add-a-quicklist-menu) |
| Show a badge | [Dock badge](/docs/os/notifications/macos) | [Badge](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/windows#show-a-badge) | [Count badge](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/linux#set-badges-and-progress) |
| Add an overlay icon or toolbar buttons | none | [Overlay and buttons](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/windows) | none |

Start with [Progress and attention](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/progress): one API covers all three
systems. The per-OS pages add what only that system has.

## What's next

- [Progress and attention](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/progress): the cross-platform API.
- [System tray](/docs/os/tray): an icon in the menu bar or notification area instead.
- [Notifications](/docs/os/notifications): messages that reach the user outside the window.

# macOS Dock menu

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/dock-taskbar/macos

Populate the Dock right-click menu of a macOS app with items, submenus, and separators, and handle clicks from Kotlin.

`launcher-macos` fills the Dock right-click menu of a macOS app with items, submenus, separators,
and disabled entries, and calls you back on the UI thread when the user clicks one.

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.launcher-macos:<version>")
}
```

## Populate the Dock menu

Each item carries a numeric `id`, which the listener receives:

```kotlin
MacOsDockMenu.setDockMenu(listOf(
    DockMenuItem(id = 1, title = "New Window"),
    DockMenuItem.separator(id = 2),
    DockMenuItem(
        id = 3,
        title = "Recent",
        children = listOf(
            DockMenuItem(id = 31, title = "project.kt"),
            DockMenuItem(id = 32, title = "build.gradle.kts"),
        ),
    ),
))

MacOsDockMenu.listener = DockMenuListener { id ->
    when (id) {
        1 -> openNewWindow()
        in 30..39 -> openRecent(id)
    }
}
```

`clearDockMenu()` restores the default Dock menu. Every method does nothing off macOS or when
the native library fails to load; check `isAvailable` first. The Dock renders text only, so item
images are not supported.

The listener now runs on the host UI thread instead of the Swing EDT. Under
`nucleusApplication` that is the thread Compose uses, so you can write Compose state from it
directly. See [Threading](/docs/concepts/threading) and
[Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

Test from a packaged build or `runDistributable`. Under `./gradlew run`, the Dock tile belongs to
the `java` launcher, which has no bundle identifier.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- The first `setDockMenu(...)` call swizzles `applicationDockMenu:` on the running
  `NSApplicationDelegate`. AppKit then asks Nucleus for the menu on each right-click.
- In a plain Compose Desktop or Swing host, the listener runs on the AWT event dispatch thread.
- The module ships the ProGuard and GraalVM metadata that keeps
  `dev.nucleusframework.launcher.macos.NativeMacOsDockMenuBridge` reachable.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Symbol | Notes |
|---|---|
| `MacOsDockMenu.isAvailable` | `false` off macOS or when the native library failed to load. |
| `MacOsDockMenu.listener: DockMenuListener?` | One global listener. Dispatch on `id` inside it. |
| `MacOsDockMenu.setDockMenu(items)` | Replaces the menu. |
| `MacOsDockMenu.clearDockMenu()` | Removes the menu; the OS default returns. |
| `DockMenuItem(id, title = "", enabled = true, children = emptyList())` | `id` must be `> 0`. Non-empty `children` makes a submenu. |
| `DockMenuItem.separator(id)` | A separator. |
| `DockMenuListener.onItemClicked(itemId: Int)` | `fun interface`, called on the host UI thread. |

## What's next

- [Taskbar progress](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/progress): progress and attention requests on the Dock icon.
- [Deep links](/docs/lifecycle/deep-links): receive `myapp://` URLs through Apple Events.
- [Windows taskbar](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/windows): jump lists and thumbnail toolbars.

# Windows taskbar

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/dock-taskbar/windows

Drive the Windows taskbar from Kotlin with overlay icons, jump lists, thumbnail toolbar buttons, and badges.

`launcher-windows` drives four parts of the Windows taskbar: overlay icons, jump lists, thumbnail
toolbar buttons, and badges. Each part is a separate `object`.

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.launcher-windows:<version>")
}
```

## Get the window handle

Overlay icons and thumbnail buttons take the window's `HWND` as a `Long`. It is `0` until the
native window exists:

```kotlin
DecoratedWindow(onCloseRequest = ::exitApplication) {
    val hwnd = nucleusWindow.unsafe.taoWindow?.nativeHandle ?: 0L
}
```

2.x snippets passed an AWT `Window`. A `nucleusApplication` app has no AWT window: pass the
`HWND` above. AWT hosts can still use the `java.awt.Window` overloads or
`WindowsWindowHandle.of(window)`. See [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

## Set an overlay icon

A 16x16 status marker on the taskbar button. Works with every packaging type:

```kotlin
WindowsOverlayIcon.setIcon(hwnd, TaskbarIconSource.FromStock(StockIcon.WARNING), "1 unread message")
WindowsOverlayIcon.clearIcon(hwnd)
```

Each call returns `true` on success; `lastError` holds the last failure.

## Build a jump list

`setJumpList` replaces the whole right-click menu in one call:

```kotlin
WindowsJumpListManager.setJumpList(
    categories = listOf(
        JumpListCategory("Recent", items = listOf(
            JumpListItem("Project A", arguments = "myapp://open?project=a"),
        )),
    ),
    tasks = listOf(
        JumpListItem("New window", arguments = "myapp://new"),
        JumpListItem.SEPARATOR,
        JumpListItem("Settings", arguments = "myapp://settings"),
    ),
)
```

A click starts a new process with the entry's `arguments`. The
[single-instance](/docs/lifecycle/single-instance) lock forwards a deep link to the running app,
where [`onDeepLink`](/docs/lifecycle/deep-links) receives it.

- Unpackaged builds (NSIS, MSI, distributable) need a process AUMID before the first window.
  `nucleusApplication` sets it; otherwise call `WindowsJumpListManager.setProcessAppId()` at the
  start of `main`. APPX and MSIX use the package identity.
- Under `./gradlew run` the process is `java.exe`, so test from `runDistributable` or a packaged
  build.

## Add thumbnail toolbar buttons

Up to seven buttons in the window's taskbar preview, registered once per window:

```kotlin
WindowsThumbnailToolbar.setButtons(
    hwnd,
    buttons = listOf(
        ThumbnailToolbarButton(id = 0, tooltip = "Previous", icon = TaskbarIconSource.FromFile("icons/prev.ico")),
        ThumbnailToolbarButton(id = 1, tooltip = "Play", icon = TaskbarIconSource.FromFile("icons/play.ico")),
    ),
    onClick = { buttonId -> handleTransport(buttonId) },
)
```

Windows allows no new buttons after the first call. Change icon, tooltip, or flags with
`updateButtons(hwnd, buttons)` using the same ids, hide one with `hidden = true`, and call
`unregister(hwnd)` when the window closes. `onClick` runs on the UI thread.

## Show a badge

A count or status glyph on the taskbar button and Start tile. Windows grants badges only to APPX
and MSIX apps, and `initialize()` is the call that fails elsewhere (`isAvailable` is `true` on any
Windows machine):

```kotlin
if (WindowsBadgeManager.initialize()) {
    WindowsBadgeManager.setGlyph(BadgeGlyph.NEW_MESSAGE)
    WindowsBadgeManager.setCount(5) // 1 to 99, then "99+"; 0 clears
}
```

Call `uninitialize()` on shutdown.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Overlay icons and the thumbnail toolbar use COM `ITaskbarList3`, keyed by `HWND`. Jump lists
  use `ICustomDestinationList`. Windows owns that menu, which is why entries carry `arguments`
  instead of a callback.
- Badges use WinRT and need the package identity. Pass an `aumid` to `initialize` to override it.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Symbol | Notes |
|---|---|
| `WindowsOverlayIcon.setIcon(hwnd, icon, description = "")` / `clearIcon(hwnd)` | Return `Boolean`. |
| `WindowsOverlayIcon.isAvailable` / `lastError` | Native library loaded; last failure message. |
| `WindowsJumpListManager.setProcessAppId(aumid = null)` | Sets the process AUMID. |
| `WindowsJumpListManager.setJumpList(categories, tasks, knownCategories)` | Every parameter defaults to empty. |
| `WindowsJumpListManager.clearJumpList()` | Removes every entry. |
| `JumpListCategory(name, items)` | A named group of entries. |
| `JumpListItem(title, arguments, description, icon, isSeparator)` | Every parameter has a default. `JumpListItem.SEPARATOR` is valid in `tasks` only. |
| `KnownCategory.FREQUENT` / `RECENT` | Shell-managed lists fed by your file associations. |
| `WindowsThumbnailToolbar.setButtons(hwnd, buttons, onClick = null)` | Up to 7 buttons, once per window. |
| `WindowsThumbnailToolbar.updateButtons(hwnd, buttons)` / `unregister(hwnd)` | Update registered buttons; remove the callback. |
| `ThumbnailToolbarButton(id, tooltip, icon, enabled, hidden, noBackground, dismissOnClick, nonInteractive)` | `id` from `0` to `6`, `tooltip` at most 259 characters. |
| `WindowsBadgeManager.initialize(aumid = null)` | Required first. APPX and MSIX only. |
| `WindowsBadgeManager.setCount(count)` / `setGlyph(glyph)` / `clear()` / `uninitialize()` | `BadgeGlyph.NONE` clears a glyph. |

`BadgeGlyph`: `NONE`, `ACTIVITY`, `ALARM`, `ALERT`, `ATTENTION`, `AVAILABLE`, `AWAY`, `BUSY`,
`ERROR`, `NEW_MESSAGE`, `PAUSED`, `PLAYING`, `UNAVAILABLE`.

`TaskbarIconSource` is one of `FromStock(StockIcon.WARNING)` (93 built-in icons, no file),
`FromFile(path)` (an `.ico`), or `FromResource(dllPath, index)` (an icon in a DLL such as
`shell32.dll`).

## What's next

- [Taskbar progress](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/progress): progress bars in the taskbar button.
- [Single instance](/docs/lifecycle/single-instance): forward jump-list arguments to the running app.
- [macOS Dock menu](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/macos): the Dock menu on macOS.
- [Linux launcher](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/linux): launcher entries and quicklists on Linux.

# Linux launcher

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/dock-taskbar/linux

Set count badges, progress bars, urgency flags, and right-click quicklist menus on the Linux launcher from Kotlin.

`launcher-linux` draws count badges, progress bars, and urgency flags on your launcher icon, and
attaches a right-click quicklist. Unity, KDE Plasma, Plank, and budgie-panel support it. XFCE
without `docklike-plugin` does not: calls succeed and nothing is drawn.

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.launcher-linux:<version>")
}
```

## Set badges and progress

Build the launcher URI from your `.desktop` file name, which `launcher-linux` never guesses, then
set one property or several at once:

```kotlin
val appUri = LinuxLauncherEntry.appUri("myapp.desktop")

LinuxLauncherEntry.setCount(appUri, 42)
LinuxLauncherEntry.setProgress(appUri, 0.65) // 0.0..1.0

LinuxLauncherEntry.update(
    appUri,
    LauncherProperties(count = 5, countVisible = true, progress = 0.8, progressVisible = true),
)
```

`update` sends every non-null field in one signal. For a cross-platform progress bar that finds
the `.desktop` file for you, use [Taskbar progress](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/progress).

## Add a quicklist menu

Create a `LinuxQuicklist` on a D-Bus object path of your choice, install the menu, then point the
launcher entry at that path:

```kotlin
val quicklist = LinuxQuicklist("/com/example/MyApp/Menu")

quicklist.listener = LinuxQuicklist.Listener { id ->
    when (id) {
        1 -> openNewWindow()
        8 -> exitApp()
    }
}

quicklist.setMenu(listOf(
    DbusmenuItem(id = 1, label = "New Window", icon = FreedesktopIcon.Action.WINDOW_NEW),
    DbusmenuItem.separator(id = 2),
    DbusmenuItem(id = 8, label = "Quit", disposition = DbusmenuItem.Disposition.ALERT),
))

LinuxLauncherEntry.update(appUri, LauncherProperties(quicklist = quicklist.objectPath))
```

Icons come from [`freedesktop-icons`](/docs/os/icons/freedesktop). To change a toggle, call
`setMenu(...)` again with the new `toggleState`. On shutdown, unset the quicklist and release it:

```kotlin
LinuxLauncherEntry.update(appUri, LauncherProperties(quicklist = ""))
quicklist.dispose()
```

Quicklist clicks now arrive on the host UI thread instead of the Swing EDT. Under
`nucleusApplication` that is the thread Compose uses. See [Threading](/docs/concepts/threading)
and [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Nucleus emits an `Update` signal on the `com.canonical.Unity.LauncherEntry` D-Bus interface
  with your `.desktop` URI. Each `LinuxQuicklist` registers a `com.canonical.dbusmenu` object,
  and the shell re-reads its layout each time it opens the menu.
- The native bridge uses GIO/GDBus, with no Java D-Bus library.
- Without a session bus (`DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` unset), the module reports no bus instead of
  spawning `dbus-launch`.
- In a plain Compose Desktop or Swing host, quicklist clicks run on the AWT event dispatch thread.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Symbol | Notes |
|---|---|
| `LinuxLauncherEntry.isAvailable` | `false` off Linux or when the native library failed to load. |
| `LinuxLauncherEntry.appUri(desktopFileId)` | Builds the `application://<id>` URI. |
| `LinuxLauncherEntry.update(appUri, properties): Boolean` | Sends every non-null field. |
| `setCount` / `clearCount` / `setProgress` / `clearProgress` / `setUrgent` / `setUpdating` | Wrappers over `update`. |
| `registerQueryHandler(appUri)` / `unregister()` | Answers the shell's queries for the entry state, then stops. |
| `LauncherProperties(count, countVisible, progress, progressVisible, urgent, quicklist, updating)` | All nullable; null fields are skipped. `quicklist = ""` unsets the menu. |
| `LinuxQuicklist(objectPath)` | `listener`, `setMenu(items): Boolean`, `dispose()`. |
| `LinuxQuicklist.Listener.onItemClicked(itemId: Int)` | `fun interface`, called on the host UI thread. |
| `DbusmenuItem.separator(id)` | A separator. |

`DbusmenuItem` fields: `id` (`> 0`), `label` (`_` marks a mnemonic), `icon` (a
`FreedesktopIcon`), `enabled`, `visible`, `type` (`STANDARD`, `SEPARATOR`), `toggleType` (`NONE`,
`CHECKBOX`, `RADIO`), `toggleState` (`-1` indeterminate, `0` unchecked, `1` checked), `shortcut`,
`disposition` (`NORMAL`, `INFORMATIONAL`, `WARNING`, `ALERT`), and `children`.

## What's next

- [Taskbar progress](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/progress): cross-platform progress and attention.
- [Freedesktop icons](/docs/os/icons/freedesktop): symbolic icon names for menu items.
- [macOS Dock menu](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/macos): the Dock menu on macOS.

# Progress and attention

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/dock-taskbar/progress

Show progress and attention requests on the Dock icon, the taskbar button, or the Linux launcher entry from Kotlin.

Taskbar progress draws a progress bar and requests attention on the macOS Dock icon, the Windows
taskbar button, or the Linux launcher entry. When the desktop does not support it, calls return
`false` instead of throwing.

## Add the dependency

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.taskbar-progress-tao:<version>")
}
```

A plain Compose Desktop or Swing host uses `taskbar-progress` alone. See
[Use the plain API](#use-the-plain-api).

## Show progress from a window

```kotlin
DecoratedWindow(onCloseRequest = ::exitApplication) {
    val progress by download.progress.collectAsState()

    LaunchedEffect(progress) {
        if (progress < 1.0) nucleusWindow.showTaskbarProgress(progress)
        else nucleusWindow.hideTaskbarProgress()
    }
    DisposableEffect(Unit) {
        onDispose { nucleusWindow.hideTaskbarProgress() }
    }
}
```

The value is a fraction in `0.0..1.0`. Clear it in `onDispose` so a stale bar does not outlive the
screen that set it. `showTaskbarIndeterminate()`, `showTaskbarError()`, `showTaskbarPaused()`,
`requestTaskbarAttention()` and `stopTaskbarAttention()` work the same way.

On macOS and Linux, progress belongs to the app, not the window: two windows share one indicator.

Inside composition, `rememberTaoTaskbarProgress()` returns a handle bound to the current window
(`null` outside one): `taskbar?.showProgress(progress)`.

## Use the plain API

`TaskbarProgress` takes a `java.awt.Window`, for Compose Desktop and Swing hosts:

```kotlin
TaskbarProgress.showProgress(window, 0.75)
TaskbarProgress.showError(window, 1.0)
TaskbarProgress.hideProgress(window)
TaskbarProgress.requestAttention(window, TaskbarProgress.AttentionType.INFORMATIONAL)
```

`nucleusApplication` windows have no AWT `Window`. Move those calls to the `nucleusWindow`
extensions. See [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

## Set the Linux desktop file

If `.desktop` detection fails, `isAvailable()` returns `false`. Set the name yourself:

```kotlin
TaskbarProgress.linuxDesktopFilename = "myapp.desktop"
```

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Linux uses the Unity `LauncherEntry` D-Bus protocol, shared with
  [`launcher-linux`](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/linux).
- The `nucleusWindow` extensions run on a worker thread: `true` means queued, not drawn.
- Linux detection tries `NucleusApp.appId`, `GIO_LAUNCHED_DESKTOP_FILE`, `BAMF_DESKTOP_FILE_HINT`,
  the executable name, then an `Exec` match in the XDG application directories.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| `nucleusWindow` extension | `TaskbarProgress` | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `showTaskbarProgress(value)` | `showProgress(window, value)` | `NORMAL` at `value` |
| `showTaskbarIndeterminate()` | `showIndeterminate(window)` | `INDETERMINATE` |
| `showTaskbarError(value = 1.0)` | `showError(window, value)` | `ERROR` at `value` |
| `showTaskbarPaused(value = 1.0)` | `showPaused(window, value)` | `PAUSED` at `value` |
| `hideTaskbarProgress()` | `hideProgress(window)` | `NO_PROGRESS` |
| `setTaskbarProgress(value)` / `setTaskbarState(state)` | `setProgress` / `setState` | Fraction or state alone |
| `requestTaskbarAttention(type)` / `stopTaskbarAttention()` | `requestAttention` / `stopAttention` | Start or cancel attention |

`TaskbarProgress` also has `isAvailable()`, `linuxDesktopFilename`, and `*ForHwnd` variants for a
raw Windows `HWND`.

| State | Windows | macOS | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| `INDETERMINATE` | Pulsing bar | Static bar | Same as `NORMAL` |
| `NORMAL` | Green | Blue | Accent |
| `ERROR` | Red | Red | Plain progress; add `requestAttention` |
| `PAUSED` | Yellow | Yellow | Plain progress |

| `AttentionType` | Windows | macOS |
|---|---|---|
| `INFORMATIONAL` | Flashes four times | Bounces once |
| `CRITICAL` | Flashes until focused | Bounces until activated |

On Linux, both set the `urgent` flag.

- [Linux launcher](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/linux): badges, urgency, and quicklists.
- [macOS Dock menu](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/macos): the Dock menu.
- [Energy manager](/docs/lifecycle/energy-manager): keep the machine awake during long work.
