# macOS menu bar

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/menus/menu-bar

Build the native macOS menu bar from Compose, with items, shortcuts, icons, badges, and submenus that follow your state.

`menu-macos` builds the native macOS menu bar from Compose. You declare menus and items as a tree,
and the bar updates when the state it reads changes. `NativeMenuBar` does nothing on Windows and
Linux, so the call can stay in shared code.

## Add the dependency

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.menu-macos:<version>")
}
```

It brings [`sf-symbols`](/docs/os/icons/sf-symbols) for typed icon names.

## Build a menu bar

```kotlin
fun main() = nucleusApplication {
    NativeMenuBar {
        Menu("MyApp") {
            Item("About MyApp") { showAbout() }
            Separator()
            Item("Quit MyApp", shortcut = NativeKeyShortcut("q")) { exitApplication() }
        }
        Menu("File") {
            Item(
                "New",
                shortcut = NativeKeyShortcut("n"),
                icon = NsMenuItemImage.SystemSymbol(SFSymbolObjectsAndTools.DOCUMENT_BADGE_PLUS),
            ) { newDocument() }
            Menu("Recent") {
                Item("notes.md") { open("notes.md") }
            }
        }
        MenuWindow("Window")
        MenuHelp("Help") {
            Item("Documentation") { openDocs() }
        }
    }

    // Windows
}
```

- The first `Menu` becomes the application menu, the bold entry named after your app. A `Menu`
  inside a `Menu` is a submenu.
- Keep `NativeMenuBar` outside any window's content, so the bar stays while windows open and
  close.
- macOS fills `MenuWindow` (window list, Bring All to Front) and `MenuHelp` (search field); their
  content is optional.
- Click handlers run on the UI thread and can change Compose state.

## Add checkboxes and radio buttons

You hold the state; the item shows the checkmark:

```kotlin
var darkMode by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }

Menu("View") {
    CheckboxItem("Dark mode", checked = darkMode, onCheckedChange = { darkMode = it })
    Separator()
    RadioButtonItem("Light", selected = !darkMode, onClick = { darkMode = false })
    RadioButtonItem("Dark", selected = darkMode, onClick = { darkMode = true })
}
```

## Add search and section headers

```kotlin
Menu("History") {
    SearchField(placeholder = "Search history")
    SectionHeader("Today")
    Item("nucleusframework.dev") { open(url) }
}
```

`SearchField` filters the menu's items by title as the user types. `SectionHeader` needs macOS 14
and falls back to a disabled item on older systems.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- On first composition, `NativeMenuBar` saves the current menu bar and installs an `NSMenu` built
  from your tree. It restores the saved bar when it leaves the composition.
- `MenuWindow` and `MenuHelp` become AppKit's Window and Help menus.
- AppKit fires actions on its main thread; Nucleus posts them to `Dispatchers.Main`.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

`Item(text) { onClick }` parameters:

| Parameter | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `enabled` | Grey the item out when `false` |
| `shortcut` | `NativeKeyShortcut(key)`: Command by default; add `shift`, `option`, `control`, `function`, or `command = false`. `NativeKey` holds `ESCAPE`, `RETURN`, `TAB`, `DELETE`, `BACKSPACE`, arrow keys and more |
| `icon` | `NsMenuItemImage.SystemSymbol` (an `SFSymbol` or raw name, macOS 11+), `Named` (AppKit or bundle image), or `File` |
| `state` | `NsMenuItemState.OFF`, `ON`, or `MIXED` |
| `badge` | `NsMenuItemBadge.Count`, `Text`, or the localized `Alerts`, `NewItems`, `Updates` (macOS 14+) |
| `subtitle` | Second line under the title (macOS 14.4+) |
| `toolTip` / `tag` / `indentationLevel` | Hover text / integer tag / indentation |
| `isAlternate` | Show in place of the previous item while its modifier is held |
| `isHidden` | Hide the item but keep its key equivalent |
| `onStateImage`, `offStateImage`, `mixedStateImage` | Replace the checkmark per state |

`Menu` also accepts an `icon`.

## What's next

- [SF Symbols](/docs/os/icons/sf-symbols): typed names for `SystemSymbol` icons.
- [Context menus](/docs/os/menus/context-menu): native right-click menus inside your windows.
- [Application entry point](/docs/lifecycle/application): how Cmd+Q and Dock > Quit reach your windows.

# Context menus

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/menus/context-menu

Replace Compose-drawn context menus with the platform menu, NSMenu on macOS and a Fluent, Adwaita, or Breeze flyout on Windows and Linux.

Nucleus replaces Compose's context menus with the platform menu: an `NSMenu` on macOS, and a
flyout styled as Fluent on Windows, Adwaita on GTK desktops, or Breeze on Qt desktops. It comes
with `nucleus-application`.

## Turn on the native menu

```kotlin
fun main() = nucleusApplication {
    DecoratedWindow(
        onCloseRequest = ::exitApplication,
        title = "MyApp",
        nativeContextMenu = true,
    ) {
        // Text fields now show the platform Cut/Copy/Paste menu
    }
}
```

The flag covers `ContextMenuArea`, the text-field Cut/Copy/Paste menu, and
[spell-check suggestions](/docs/os/spell-check). `HostedWindow` and the Material and Jewel windows
take the same parameter. The style follows the platform, and on Linux the session's toolkit.

## Add your own items

`NucleusContextMenuItem` extends Compose's `ContextMenuItem` with an icon and a shortcut label:

```kotlin
ContextMenuArea(
    items = {
        listOf(
            NucleusContextMenuItem(
                label = "Reveal in Finder",
                icon = ContextMenuIcon.Folder,
                onClick = { revealInFileManager(path) },
            ),
            NucleusContextMenuDivider,
            NucleusContextMenuItem(
                label = "Delete",
                icon = ContextMenuIcon.Delete,
                shortcut = "Del",
                onClick = { delete(path) },
            ),
        )
    },
) {
    FileRow(path)
}
```

`NucleusContextMenuSubmenu` nests a group. Its `items` lambda runs when the menu opens, so it can
list data that changes:

```kotlin
NucleusContextMenuSubmenu(label = "Open recent") { recentFiles.map { fileItem(it) } }
```

Icons differ per platform: Adwaita shows none, and `ContextMenuIcon.SfSymbol` applies to macOS
only.

## Show keyboard shortcuts

An item with a stock editing icon gets the platform label on its own: `⌘C` on macOS, `Ctrl+C`
elsewhere. Pass `shortcut` to override it, or `shortcut = ""` to hide it. The macOS `NSMenu` does
not show shortcut labels.

## How the flyout behaves on screen

On Windows and Linux the flyout opens in its own native popup surface, even when the window keeps
`nativePopupLayers = false`. Your other popups still follow that flag.

The flyout can leave its window and stays within the work area of its display. A second right
click while the menu is open moves it to the new spot. The flyout closes when its window loses
focus.

To give one of your own popups the same treatment, wrap it:

```kotlin
NativePopupLayers {
    DropdownMenu(expanded = open, onDismissRequest = { open = false }) { /* … */ }
}
```

See [Dialogs and popups](/docs/windows/dialogs-popups) for the full popup-layer model.

## Detect the Linux toolkit

Read the value Nucleus uses to pick the Linux style, for example to match another widget:

```kotlin
when (LinuxUiToolkit.Current) {
    LinuxUiToolkit.Qt -> // KDE Plasma, LXQt, Deepin, …
    LinuxUiToolkit.Gtk -> // GNOME, Xfce, Cinnamon, MATE, …
}
```

Unknown desktops and bare tiling window managers resolve to `Gtk`.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- macOS renders the menu through [`menu-macos`](/docs/os/menus/menu-bar). If its native library fails
  to load, `isNativeContextMenuSupported` is `false` and Compose menus stay.
- Under native Wayland the flyout maps as an `xdg_popup`, so the compositor flips or slides it to
  stay on screen.
- Nucleus drops leading, trailing, and repeated separators, and an empty list closes the menu.
- `LinuxUiToolkit.Current` reads `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`, `DESKTOP_SESSION`, and
  `XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP`, then `KDE_FULL_SESSION` and `QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME`.
- The Fluent flyout paints the acrylic fallback color and does not blur what sits behind it.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

Package `dev.nucleusframework.application.contextmenu`.

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| `NucleusContextMenuItem(label, enabled, icon, shortcut, onClick)` | Item with an optional icon and shortcut label. |
| `NucleusContextMenuDivider` | Separator item. |
| `NucleusContextMenuSubmenu(label) { items }` | Nested group. `items` runs when the menu opens. |
| `ContextMenuIcon` | `Cut`, `Copy`, `Paste`, `SelectAll`, `Delete`, `Folder`, `SfSymbol(name)`. |
| `ContextMenuIcon.stockShortcut()` | Platform shortcut label for the editing icons, else `null`. |
| `NativeContextMenuProvider(enabled) { }` | Installs the native menu for a subtree without the window parameter. |
| `isNativeContextMenuSupported` | Whether this platform can show it. |
| `LocalContextMenuDivider` | The separator the active renderer draws, or `null`. |
| `LocalContextMenuItemInterpreter` | Overrides how Compose items map to `ContextMenuEntry` for a subtree. |
| `NativePopupLayers { }` | Package `dev.nucleusframework.window.tao`. Opens a subtree's popups in native surfaces. |

To show an `NSMenu` yourself, `menu-macos` provides `popUpNativeMenu(items)` with
`NativePopupMenuItem` entries. It blocks until the menu closes.

Call `popUpNativeMenu` off the UI thread. From a UI-thread callback it stops frames, animations,
`Dispatchers.Main`, and `delay` until the menu closes.

## What's next

- [Spell check](/docs/os/spell-check): suggestions inside these menus.
- [Dialogs and popups](/docs/windows/dialogs-popups): native popup layers for the rest of your
  popups.
- [macOS menu bar](/docs/os/menus/menu-bar): the application menu, on the same native layer.

# File dialogs

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/file-dialogs

Open, save and folder pickers with FileKit, set up for you by nucleusApplication.

Nucleus apps use [FileKit](https://filekit.mintlify.app) for native open, save and folder
pickers. Add the dependency and call FileKit: Nucleus does the setup. For the full API (file
types, multiple selection, savers, `PlatformFile`), see the
[FileKit documentation](https://filekit.mintlify.app/dialogs/setup).

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("io.github.vinceglb:filekit-dialogs:<filekit-version>")
}
```

## Pick a file

```kotlin
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()

Button(onClick = {
    scope.launch {
        val file = FileKit.openFilePicker(type = FileKitType.Image)
        // file is null when the user cancels
    }
}) {
    Text("Open image")
}
```

## What Nucleus does for you

- **Initialization.** `nucleusApplication` calls `FileKit.init(NucleusApp.appId)` when FileKit is
  on the classpath. Dev runs, packaged apps and native images share one files directory.
- **Uninstall.** On Windows that directory is `%APPDATA%\<appId>`, which the NSIS uninstaller
  removes when you set `deleteAppDataOnUninstall`.
- **Native image.** The Nucleus plugin ships FileKit's GraalVM metadata, so the pickers work in a
  native image with no configuration.

The automatic `FileKit.init` is new. Your own `FileKit.init(…)` before `nucleusApplication` still
wins, a call inside `content` replaces the automatic one, and
`nucleusApplication(args, initializeFileKit = false)` turns it off. See
[Migrate from Nucleus 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x#check-the-filekit-initialization).

## Attach the dialog to a window

To make the picker modal to a window, pass the window's platform handle from
`nucleusWindow.unsafe.taoWindow`: `nativeHandle` on Windows, `nsWindowHandle` on macOS, and
`xdgPortalParent()` on Linux (X11 and Wayland).

## What's next

- [Application entry point](/docs/lifecycle/application): every `nucleusApplication` option.
- [FileKit documentation](https://filekit.mintlify.app): the full picker and file API.
- [Windows](/docs/windows): `nucleusWindow` and the native window handle.

# SF Symbols

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/icons/sf-symbols

Typed Kotlin constants for Apple SF Symbols names used by macOS APIs.

`sf-symbols` provides Apple's [SF Symbols](https://developer.apple.com/sf-symbols/) names as
typed Kotlin constants. You write `SFSymbolObjectsAndTools.SCISSORS` instead of `"scissors"`, and
the compiler catches typos.

## Add the dependency

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.sf-symbols:<version>")
}
```

[`menu-macos`](/docs/os/menus/menu-bar) already brings it.

## Reference a symbol

Pick the constant from the category enum that matches its use, and pass it to a macOS API that
takes a symbol:

```kotlin
val icon = NsMenuItemImage.SystemSymbol(SFSymbolObjectsAndTools.SCISSORS)

// A name the constants do not cover, such as one from a newer SF Symbols release
val custom = SFSymbol.Custom("bird.fill")
```

Number symbols take an underscore prefix, since Kotlin identifiers cannot start with a digit:
`SFSymbolNumbers._0_CIRCLE` maps to `"0.circle"`. SF Symbols need macOS 11 or later; the module
still compiles and loads on every OS.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Each constant carries its name in `symbolName` (`GEAR` holds `"gear"`). `Custom` is an inline
  value class that wraps any string, passed unchanged.
- AppKit resolves the name with `imageWithSystemSymbolName:accessibilityDescription:` at render
  time, so the glyph follows the system appearance and you ship no image assets.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

`SFSymbol` is a sealed interface with 21 category enums plus `Custom(symbolName)`:

| Category | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| `SFSymbolGeneral` | `GEAR`, `GEARSHAPE` |
| `SFSymbolHuman` | `ACCESSIBILITY`, `BRAIN` |
| `SFSymbolShapes` | `APP`, `APP_BADGE` |
| `SFSymbolArrows` | `ARROW_LEFT`, `ARROW_CLOCKWISE` |
| `SFSymbolTransportation` | `AIRPLANE`, `AIRPLANE_ARRIVAL` |
| `SFSymbolObjectsAndTools` | `SCISSORS`, `FOLDER`, `TRASH` |
| `SFSymbolDevices` | `DESKTOPCOMPUTER`, `KEYBOARD` |
| `SFSymbolNumbers` | `_0_CIRCLE`, `_0_CIRCLE_FILL` |
| `SFSymbolWeather` | `CLOUD`, `SUN_MAX`, `BOLT` |
| `SFSymbolStatus` | `CHECKMARK`, `INFO_CIRCLE` |
| `SFSymbolCommerce` | `BAG`, `BAG_BADGE_PLUS` |
| `SFSymbolMedia` | `PLAY`, `PAUSE`, `STOP` |
| `SFSymbolLetters` | `A_CIRCLE`, `A_SQUARE` |
| `SFSymbolTextFormatting` | `BOLD`, `CHARACTER` |
| `SFSymbolCommunication` | `ENVELOPE`, `PHONE`, `MESSAGE` |
| `SFSymbolPower` | `POWER`, `POWER_CIRCLE` |
| `SFSymbolSecurity` | `KEY`, `KEY_FILL` |
| `SFSymbolHealth` | `ALLERGENS`, `BASEBALL` |
| `SFSymbolLocation` | `FLAG`, `COMPASS_DRAWING` |
| `SFSymbolTime` | `ALARM`, `ALARM_FILL` |
| `SFSymbolConnectivity` | `CABLE_COAXIAL`, `CABLE_CONNECTOR` |

## What's next

- [macOS menu bar](/docs/os/menus/menu-bar): use `SystemSymbol` icons on menu items.
- [FreeDesktop icon names](/docs/os/icons/freedesktop): the typed icon names for Linux.

# FreeDesktop icon names

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/icons/freedesktop

Typed Kotlin constants for the names defined by the FreeDesktop Icon Naming Specification.

`freedesktop-icons` provides the names of the
[FreeDesktop Icon Naming Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/icon-naming/latest/)
as typed Kotlin constants. You send `dialog-information` instead of shipping `info.png`, and the
user's Linux icon theme draws its own version.

## Add the dependency

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.freedesktop-icons:<version>")
}
```

`notification-linux` and `launcher-linux` already bring it.

## Reference an icon

Pick the constant from the category enum that matches its context:

```kotlin
val info = FreedesktopIcon.Status.DIALOG_INFORMATION
val printer = FreedesktopIcon.Device.PRINTER

// A name outside the specification, an absolute path, or a file:// URI
val named = FreedesktopIcon.Custom("my-app-icon")
val path = FreedesktopIcon.Custom("/home/user/icon.png")

// Country flag from an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code
val flag = FreedesktopIcon.flag("FR") // Custom("flag-fr")
```

- Themes do not implement every name. Names from the core specification have the best chance of
  a match.
- Flag names are not part of the specification. They resolve only in themes that ship
  `flag-<code>` icons.
- The module compiles on every OS, but no theme resolves the names outside Linux.

## API reference

| Category | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| `FreedesktopIcon.Action` | `DOCUMENT_OPEN`, `EDIT_COPY`, `MEDIA_PLAYBACK_START` |
| `FreedesktopIcon.Animation` | `PROCESS_WORKING` |
| `FreedesktopIcon.Application` | `ACCESSORIES_TEXT_EDITOR`, `MULTIMEDIA_VOLUME_CONTROL`, `UTILITIES_TERMINAL` |
| `FreedesktopIcon.Category` | `APPLICATIONS_INTERNET`, `PREFERENCES_DESKTOP`, `SYSTEM_HELP` |
| `FreedesktopIcon.Device` | `PRINTER`, `CAMERA_PHOTO`, `INPUT_KEYBOARD` |
| `FreedesktopIcon.Emblem` | `IMPORTANT`, `FAVORITE`, `SHARED` |
| `FreedesktopIcon.Emote` | `FACE_SMILE`, `FACE_SAD`, `FACE_WINK` |
| `FreedesktopIcon.MimeType` | `TEXT_X_GENERIC`, `IMAGE_X_GENERIC`, `X_OFFICE_DOCUMENT` |
| `FreedesktopIcon.Place` | `FOLDER`, `USER_HOME`, `NETWORK_SERVER` |
| `FreedesktopIcon.Status` | `DIALOG_INFORMATION`, `DIALOG_WARNING`, `BATTERY_LOW` |
| `FreedesktopIcon.Custom(value)` | Inline value class, sent unchanged: theme name, absolute path or `file://` URI |
| `FreedesktopIcon.flag(countryCode)` | Lowercases the code and returns `Custom("flag-<code>")` |

Each constant holds its specification name in `value`.

## What's next

- [Notifications on Linux](/docs/os/notifications/linux): pass a `FreedesktopIcon` as the notification icon.
- [Linux launcher](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/linux): use the same constants in quicklist items.
- [SF Symbols](/docs/os/icons/sf-symbols): the typed symbol names for macOS.

# Dark mode detector

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/theme/dark-mode

Read the operating system's light or dark theme from Kotlin and recompose your Compose UI when it changes.

`darkmode-detector` reports whether macOS, Windows or Linux runs in dark mode and tells you when
that changes. It comes with `nucleus-application`; declare
`dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.darkmode-detector` only to use it without `nucleusApplication`.

## Follow the system theme

Inside `nucleusApplication`, Compose's `isSystemInDarkTheme()` recomposes when the user switches
the OS theme, so Material, Jewel and third-party libraries follow it too:

```kotlin
fun main() = nucleusApplication {
    val dark = isSystemInDarkTheme()
    MaterialTheme(colorScheme = if (dark) darkColorScheme() else lightColorScheme()) {
        DecoratedWindow(onCloseRequest = ::exitApplication, title = "MyApp") {
            // Content
        }
    }
}
```

In any other Compose host, call `isSystemInDarkMode()` from
`dev.nucleusframework.darkmodedetector`. It returns the same value, and falls back to
`isSystemInDarkTheme()` in a `@Preview`.

## How nucleusApplication provides the theme

`nucleusApplication` feeds the detector's value into Compose's `LocalSystemTheme`, which every
window inherits. It also turns off Compose's once-a-second theme polling
(`ComposeUiFlags.pollSystemTheme`) before it creates any window.

## Read the theme outside Compose

```kotlin
val detector = getPlatformDarkModeDetector()
val dark: Boolean = detector.isDark()

val listener = Consumer<Boolean> { isDark -> println("dark mode: $isDark") }
detector.registerListener(listener)
// Later
detector.removeListener(listener)
```

The listener runs on the thread that receives the OS notification. Move UI work to
`Dispatchers.Main`.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- macOS observes the `AppleInterfaceStyle` preference through `NSDistributedNotificationCenter`.
- Windows watches `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize\AppsUseLightTheme`
  with `RegNotifyChangeKeyValue`.
- Linux reads the XDG Desktop Portal `color-scheme` setting. The value `1` means dark.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Symbol | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `isSystemInDarkMode()` | Composable, recomposes on change |
| `getPlatformDarkModeDetector()` | Detector for the current OS, or `NoopDarkModeDetector` elsewhere |
| `IDarkModeDetector.isDark()` | Current theme |
| `registerListener(Consumer<Boolean>)` / `removeListener` | Change notifications |
| `NoopDarkModeDetector` | Always light, ignores listeners. For tests and headless runs |

## What's next

- [System accent color](/docs/os/theme/accent-color): read the accent color and high-contrast state.
- [Toolkits](/docs/toolkits): themed windows that follow the OS appearance.
- [Application entry point](/docs/lifecycle/application): what else `nucleusApplication` sets up.

# System accent color

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/theme/accent-color

Read the user's OS accent color and high-contrast setting as Compose state that follows system changes.

`system-color` reads the user's accent color and high-contrast setting on macOS, Windows and
Linux. Both are composables that recompose when the user changes them in the system settings.

## Add the dependency

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.system-color:<version>")
}
```

## Read the accent color

```kotlin
import dev.nucleusframework.systemcolor.systemAccentColor

@Composable
fun App() {
    val accent = systemAccentColor()
    val scheme = if (accent != null) darkColorScheme(primary = accent) else darkColorScheme()

    MaterialTheme(colorScheme = scheme) {
        // Recomposes when the user picks another accent.
    }
}
```

`systemAccentColor()` returns `null` when the OS does not report an accent, for example on a Linux
desktop whose portal lacks the `accent-color` key. Fall back to your brand color.

## Read the high-contrast setting

```kotlin
val highContrast = isSystemInHighContrast()
// Strengthen borders and contrast tokens when highContrast is true.
```

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Each OS bridge subscribes to the system's change notifications; nothing polls.
- On Linux, the values come from the `accent-color` and `contrast` keys of
  `org.freedesktop.portal.Settings`.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Function | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `isSystemAccentColorSupported(): Boolean` | Whether the OS can report an accent color. Not composable, so you can call it anywhere |
| `@Composable systemAccentColor(): Color?` | The current accent color, or `null` |
| `@Composable isSystemInHighContrast(): Boolean` | Whether the OS runs in high-contrast mode |

## What's next

- [Dark mode detector](/docs/os/theme/dark-mode): combine the accent with the system theme.
- [Accessibility](/docs/input/accessibility): expose your UI to screen readers.
- [Toolkits](/docs/toolkits): native window looks for each OS.

# Global hotkeys

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/global-hotkey

Register system-wide keyboard shortcuts that fire while your app is in the background.

`global-hotkey` registers keyboard shortcuts that fire whichever app has focus, on macOS, Windows
and Linux.

## Add the dependency

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.global-hotkey:<version>")
}
```

## Register a hotkey

```kotlin
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()

DisposableEffect(Unit) {
    GlobalHotKeyManager.initialize()
    val handle = GlobalHotKeyManager.register(
        keyCode = KeyEvent.VK_K,
        modifiers = HotKeyModifier.CONTROL + HotKeyModifier.SHIFT,
    ) { _, _ ->
        scope.launch { showQuickSwitcher() }
    }
    onDispose { GlobalHotKeyManager.unregister(handle) }
}
```

- `register` returns a handle, or `-1` when the system refuses the binding. `lastError` says why.
- `keyCode` takes the `java.awt.event.KeyEvent` constants. The module does not start AWT.
- The listener runs on a native thread. Switch to a composition scope or `Dispatchers.Main` before
  you touch state.
- `GlobalHotKeyManager.register(MediaKey.PLAY_PAUSE) { … }` binds a media key on Windows and
  Linux. On macOS it returns `-1`; use [media controls](/docs/os/media-control) there.

## Linux portal registrations

On Wayland, the desktop portal asks the user to approve your shortcuts, once per chord. Nucleus
batches `register` calls into one dialog, and `description` labels each shortcut in it. Call
`commitRegistrations()` to show the dialog now and learn whether the portal accepted the set.

The portal needs a reverse-DNS `.desktop` file, and the app must start from it. Compositors
without the portal do not deliver global shortcuts.

macOS can ask the user to allow your app under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Input
Monitoring, and sometimes Accessibility. Callbacks stay silent until the user accepts. Open that
pane with `x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_ListenEvent`.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Backends: `RegisterHotKey` on Windows, Carbon `RegisterEventHotKey` on macOS, `XGrabKey` on
  X11, `org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts` on Wayland.
- The portal remembers each grant per `(app_id, shortcut_id)`. Nucleus derives the id from the
  chord (`nucleus_m{mods}_k{keyCode}`), so it stays stable across launches.
  `portalShortcutId(handle)` returns it, or `null` off Linux.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Symbol | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `initialize()` | Loads the native library and starts the event source |
| `register(keyCode, modifiers = 0, description = null, listener): Long` | Also `register(MediaKey, listener)`: `PLAY_PAUSE`, `STOP`, `NEXT_TRACK`, `PREV_TRACK` |
| `HotKeyModifier.ALT` / `CONTROL` / `SHIFT` / `META` | Combine with `+`; `0 + META` for one. On macOS `ALT` is Option and `META` is Command, elsewhere `META` is Windows or Super |
| `commitRegistrations()` | Shows the Wayland portal dialog now |
| `isAvailable` / `lastError` | Native library loaded; last failure message, `null` after a success |
| `unregister(handle): Boolean` / `shutdown()` | Release one binding / all of them. Call `shutdown()` on exit |

## What's next

- [Media controls](/docs/os/media-control): publish playback state and receive media commands.
- [Tray menu DSL](/docs/os/tray/menu): show shortcut hints in the tray menu.
- [Threading](/docs/concepts/threading): the threads Nucleus runs your code on.

# Media controls

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/media-control

Publish now-playing metadata to the system media center and receive playback commands on macOS, Windows, and Linux from Kotlin.

`media-control` publishes track metadata to the system media center and receives playback
commands: Now Playing on macOS, the System Media Transport Controls (SMTC) on Windows, and MPRIS
on Linux.

## Add the dependency

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.media-control:<version>")
}
```

## Publish now-playing metadata

```kotlin
if (MediaControlService.isAvailable()) {
    MediaControlService.configure()
    MediaControlService.setMetadata(
        MediaMetadata(
            title = "Strobe",
            artist = "deadmau5",
            coverUrl = "file:///tmp/cover.png",
            duration = 10 * 60 * 1_000L,
        ),
    )
    MediaControlService.setPlaybackState(
        MediaPlaybackState(status = MediaPlaybackStatus.PLAYING, positionMs = 0),
    )
}
```

Push metadata when the track changes, and a state on each play, pause, stop and seek. Times are
in milliseconds. When the native library does not load, every call does nothing.

## Handle playback commands

```kotlin
MediaControlService.attach { event ->
    when (event) {
        MediaControlEvent.Play -> player.play()
        MediaControlEvent.Pause -> player.pause()
        MediaControlEvent.Next -> player.skipToNext()
        is MediaControlEvent.SetPosition -> player.seekTo(event.positionMs)
        else -> {}
    }
}
```

The listener runs on the UI thread and can change Compose state directly. A second `attach`
replaces the first listener. `detach()` unregisters the app from the media center.

The `attach` listener ran on the AWT event dispatch thread in 2.x. It now runs on the host UI
thread (the Tao main thread). See [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

| Event | Linux | macOS | Windows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Play`, `Pause`, `Next`, `Previous`, `Stop`, `SetPosition` | yes | yes | yes |
| `Toggle` | yes | yes | no |
| `SeekBy` | yes | no | yes |
| `SetVolume`, `OpenUri`, `Raise`, `Quit` | yes | no | no |

## Platform notes

- **macOS**: set `appCategory = "public.app-category.music"` under
  `nucleus.application.nativeDistributions.macOS` so Now Playing treats the app as a media player.
  Hardware media keys then send Play, Pause, Next and Previous.
- **Windows**: test with the installed app, since SMTC identifies it through its Start Menu
  shortcut. `coverUrl` accepts `file://`, a bare path or `http(s)://`.
- **Linux**: the player appears as `org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.<suffix>`, derived from
  `NucleusApp.appId`, for `playerctl` and desktop indicators. A local `coverUrl` must use
  `file://`. If the session bus is unreachable or `dbusName` is invalid, `attach` logs a
  warning and returns, while `isAvailable()` still returns `true`.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- macOS uses `MPNowPlayingInfoCenter` and `MPRemoteCommandCenter`; the app bundle provides the
  identity.
- SMTC uses the AUMID the Nucleus plugin stamps on the Start Menu shortcut, or the MSIX package
  identity. It treats the most recent publisher as the current source.
- On Linux, `configure` registers the MPRIS bus name over D-Bus. Illegal characters in `appId`
  become `_`, elements that start with a digit get an `_` prefix, empty elements drop out, and
  the suffix stays under 255 characters.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Symbol | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `isAvailable()` | `true` when the native library loaded |
| `configure(dbusName, displayName)` | Both optional; `displayName` defaults to `NucleusApp.appName`, or `"Nucleus App"` |
| `setMetadata(MediaMetadata)` | `title`, `artist`, `album`, `coverUrl`, `duration`; each defaults to `null` |
| `setPlaybackState(MediaPlaybackState)` | `status` (`STOPPED`, `PAUSED`, `PLAYING`), optional `positionMs` |
| `setVolume(value)` | Clamped to `0.0..1.0`. macOS ignores it |
| `attach(listener)` / `detach()` | Receive `MediaControlEvent`s / stop and unregister |

## What's next

- [Global hotkeys](/docs/os/global-hotkey): bind media keys and other shortcuts system-wide.
- [Cross-platform notifications](/docs/os/notifications): show a track change as a notification.
- [Threading](/docs/concepts/threading): the thread your listener runs on.

# Spell check

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/spell-check

Check spelling in Compose text fields with each operating system's engine, NSSpellChecker on macOS, the Windows Spell Checking API, and Hunspell on Linux.

`spellcheck` checks spelling with the engine each operating system ships, underlines misspelled
words in a Compose text field and adds suggestions to its context menu. It comes with
`nucleus-application`; declare `dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.spellcheck` alone to use the engine
without Compose.

## Check a text field

Wrap the field in `SpellcheckContextMenu`:

```kotlin
import dev.nucleusframework.application.spellcheck.SpellcheckContextMenu

@Composable
fun NoteField(value: String, onValueChange: (String) -> Unit) {
    SpellcheckContextMenu(text = value, onTextChange = onValueChange) {
        BasicTextField(value = value, onValueChange = onValueChange, singleLine = true)
    }
}
```

Misspelled words get a red wavy underline. A right click lists suggestions and Add to dictionary
next to Cut, Copy and Paste. Picking a suggestion calls `onTextChange` with the new text. An
overload takes a `TextFieldState` and edits it for you:
`SpellcheckContextMenu(state = state) { TextField(state = state) }`.

The wrapper works with `BasicTextField`, Material `TextField` and Jewel `TextField`, and keeps the
menu renderer you installed, such as the [native context menu](/docs/os/menus/context-menu) or
Jewel's.

## Choose the check language

The wrapper checks in `SpellChecker.locale`, which starts as `Locale.getDefault()`. Pass `locale`
to check one field in another language, or `session` to supply your own `SpellcheckSession` (it
wins over `locale`).

To switch the whole app, assign `SpellChecker.locale`. Loading a dictionary reads from disk, so
warm the session off the UI thread:

```kotlin
LaunchedEffect(locale) {
    SpellChecker.locale = locale
    withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { SpellChecker.ensureSession(locale) }
}
```

`SpellChecker.session` blocks on first access while the dictionary loads. On a frame path, read
`sessionIfReady` instead.

## Place the menu items

`menuPlacement = SpellcheckMenuPlacement.Top` puts the suggestions above Cut, Copy, Paste and your
app items. The default, `Bottom`, puts them below. A separator appears when the menu renderer
publishes one, as the native context menu and Jewel do.

## Platform notes

- **Linux**: your users need the distribution's Hunspell library and a dictionary package
  (`<tag>.aff` and `<tag>.dic`).
  Nucleus searches `$DICPATH` (colon-separated) before the system folders.
- **macOS** and **Windows**: you ship no dictionary files. The languages come from the system
  and, on Windows, the language packs the user installed.
- With no engine or dictionary, nothing throws: `check` and `addToDictionary` return `false`,
  `suggest` returns an empty list, and `SpellcheckContextMenu` renders its content unchanged.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Engines: `NSSpellChecker` on macOS, `ISpellChecker` on Windows, Hunspell loaded with `dlopen`
  on Linux (`libhunspell-1.7.so.0`, `libhunspell-1.7.so`, `libhunspell.so.0`,
  `libhunspell-1.6.so.0`, then `libhunspell.so`).
- Linux dictionary search: `$DICPATH`, `/usr/share/hunspell`, `/usr/share/myspell/dicts`,
  `/usr/share/myspell`, `/usr/local/share/hunspell`, `$XDG_DATA_HOME/hunspell` (default
  `~/.local/share/hunspell`). The tag resolves as `lang_COUNTRY`, then the language, then an
  alias list: `en` tries `en_US` and `en_GB`, `fr` tries `fr_FR`.
- Add to dictionary writes to `~/.config/nucleus/spellcheck/<tag>.dic` (or under
  `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). The system's learned-word list stays untouched on macOS and Windows.
- A token is a run of Unicode letters with internal apostrophes (`don't`, `l'eau`). Hyphens split
  words. Nucleus skips all-digit tokens and tokens over 64 characters.
- `JewelDecoratedWindow` and `JewelDecoratedDialog` install `ProvideJewelSpellcheckMenu` for
  Jewel menu styling.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

Compose, in `dev.nucleusframework.application.spellcheck`:

| Symbol | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `SpellcheckContextMenu(text, onTextChange, session?, locale?, menuPlacement, content)` | Underlines misspellings and adds suggestions to the field's menu |
| `SpellcheckContextMenu(state, session?, locale?, menuPlacement, content)` | Same, for a `TextFieldState` |
| `NucleusSpellcheckInstaller.menuItems(word, session, onSuggestion, onAddToDictionary, separator?, menuPlacement)` | Suggestion items for a menu you assemble |
| `drawMisspellingSquiggles(drawScope, layout, ranges, color)` | Wavy underline for a custom text renderer |

Engine, in `dev.nucleusframework.spellcheck`:

| Symbol | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `SpellChecker` | Process-wide: `locale`, `session`, `sessionIfReady`, `isAvailable`, `ensureSession()`, `check()`, `suggest()`, `addToDictionary()`, `misspellings()` |
| `SpellcheckSession(locale, osName, dictionaryDirectories, userDictionaryFile)` | One dictionary, `AutoCloseable`. `defaultUserDictionaryFile(locale)` gives the user file path |
| `DictionaryLocator.defaultDirectories()` / `find(locale, directories)` | Hunspell search path / matching `DictionaryFiles(aff, dic, tag)` |
| `iterateWords`, `misspellingRanges`, `wordAt`, `replaceWord` | Tokenize text (`SpellcheckWord(start, end, word)`) and edit one token |
| `buildSpellcheckMenuModel(word, session, range?, maxSuggestions)`, `applySuggestion(text, model, suggestion)` | Suggestions plus the localized Add to dictionary label, and the edit they produce |

## What's next

- [Context menus](/docs/os/menus/context-menu): the menu the suggestions appear in.
- [Jewel](/docs/toolkits/jewel): IntelliJ-style windows with matching spell-check menus.

---

# System info

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/os/system-info

Read host details such as the OS, CPU, memory, disks, GPUs, batteries, network, processes, and users through the SystemInfo object.

`SystemInfo` reads host details on macOS, Windows and Linux: the operating system, CPU, memory,
disks, GPUs, batteries, network interfaces, processes and users.

## Add the dependency

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.system-info:<version>")
}
```

## Read the host

```kotlin
import dev.nucleusframework.systeminfo.SystemInfo

val os = SystemInfo.osInfo() ?: return
println("OS: ${os.longOsVersion} (${os.cpuArch})")

SystemInfo.memoryInfo()?.let { mem ->
    println("Memory: ${mem.usedMemory / 1_048_576} MB of ${mem.totalMemory / 1_048_576} MB")
}

SystemInfo.batteryInfo()?.let { battery ->
    println("Battery: ${(battery.stateOfCharge * 100).toInt()}% (${battery.state})")
}
```

- Each call reads the current values and returns; nothing polls or caches. To refresh a display,
  call again on your own schedule, off the UI thread for the expensive ones.
- A value the host cannot provide comes back as `null` (single values) or an empty list. No call
  throws.
- Coverage varies by OS. Windows reports few temperature sensors through `components()`, and
  `motherboard()` returns the most fields on Linux.
- `processes()` walks the whole process table. Call `process(pid)` when you need one entry.

## API reference

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `isAvailable()` | Whether the native library loaded on this OS |
| `osInfo()` | `OsInfo?`: `name`, `osVersion`, `longOsVersion`, `kernelVersion`, `distributionId`, `hostName`, `cpuArch`, `uptime`, `bootTime` |
| `cpuInfo()` | `CpuGlobalInfo?`: `globalCpuUsage`, `physicalCoreCount`, `cpus` (one `CpuInfo` per logical core: `name`, `vendorId`, `brand`, `frequency`, `cpuUsage`) |
| `memoryInfo()` | `MemoryInfo?`: `totalMemory`, `freeMemory`, `availableMemory`, `usedMemory`, `totalSwap`, `freeSwap`, `usedSwap`, in bytes |
| `disks()` | `List<DiskInfo>`: `name`, `fileSystem`, `mountPoint`, `totalSpace`, `availableSpace`, `kind`, `isRemovable`, `isReadOnly` |
| `gpus()` | `List<GpuInfo>`: name, vendor and device ids, video memory, and, where the driver reports them, `driverVersion`, `temperature`, `gpuUsage`, clocks, fan speed, power draw |
| `batteryInfo()` | `BatteryInfo?`: `stateOfCharge` (`0.0..1.0`), `state` (`Charging`, `Discharging`, `Full`, `Unknown`), `isPluggedIn`, capacities, `cycleCount`, `health`, time estimates, device identity. `null` without a battery |
| `networks()` | `List<NetworkInterfaceInfo>` |
| `connectivityInfo()` | `ConnectivityInfo?`: `isConnected`, `meteredStatus` (`NOT_AVAILABLE`, `UNKNOWN`, `UNMETERED`, `METERED`) |
| `processes()` / `process(pid: Long)` | `List<ProcessInfo>` / `ProcessInfo?` |
| `users()` | `List<UserInfo>` |
| `components()` | `List<ComponentInfo>`: temperature sensors |
| `motherboard()` / `product()` | `MotherboardInfo?` / `ProductInfo?` |
| `idleTime()` | Seconds since the last user input, or `-1` when the native library did not load |

# Lifecycle

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle

The modules that connect a Nucleus app to OS events and services that outlive a single window.

The lifecycle modules connect your app to OS events and services that outlive any window.
`nucleus-application` brings `core-runtime`; add the other modules when you need them. Each one
does nothing on platforms it does not support, so you can call it from common code.

| Stage | Module | Page |
|---|---|---|
| Startup, exit, and system quit | `nucleus-application` | [Application entry point](/docs/lifecycle/application) |
| Instance locking | `core-runtime` | [Single instance](/docs/lifecycle/single-instance) |
| URL schemes | `core-runtime` + plugin DSL | [Deep links](/docs/lifecycle/deep-links) |
| App id, version, and vendor at runtime | `core-runtime` | [App metadata](/docs/lifecycle/app-metadata) |
| Packaging format and sandbox | `core-runtime` | [Executable type](/docs/lifecycle/executable-type) |
| Dock menu (macOS) | `launcher-macos` | [macOS Dock menu](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/macos) |
| Overlay icons, jump lists, badges (Windows) | `launcher-windows` | [Windows taskbar](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/windows) |
| Launcher badges and quicklists (Linux) | `launcher-linux` | [Linux launcher](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/linux) |
| Launch at login | `autolaunch` | [Auto-launch](/docs/lifecycle/background/launch-at-login) |
| Periodic and calendar background work | `scheduler`, `scheduler-testing` | [Scheduler](/docs/lifecycle/background/scheduler) |
| `SMAppService` agents (macOS) | `service-management-macos` | [Service management](/docs/lifecycle/background/service-management) |
| Efficiency mode and keep-awake | `energy-manager` | [Energy manager](/docs/lifecycle/energy-manager) |
| Progress on the Dock or taskbar | `taskbar-progress`, `taskbar-progress-tao` | [Taskbar progress](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/progress) |
| File and directory changes | `fs-watcher` | [Filesystem watcher](/docs/lifecycle/fs-watcher) |

# Application entry point

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/application

Start a Nucleus app with nucleusApplication, and control how it quits, locks to one instance, and initializes FileKit.

`nucleusApplication` is the `main` entry point of a Nucleus app. It starts the native event loop,
runs your Compose content, and handles exit, system quit, single instance, and FileKit. It ships
in `nucleus-application`.

```kotlin
import dev.nucleusframework.application.DecoratedWindow
import dev.nucleusframework.application.nucleusApplication

fun main(args: Array<String>) = nucleusApplication(args) {
    DecoratedWindow(onCloseRequest = ::exitApplication, title = "MyApp") {
        // window content
    }
}
```

Pass the `main` arguments so deep links and login launches reach the runtime. The app ends on
`exitApplication()` or when its last window closes. Use `DecoratedWindow`, not Compose Desktop's
AWT `Window`, `Dialog`, or `Tray`: they compile in this scope but are not supported.

## Choose what happens on exit

By default the JVM exits when the event loop stops: code 0 after a normal quit, 1 after a fatal
error. Pass `exitProcessOnExit = false` to return to your `main` instead. A fatal error is then
logged at `SEVERE` and rethrown, and you call `exitProcess` yourself, since the AWT thread can
keep the JVM alive:

```kotlin
fun main(args: Array<String>) {
    nucleusApplication(args, exitProcessOnExit = false) { /* ... */ }
    flushLogs()
    exitProcess(0)
}
```

## Handle a system quit

On macOS, Cmd+Q, Dock → Quit, logout, and shutdown call `onCloseRequest` on every open window,
newest first, so your close-button logic covers a system quit. A window consents when its handler
calls `exitApplication()` or closes the window. A window that stays open vetoes the quit. A
window opened during the quit, such as a "Save changes?" dialog, delays the exit until it closes.

In 2.x, a system quit on macOS terminated the app without calling `onCloseRequest`. A handler
that never calls `exitApplication()` or closes its window now cancels the quit. See
[Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

A window that hides to the tray must let a real quit through. `isQuitting` is `true` during a
system quit and resets if a window vetoes:

```kotlin
DecoratedWindow(
    onCloseRequest = { if (isQuitting) exitApplication() else visible = false },
    visible = visible,
) { /* ... */ }
```

## Enforce a single instance

Packaged builds hold the [single-instance](/docs/lifecycle/single-instance) lock. Dev runs skip
it, so you can debug next to a packaged copy.

`enableSingleInstance` now defaults to `!ExecutableRuntime.isDev()` instead of `true`. Pass
`true` to test it from `./gradlew run`. See [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

## Initialize FileKit

When [FileKit](/docs/os/file-dialogs) is on the classpath, `nucleusApplication` calls
`FileKit.init(NucleusApp.appId)` before your content runs. Dev runs, packaged builds, and native
images then share one data directory (`%APPDATA%\<appId>` on Windows, which the uninstaller
deletes when `deleteAppDataOnUninstall` is set). Your own `FileKit.init` call, before
`nucleusApplication` or inside `content`, wins. `initializeFileKit = false` skips it.

## Set the locale and Dock policy

- `defaultLocale = Locale.FRENCH` forces the locale before any UI is built, including Compose's
  text context menu and the default spellcheck language.
- `dockIconFollowsWindows = true` (macOS) starts the app without a Dock icon and shows one only
  while a `DecoratedWindow` with `hiddenFromDock = false` is visible. Tray popups never count.

## Watch for a stalled UI

On Windows, Nucleus logs `SEVERE` with a thread dump when the event loop stops responding, and
calls your handlers on their own thread:

```kotlin
onUnresponsive { showWaitOrQuit() }
onResponsive { hideWaitOrQuit() }
```

Wrap a known long call in `expectUnresponsive { }` to skip the report. Detection rules and the
`-Dnucleus.tao.watchdog*` flags are on [Threading](/docs/concepts/threading).

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Before your content composes, `nucleusApplication` initializes GraalVM support, applies
  `defaultLocale`, takes the single-instance lock, caches
  [`AutoLaunch.wasStartedAtLogin(args)`](/docs/lifecycle/background/launch-at-login), sets the Windows AUMID
  through `launcher-windows` when present, initializes FileKit, and starts the Tao event loop,
  which serves as `Dispatchers.Main`.
- It clears `ComposeUiFlags.pollSystemTheme`, so `isSystemInDarkTheme()` follows the reactive
  `darkmode-detector` instead of polling the OS every second.
- FileKit is `compileOnly`. Without it on the classpath, the init call fails with a caught
  `LinkageError`.
- `taoApplication` in `dev.nucleusframework.window.tao` is the bare event loop underneath. It
  handles system quit but has no single-instance lock, FileKit, theme bridge, or `onDeepLink`.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

### nucleusApplication

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `args` | `Array<String>` | `emptyArray()` | `main` arguments. Scanned for deep links and the login-launch marker. |
| `enableSingleInstance` | `Boolean` | `!ExecutableRuntime.isDev()` | Acquires the single-instance lock. A second instance forwards its deep link and exits. |
| `defaultLocale` | `Locale?` | `null` | Forces `Locale.getDefault()` and the `user.*` properties before the UI starts. |
| `dockIconFollowsWindows` | `Boolean` | `false` | macOS only. Shows the Dock icon only while a visible window asks for it. |
| `exitProcessOnExit` | `Boolean` | `true` | Terminates the JVM when the app ends. `false` returns to the caller. |
| `initializeFileKit` | `Boolean` | `true` | Calls `FileKit.init(NucleusApp.appId)` when FileKit is present and not yet initialized. |
| `content` | `@Composable NucleusApplicationScope.() -> Unit` | required | The application content. |

### NucleusApplicationScope

Extends Compose's `ApplicationScope`. `LocalNucleusApplicationScope` exposes it to composables
deep in the tree.

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `exitApplication()` | Asks the event loop to stop. During a system quit, counts as this window's consent. |
| `isQuitting: Boolean` | `true` while a system quit is asking the windows to close. |
| `onDeepLink(block: (URI) -> Unit)` | Registers the deep-link callback. See [Deep links](/docs/lifecycle/deep-links). |
| `onUnresponsive(block)` / `onResponsive(block)` | Windows event-loop stall callbacks. |
| `expectUnresponsive(block): T` | Runs `block` without reporting the stall it causes. |
| `aotMode`, `isAotTraining`, `isAotRuntime` | The AOT cache mode of the running JVM. See [AOT cache](/docs/performance/aot-cache). |

# Single instance

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/single-instance

Keep one running instance of your app and forward a second launch's deep link to the primary process.

A packaged Nucleus app runs as one process. A second launch hands its
[deep link](/docs/lifecycle/deep-links) to the running process, which raises and focuses every
`DecoratedWindow`, then exits before Compose starts. `nucleusApplication` does this with no code,
the same way on macOS, Windows, and Linux.

## Enable it in dev runs

`./gradlew run` and IDE launches skip the lock, so a second debug copy starts normally. Turn it on
to test the hand-off, or pass `false` to turn it off in packaged builds too:

```kotlin
fun main(args: Array<String>) = nucleusApplication(args, enableSingleInstance = true) {
    // ...
}
```

In 2.x, `enableSingleInstance` defaulted to `true` in dev runs as well. It now defaults to
`!ExecutableRuntime.isDev()`. See [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

## React to a second launch

When your main surface is not a `DecoratedWindow`, such as a tray popup, restore it yourself.
The callback runs on the UI thread:

```kotlin
SingleInstanceRestoreEffect { popupVisible = true }
```

## Wire it manually

Without `nucleusApplication`, call `SingleInstanceManager.isSingleInstance` at the top of `main`,
before you build any UI:

```kotlin
fun main(args: Array<String>) {
    val isPrimary = SingleInstanceManager.isSingleInstance(
        onRestoreFileCreated = {
            // Second instance. `this` is the restore-request Path: write the payload.
        },
        onRestoreRequest = {
            // Primary, on a background thread.
            NucleusUiThread.post { bringMainWindowToFront() }
        },
    )
    if (!isPrimary) exitProcess(0)
    startUi(args)
}
```

`onRestoreFileCreated` is optional. To pass a URI, use
[`DeepLinkHandler.writeUriTo`](/docs/lifecycle/deep-links).

The lock is named after the app id and lives in the per-user temp directory, so two apps never
collide and two users can each run the app.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- The lock is a `java.nio.channels.FileLock` on `<lockIdentifier>.lock`. The kernel releases it
  when the JVM exits or crashes, so a killed primary does not lock the app out.
- A second launch writes `<lockIdentifier>.restore_request` next to it. The primary watches the
  directory with a `WatchService` and calls `onRestoreRequest`.
- A stale or unreadable lock file is deleted and retried once. Only an unrecoverable error makes
  the process continue as the primary.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Symbol | Notes |
|---|---|
| `SingleInstanceManager.isSingleInstance(onRestoreFileCreated, onRestoreRequest): Boolean` | `true` in the primary. `onRestoreRequest` runs on a daemon thread. |
| `SingleInstanceManager.configuration` | Assign before the first `isSingleInstance` call, or it throws `IllegalStateException`. |
| `Configuration.lockFilesDir` | Lock directory. Default `java.io.tmpdir`. |
| `Configuration.lockIdentifier` | Base name of the lock files. Default: the app id. |
| `SingleInstanceRestoreEffect(onRestore)` | Composable in `dev.nucleusframework.application`. Runs on each second launch. |

## What's next

- [Application entry point](/docs/lifecycle/application): every `nucleusApplication` option.
- [Deep links](/docs/lifecycle/deep-links): forward `myapp://` URLs from a second launch.
- [App metadata](/docs/lifecycle/app-metadata): where the app id that names the lock comes from.

# Deep links and URL schemes

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/deep-links

Register a custom URL scheme at packaging time and receive the incoming deep-link URI in your Nucleus app.

Deep links let you register a `myapp://` URL scheme and receive the incoming URI in Kotlin.
`DeepLinkHandler` ships in `core-runtime`, which comes with `nucleus-application`.

## Declare the URL scheme

The plugin registers the scheme with the OS in every installer it builds:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
nucleus.application {
    nativeDistributions {
        // protocol(name, vararg schemes): name appears in OS UI, schemes have no "://".
        protocol("MyApp", "myapp")
    }
}
```

## Handle incoming URIs

`onDeepLink` fires for the URI that launched the app and for every later activation. On Windows
and Linux, a later activation reaches the running process through the
[single-instance](/docs/lifecycle/single-instance) lock.

```kotlin
fun main(args: Array<String>) = nucleusApplication(args) {
    onDeepLink { uri: URI -> navigateTo(uri) }

    DecoratedWindow(onCloseRequest = ::exitApplication) { /* ... */ }
}
```

A URI that arrives before you register is replayed once you do. The launch URI fires once per
process, even if the registration re-runs on recomposition.

Test with a packaged build, since the installer registers the scheme: `open myapp://test`
(macOS), `start myapp://test` (Windows), or `xdg-open myapp://test` (Linux). In a dev run, pass
`enableSingleInstance = true` to test the forwarding.

## Use DeepLinkHandler without nucleusApplication

In a plain Compose Desktop or Swing host, wire `DeepLinkHandler` yourself. On macOS, also install
the AWT Apple Events handler:

```kotlin
fun main(args: Array<String>) {
    DeepLinkHandler.setHandler(args) { uri -> navigateTo(uri) }
    DeepLinkHandler.installAwtAppleEventHandler() // macOS, AWT hosts only
    startUi()
}
```

Never call `installAwtAppleEventHandler` in a `nucleusApplication` app: on macOS, AWT and the Tao
event loop deadlock. `onDeepLink { }` already receives Apple Events there.

For file associations, such as opening `.csv` files, use the plugin's `fileAssociation(...)` DSL.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- macOS registers `CFBundleURLTypes` in `Info.plist` and delivers an Apple Event to the running
  app. Windows writes `HKCU\Software\Classes\<scheme>`. Linux adds
  `MimeType=x-scheme-handler/<scheme>;` to the `.desktop` file plus an `xdg-mime` association.
  Both start a new process with the URL as an argument.
- `setHandler` reads the first deep-link-shaped entry of `args`. It accepts `myapp://path` and
  the opaque form `myapp:?query=…` (common from `xdg-open`), and rejects Windows drive paths.
- A second launch records its URI with `captureFromArgs`, writes it with `writeUriTo(path)`, and
  exits. The primary reads it with `readUriFrom(path)`, which fires your callback.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Symbol | Notes |
|---|---|
| `protocol(name, vararg schemes)` | Gradle DSL in `nativeDistributions`. |
| `NucleusApplicationScope.onDeepLink(block: (URI) -> Unit)` | Apple Events on macOS and the `args` passed to `nucleusApplication`. |
| `DeepLinkHandler.setHandler(args, onDeepLink)` | Registers the callback and delivers the launch URI once. Does not touch AWT. |
| `DeepLinkHandler.installAwtAppleEventHandler()` | macOS, AWT hosts. Initializes AWT. |
| `DeepLinkHandler.captureFromArgs(args)` | Records a URI from `args` without a callback. |
| `DeepLinkHandler.writeUriTo(path)` / `readUriFrom(path)` | Hand a URI over through a file. `readUriFrom` fires the callback. |
| `DeepLinkHandler.deliver(newUri)` | Pushes a URI through the handler, for other delivery paths and tests. |
| `DeepLinkHandler.uri` | The last URI received, including the launch URI. |
| `DeepLinkHandler.register(args, onDeepLink)` | Deprecated: always installs the AWT handler. Use `onDeepLink { }` or `setHandler`. |

## What's next

- [Single instance](/docs/lifecycle/single-instance): the lock that forwards a URI to the running process.
- [Application entry point](/docs/lifecycle/application): `nucleusApplication` and its options.
- [Windows taskbar](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/windows): jump-list entries that relaunch the app with arguments.

# App metadata at runtime

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/app-metadata

Read your app's id, version, vendor, display name, and Windows AUMID from Kotlin at runtime.

`NucleusApp` reads your app's id, version, vendor, display name, and Windows AUMID from Kotlin.
The Gradle plugin injects the values you configure, so you never hardcode them. `NucleusApp`
ships in `core-runtime`, which comes with `nucleus-application`.

## Read the metadata

```kotlin
@Composable
fun AboutDialog() {
    Column {
        Text(NucleusApp.appName ?: NucleusApp.appId)
        NucleusApp.version?.let { Text("Version $it") }
        NucleusApp.vendor?.let { Text("by $it") }
    }
}
```

`appId` and `aumid` are never null. Guard the other properties or supply a fallback.
`isConfigured` tells you whether the plugin injected metadata at all.

`isConfigured` is also `true` under `./gradlew run`. To keep auto-update or telemetry out of
development runs, test `ExecutableRuntime.isDev()`. See
[Executable type](/docs/lifecycle/executable-type).

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Each property takes the first non-blank value from the `nucleus.app.*` system properties, then
  the `nucleus/nucleus-app.properties` resource in packaged JARs. It resolves once and is cached.
- The `run` task gets only `-Dnucleus.app.id` and `-Dnucleus.executable.type`.
- `isConfigured` checks only `nucleus.app.id` and the resource file, not each property.
- The same values name the single-instance lock, the Windows AUMID used by toasts, badges, and
  jump lists, the MSIX startup task, and the FileKit data directory.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Property | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `appId` | `String` | Matches the plugin's `packageName`. Falls back to a value derived from the main class. |
| `appName` | `String?` | Display name. |
| `version` | `String?` | Application version. |
| `vendor` | `String?` | Application vendor. |
| `description` | `String?` | Application description. |
| `aumid` | `String` | Windows Application User Model ID. Falls back to `appId`. |
| `startupTaskId` | `String?` | MSIX startup task id, set when `appx { addAutoLaunchExtension = true }`. Read by [Auto-launch](/docs/lifecycle/background/launch-at-login). |
| `isConfigured` | `Boolean` | `true` when the plugin injected metadata. |

## What's next

- [Executable type](/docs/lifecycle/executable-type): tell a DMG, a Flatpak, or `./gradlew run` apart.
- [Single instance](/docs/lifecycle/single-instance): the lock named after your app id.
- [Auto-launch](/docs/lifecycle/background/launch-at-login): start the app at login with `startupTaskId`.

# Executable type

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/executable-type

Detect at runtime how the app was packaged and whether it runs in an OS sandbox, from a DMG or Snap to a plain ./gradlew run.

`ExecutableRuntime` reports how the current process was packaged (DMG, APPX, Flatpak, Snap,
`./gradlew run`, and so on) and whether it runs in an OS sandbox. Branch on it to pick an update
channel or turn off a feature the sandbox forbids. It ships in `core-runtime`, which comes with
`nucleus-application`.

## Detect the packaging format

```kotlin
when (ExecutableRuntime.type()) {
    ExecutableType.APPX    -> showMicrosoftStoreUpdate()
    ExecutableType.SNAP    -> showSnapStoreUpdate()
    ExecutableType.FLATPAK -> showFlathubUpdate()
    ExecutableType.DEV     -> Unit // no updates in development
    else                   -> checkForUpdatesDirectly()
}
```

For a single format, use the matching check, such as `ExecutableRuntime.isDev()`. Any unpackaged
run returns `DEV`, and so does an unknown or missing type, so `DEV` cannot tell an IDE run from a
misconfigured package. In dev, `nucleusApplication` skips the
[single-instance lock](/docs/lifecycle/single-instance) and
[`AutoLaunch.wasStartedAtLogin`](/docs/lifecycle/background/launch-at-login) returns `false`.

## Detect a sandbox

`isSandboxed()` returns `true` inside the macOS App Sandbox, an AppX container, or a Flatpak.
Gate sandbox-sensitive code on it, not on the format: on macOS, a PKG built with
`macOS { pkg { appStore = false } }` is not sandboxed, while the App Store PKG is.

```kotlin
if (!ExecutableRuntime.isSandboxed()) {
    registerLaunchdTask()
}
```

Code that tested `isPkg()` to detect the Mac App Store sandbox now misfires on Developer ID
PKGs. Test `isSandboxed()` instead. See [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

Which formats build sandboxed apps is covered in [Sandboxing](/docs/packaging/sandboxing).

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- The plugin records the format at build time: `-Dnucleus.executable.type=<kind>` in the
  launcher's `.cfg` for JVM apps, or a `.nucleus-executable-type` marker next to a native-image
  executable (`Contents/Resources/` on macOS). `type()` reads the property, then the marker.
- On macOS, `isSandboxed()` reads `APP_SANDBOX_CONTAINER_ID`, which macOS sets in every
  sandboxed process.
- `aot-runtime` re-exports both types as type aliases for AOT-only code.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Member | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `type()` | `ExecutableType` | The packaging format. |
| `type(propertyName)` | `ExecutableType` | Reads the format from another system property. |
| `parseType(rawValue)` | `ExecutableType` | Parses a raw string. Unknown input maps to `DEV`. |
| `isSandboxed()` | `Boolean` | `true` in the macOS App Sandbox, an AppX container, or a Flatpak. |
| `markerVersion()` | `String?` | App version from the marker file (native images). For the version in general, read [`NucleusApp.version`](/docs/lifecycle/app-metadata). |
| `isGraalVmNativeImage` | `Boolean` | `true` in a GraalVM native image. |
| `isExe()` … `isDev()` | `Boolean` | One check per `ExecutableType` value. |

`ExecutableType` values:

- Windows: `EXE`, `MSI`, `NSIS`, `NSIS_WEB`, `PORTABLE`, `APPX`
- macOS: `DMG`, `PKG`
- Linux: `DEB`, `RPM`, `SNAP`, `FLATPAK`, `APPIMAGE`, `PACMAN`
- Archives: `ZIP`, `TAR`, `SEVEN_Z`
- Development: `DEV`

## What's next

- [App metadata](/docs/lifecycle/app-metadata): the app id, version, and vendor at runtime.
- [Scheduler](/docs/lifecycle/background/scheduler): background tasks, unavailable in the macOS sandbox.
- [Auto-update](/docs/packaging/auto-update): an update strategy per distribution channel.

# Energy manager

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/energy-manager

Lower your app's OS scheduling priority in the background and keep the system or display awake from Kotlin.

`EnergyManager` lowers your app's CPU and I/O priority while it sits in the background, and keeps
the system or display awake during long work, on Windows, macOS and Linux. Add
`dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.energy-manager` to call it; `Modifier.keepScreenOn()` works without it.

## Throttle a background window

Light mode lowers CPU priority only. Full mode also throttles I/O, and network on macOS:

```kotlin
LaunchedEffect(isMinimized, isFocused) {
    when {
        isMinimized -> {
            EnergyManager.disableLightEfficiencyMode()
            EnergyManager.enableEfficiencyMode()       // CPU and I/O throttled
        }
        !isFocused -> {
            EnergyManager.disableEfficiencyMode()
            EnergyManager.enableLightEfficiencyMode()  // CPU only
        }
        else -> {
            EnergyManager.disableEfficiencyMode()
            EnergyManager.disableLightEfficiencyMode()
        }
    }
}
```

Inside a `DecoratedWindow`, read `isMinimized` and `isFocused` from `nucleusWindow`
(`minimizedFlow`, `focusFlow`). Manual `enable` and `disable` calls are yours to pair.

## Run a block at reduced priority

```kotlin
// Dedicated low-priority thread; I/O not throttled
val report = EnergyManager.withEfficiencyMode { computeHeavyReport() }

// Process-level light mode for the block, on the calling coroutine
EnergyManager.withLightEfficiencyMode { syncDataFromServer() }
```

Both helpers restore the previous mode when the block returns or throws.

## Keep the system awake

```kotlin
EnergyManager.keepAwake(AwakeMode.SYSTEM_AND_DISPLAY) // screen stays on (default)
EnergyManager.keepAwake(AwakeMode.SYSTEM_ONLY)        // screen may blank or lock
EnergyManager.releaseAwake()
```

`keepAwake` holds a single slot: a second call replaces the mode, and one `releaseAwake()` drops
the request. On macOS, closing the lid still sleeps in `SYSTEM_ONLY`.

## Hold several awake requests at once

Take one handle per independent feature, such as a player and a download:

```kotlin
val playback = EnergyManager.acquireAwake(AwakeMode.SYSTEM_AND_DISPLAY)
EnergyManager.acquireAwake(AwakeMode.SYSTEM_ONLY).use { exportProject() }
playback.close()
```

The OS request uses the strongest mode any live handle asked for, and ends once every handle is
closed and no `keepAwake` is left. `close()` is idempotent and thread-safe.

## Keep the screen on from a composable

```kotlin
Box(Modifier.keepScreenOn()) { Player() }
```

The display stays awake while the modifier is in the composition. Requests from several windows
never release each other or your `keepAwake` slot.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Windows: EcoQoS plus `IDLE_PRIORITY_CLASS` for full mode (green leaf in Task Manager 22H2+).
  Windows 10 1709+ applies EcoQoS on battery only; Windows 11 on AC too.
- macOS: full mode runs on E-cores with I/O and network throttling on Apple Silicon.
- Linux: full mode is `nice +19`, idle I/O priority and a 100 ms timer slack; light mode is
  `nice +10`. `libdbus-1`, `libX11` and `libXss` load on demand, and a missing library turns the
  matching feature off. `SYSTEM_ONLY` needs a session bus or systemd-logind; the X11 screen-saver
  fallback cannot serve it.
- `Modifier.keepScreenOn()` shares one `acquireAwake(SYSTEM_AND_DISPLAY)` handle across windows
  and popups. When the OS refuses, it logs at `FINE` and does nothing else.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `isAvailable(): Boolean` | Whether the native bridge loaded. |
| `enableEfficiencyMode()` / `disableEfficiencyMode()` | Full process mode. |
| `enableLightEfficiencyMode()` / `disableLightEfficiencyMode()` | Light process mode. |
| `enableThreadEfficiencyMode()` / `disableThreadEfficiencyMode()` | The calling thread only. |
| `withEfficiencyMode { }` (suspend) | Runs the block on a dedicated thread in thread-level mode. |
| `withLightEfficiencyMode { }` (suspend) | Applies light process mode for the block. |
| `keepAwake(mode = SYSTEM_AND_DISPLAY)` / `releaseAwake()` | One shared awake slot; the last mode wins. |
| `acquireAwake(mode = SYSTEM_AND_DISPLAY): AwakeHandle` | An independent request, released by `close()`. |
| `isAwakeActive(): Boolean` | Whether an awake request is held. |
| `keepScreenAwake()` / `releaseScreenAwake()` / `isScreenAwakeActive()` | Deprecated forwarders to `keepAwake`, `releaseAwake`, `isAwakeActive`. |

`enable`, `disable`, `keepAwake` and `releaseAwake` return an `EnergyManager.Result` with
`success`, `errorCode` and `message`. On an unsupported platform, `success` is `false` and
`errorCode` is `-1`. `AwakeHandle` has `mode`, `isActive` and `close()`.

## What's next

- [Scheduler](/docs/lifecycle/background/scheduler): deferred and periodic background work.
- [Taskbar progress](/docs/os/dock-taskbar/progress): show the progress of long work.
- [Auto-launch](/docs/lifecycle/background/launch-at-login): start the app at login.

# Filesystem watcher

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/fs-watcher

Watch files and directories from Kotlin and collect create, modify, remove, and move events as a coroutine Flow.

`fs-watcher` watches files and directories on macOS, Windows and Linux and delivers create,
modify, remove and move events as a coroutine `Flow`. Add
`dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.fs-watcher`; it exposes `kotlinx-coroutines-core`.

## Watch a directory

```kotlin
suspend fun watchDownloads() = coroutineScope {
    if (!FsWatchers.isSupported()) return@coroutineScope
    val watcher = FsWatchers.create()

    // Collect before registering so no early event is lost.
    launch {
        watcher.events.collect { event ->
            when (event) {
                is FsWatchEvent.Created -> println("created ${event.path}")
                is FsWatchEvent.Modified -> println("modified ${event.path}")
                is FsWatchEvent.Removed -> println("removed ${event.path}")
                is FsWatchEvent.Moved -> println("moved ${event.from} -> ${event.to}")
                is FsWatchEvent.Overflow -> println("events dropped, rescan needed")
                is FsWatchEvent.Other -> println("other ${event.paths}")
            }
        }
    }

    watcher.watch(Path.of(System.getProperty("user.home"), "Downloads"), recursive = true)
}
```

- `events` and `errors` are hot flows without replay: collect before you call `watch`.
- `watch` returns an `FsWatchRegistration`; close it to stop watching that path. Closing the
  `FsWatcher` closes every registration.
- On `Overflow`, events were dropped: re-list the tree instead of trusting the stream.
- Events come back under the path you registered, even when it goes through a symlink.

## Handle renames

In the default `Debounced` mode, a rename arrives as `FsWatchEvent.Moved(from, to)` when the OS
lets Nucleus pair both halves, and as `Removed(old)` then `Created(new)` otherwise.
`FsWatchDeliveryMode.Raw` never emits `Moved`.

On macOS, a rename used to arrive as a bare `Created` for the new path, and a delete of an older
file as `Modified`. `Debounced` delivery now reports `Moved`, or `Removed` + `Created`, and
`Removed` for deletes.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Each `FsWatcher` owns one native watcher (inotify, FSEvents, `ReadDirectoryChangesW`) shared by
  its registrations. It starts on the first `watch()` and stops after the last registration closes.
- Registering one directory under two spellings creates two independent registrations.
- On macOS, `Raw` mode delivers the FSEvents flags as they come, historical ones included.
- Polling runs in the same native library. Without it, `isSupported()` returns `false` and
  `create()` throws `FsWatchException` for every strategy.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `FsWatchers.create(config = FsWatcherConfig())` | Builds a watcher. Throws `FsWatchException` when no backend fits. |
| `FsWatchers.isSupported(config)` | Whether a backend is available for `config`. |
| `FsWatcher.events` / `errors` | Hot `Flow<FsWatchEvent>` / `Flow<FsWatchError>` across all registrations. |
| `FsWatcher.registrations` | `Set<FsWatchSource>` of the registered roots. |
| `FsWatcher.watch(path, recursive = true, name = null)` | Returns an `FsWatchRegistration` (`source`, `active`, `close()`). `name` tells registrations of the same root apart. |

`FsWatcherConfig` fields:

| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `followSymlinks` | `false` | Descend into symlinks inside a watched tree. |
| `backend` | `Auto` | `Auto` or `NativeOnly` (native, no polling fallback), or `Polling(interval = 2 s, compareContents = false)`. |
| `eventBufferCapacity` | `64` | Event buffer size. A full buffer emits `Overflow`. |
| `errorBufferCapacity` | `32` | Error buffer size. |
| `deliveryMode` | `Debounced(window = 150 ms)` | Merges bursts per path and pairs renames. `Raw` delivers every event as it comes. |

Every `FsWatchEvent` carries `source` and `needsRescan`. `Created`, `Modified` and `Removed` have
`path`, `Moved` has `from` and `to`, `Other` has `paths`; all but `Overflow` have `isDirectory: Boolean?`.
`FsWatchError` has `message`, `source` (`null` for watcher-wide errors), `recoverable` and `cause`.

## What's next

- [Scheduler](/docs/lifecycle/background/scheduler): background tasks that run even when the app is closed.
- [System info](/docs/os/system-info): platform and hardware state from the same runtime.
- [Executable type](/docs/lifecycle/executable-type): where a packaged app may write.

# Launch at login

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/lifecycle/background/launch-at-login

Enable, disable, and query launch at login from Kotlin with one API that picks the backend for the current packaging format.

The `autolaunch` module enables, disables, and queries launch at login with one API on Windows
(MSIX and Win32), macOS 13+, Linux and Flatpak. It respects choices the user made outside your app.

## Add the dependency

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.autolaunch:<version>")
}
```

For MSIX, set `appx { addAutoLaunchExtension = true }`. Without it, the API returns `UNSUPPORTED`.

## Check and toggle auto-launch

```kotlin
when (AutoLaunch.state()) {
    AutoLaunchState.ENABLED          -> {}
    AutoLaunchState.DISABLED         -> AutoLaunch.enable()
    AutoLaunchState.DISABLED_BY_USER -> AutoLaunch.openSystemSettings()
    AutoLaunchState.UNSUPPORTED      -> { /* macOS < 13, unsupported Linux setup */ }
    else -> {}
}
```

Do not retry on `BLOCKED_BY_USER`. After the user turns the app off in Task Manager or System
Settings, `enable()` returns `BLOCKED_BY_USER` until they turn it back on there. Send them to
`openSystemSettings()`.

## Detect a login launch

`wasStartedAtLogin(args)` reports whether login started the process, for example to start hidden.
`nucleusApplication` caches the answer at startup, so later calls can pass an empty array:

```kotlin
LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
    startedAtLogin = AutoLaunch.wasStartedAtLogin(emptyArray())
}
```

On macOS, a call made before `nucleusApplication` returns `false`. It returns `false` in dev runs.

## Notes

- On MSIX, Task Manager's Startup apps tab refreshes only after the next login. The stored state
  is already correct.
- The Linux unit starts after `graphical-session.target` and
  `gnome-session-x11-services-ready.target`. systemd ignores the second target outside GNOME.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

| Packaging | Backend | Login detection |
|---|---|---|
| MSIX | `StartupTask` | A `sihost.exe` ancestor |
| Win32 (MSI, NSIS) | `HKCU\...\CurrentVersion\Run` | `--nucleus-autostart` |
| macOS (13+) | `SMAppService.mainApp` | The login Apple Event |
| Linux (deb, rpm, AppImage) | systemd user service in `~/.config/systemd/user/` | `INVOCATION_ID` |
| Flatpak | Background portal | `--nucleus-autostart` |

- Win32 reads `StartupApproved\Run` to detect a user disable, and updates keep the state.
- `wasStartedAtLogin` caches positive results, so polling it is safe.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| `AutoLaunch` | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `state()` | `AutoLaunchState` | Current state. |
| `enable()` / `disable()` | `AutoLaunchResult` | Turns auto-launch on or off. |
| `openSystemSettings()` | `Boolean` | Opens Startup apps (Windows) or Login Items (macOS). |
| `wasStartedAtLogin(args)` | `Boolean` | Whether login started this process. |
| `isEnabled()` | `Boolean` | `ENABLED` or `ENABLED_BY_POLICY`. |
| `isUserLocked()` | `Boolean` | `DISABLED_BY_USER`. |
| `diagnostic()` | `String` | Backend trace for support tickets. |
| `preload()` | `Unit` | Call off the UI thread to avoid a first-call stall on macOS. |

- `AutoLaunchState`: `ENABLED`, `DISABLED`, `DISABLED_BY_USER`, `DISABLED_BY_POLICY`,
  `ENABLED_BY_POLICY` (read-only, MSIX Group Policy), `UNSUPPORTED`.
- `AutoLaunchResult`: `OK`, `UNCHANGED`, `BLOCKED_BY_USER`, `BLOCKED_BY_POLICY`, `UNSUPPORTED`, `ERROR`.

`AutoLaunchConfig`, set before the first `AutoLaunch` call:

| Property | Default | Affects |
|---|---|---|
| `taskId` | `NucleusApp.startupTaskId`, then `appId` | MSIX `<uap5:StartupTask TaskId>` |
| `executablePath` | The running executable | Win32 `Run` command |
| `autostartArgument` | `"--nucleus-autostart"` | Login marker; `null` omits it |
| `registryValueName` | `NucleusApp.appName`, then `appId` | Win32 `Run` value name |
| `backgroundReason` | `null` | Flatpak portal prompt |

## What's next

- [Service management](/docs/lifecycle/background/service-management): agents and daemons on macOS.
- [Application entry point](/docs/lifecycle/application): what `nucleusApplication` primes at startup.
- [Scheduler](/docs/lifecycle/background/scheduler): background work after a login launch.
