# Native HTTP

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/performance/native-http

Configure java.net.http.HttpClient, OkHttp or Ktor to trust the operating system certificate store through NativeTrustManager.

The native HTTP modules make an HTTP client trust the operating system certificate store through
[`NativeTrustManager`](/docs/performance/native-ssl). HTTPS calls to hosts signed by a corporate
root, an MDM profile or an SSL-inspection proxy then succeed.

## Add the dependency

Pick the adapter for your client. Each one brings `native-ssl` with it.

| Artifact | Client |
|----------|--------|
| `dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.native-http` | `java.net.http.HttpClient` |
| `dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.native-http-okhttp` | OkHttp 5 |
| `dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.native-http-ktor` | Ktor client 3, with the engine you declare |

## Use the JDK HttpClient

`NativeHttpClient.create()` returns an `HttpClient` that trusts the OS store and follows
redirects. To keep your own builder, call `withNativeSsl()` on it, before any `sslParameters(...)`
of your own:

```kotlin
import dev.nucleusframework.nativehttp.NativeHttpClient
import dev.nucleusframework.nativehttp.NativeHttpClient.withNativeSsl

val client = NativeHttpClient.create()

val custom = HttpClient.newBuilder()
    .withNativeSsl()
    .followRedirects(HttpClient.Redirect.NORMAL)
    .build()
```

`withNativeSsl()` does not turn on redirects. Without `followRedirects(...)`, a host that answers
302 returns the 302 response to your code.

## Use OkHttp

Use `NativeOkHttpClient.create()`, or call `withNativeSsl()` on your own `OkHttpClient.Builder`
(import `dev.nucleusframework.nativehttp.okhttp.NativeOkHttpClient.withNativeSsl`).

## Use Ktor

`native-http-ktor` ships no engine. Declare one of CIO, Java, OkHttp or Apache5:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.native-http-ktor:<version>")
    implementation("io.ktor:ktor-client-cio:<ktor-version>")
}
```

```kotlin
import dev.nucleusframework.nativehttp.ktor.installNativeSsl

val client = HttpClient(CIO) {
    installNativeSsl()
}
```

With any other engine, `installNativeSsl()` changes nothing.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Each adapter swaps only the trust material. Pooling, HTTP/2, interceptors and timeouts stay as
  you configure them.
- `withNativeSsl()` on the JDK builder sets `sslContext(NativeTrustManager.sslContext)` and
  replaces the `SSLParameters` with a set that does not request a client certificate.
- On OkHttp it calls `sslSocketFactory(NativeTrustManager.sslSocketFactory, NativeTrustManager.trustManager)`.
- `installNativeSsl()` sets `https { trustManager }` on CIO, `sslContext` on Java and Apache5,
  and `sslSocketFactory` on OkHttp.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| API | Returns |
|-----|---------|
| `NativeHttpClient.create()` | `HttpClient` with native trust and `Redirect.NORMAL` |
| `HttpClient.Builder.withNativeSsl()` | The builder, with native trust |
| `NativeOkHttpClient.create()` | `OkHttpClient` with native trust |
| `OkHttpClient.Builder.withNativeSsl()` | The builder, with native trust |
| `HttpClientConfig<T>.installNativeSsl()` | `Unit`; configures the Ktor engine |

## What's next

- [Native SSL](/docs/performance/native-ssl): how the module reads and merges the OS store.
- [Modules](/docs/concepts/modules): the full list of Nucleus modules.

---

# Native SSL

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/performance/native-ssl

Read the trusted certificates of the operating system and merge them with the JVM defaults into one X509TrustManager.

`native-ssl` reads the root certificates the operating system trusts on macOS, Windows and Linux,
merges them with the JVM defaults, and exposes the result as one `X509TrustManager`. HTTPS
handshakes to hosts signed by an enterprise root, an MDM profile or a TLS-inspection proxy then
succeed.

## Add the dependency

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.native-ssl:<version>")
}
```

For `java.net.http`, OkHttp or Ktor, add a [Native HTTP](/docs/performance/native-http) adapter
instead. It wires `native-ssl` into the client.

## Get a trust manager

Read the property your TLS stack expects:

```kotlin
import dev.nucleusframework.nativessl.NativeTrustManager

val trustManager: X509TrustManager = NativeTrustManager.trustManager
val sslContext: SSLContext = NativeTrustManager.sslContext
val sslSocketFactory: SSLSocketFactory = NativeTrustManager.sslSocketFactory
```

The first read builds the trust manager and caches it for the life of the process. Certificates
added to the OS store after that stay invisible until the app restarts. You cannot plug in a
custom certificate source.

## ProGuard

The default ProGuard rules of the Nucleus plugin cover this module. If you replace them with your
own, keep the two bridges:

```proguard
-keep class dev.nucleusframework.nativessl.mac.NativeSslBridge {
    native <methods>;
}
-keep class dev.nucleusframework.nativessl.windows.WindowsSslBridge {
    native <methods>;
}
```

## Logging

The module logs certificate counts and sources at `FINE` under the `dev.nucleusframework.nativessl`
logger. Set that logger to `FINE`, or set `allowNucleusRuntimeLogging = true`
(`dev.nucleusframework.core.runtime.tools`) from `main()`.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- The trust manager loads the JVM default issuers and the OS certificates into an in-memory
  `KeyStore`. When the OS reports none, `trustManager` is the JVM default.
- macOS and Windows read the store through the `nucleus_ssl` JNI library. If it fails to load,
  macOS contributes nothing, and Windows falls back to the `SunMSCAPI` keystores
  (`Windows-ROOT`, `Windows-CA`, `Windows-MY`).
- **macOS:** system anchors plus the user and admin trust-settings domains, filtered with the
  rules of [JetBrains jvm-native-trusted-roots](https://github.com/JetBrains/jvm-native-trusted-roots)
  (self-signed `TrustRoot` entries, SSL policy only, unknown constraints rejected).
- **Windows:** the `ROOT` and `CA` stores of `CURRENT_USER`, `LOCAL_MACHINE`, both Group Policy
  locations and `LOCAL_MACHINE_ENTERPRISE`, which covers Active Directory deployments that
  `SunMSCAPI` misses. `ROOT` entries are kept as is; `CA` entries must pass chain validation.
  Duplicates are removed by SHA-1 thumbprint.
- **Linux:** every readable PEM bundle or directory from the list Go's `crypto/x509` uses, such as
  `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` (Debian, Ubuntu), `/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt`
  (Fedora) and `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` (Alpine), deduplicated by DER content. No native library.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| `trustManager: X509TrustManager` | JVM default roots plus the OS roots |
| `sslContext: SSLContext` | A `TLS` context initialized with `trustManager` |
| `sslSocketFactory: SSLSocketFactory` | `sslContext.socketFactory` |

## What's next

- [Native HTTP](/docs/performance/native-http): wire the trust manager into `java.net.http`, OkHttp or Ktor.
- [Native library loader](/docs/performance/native-library-loader): how `nucleus_ssl` loads.
- [Modules](/docs/concepts/modules): the full list of Nucleus modules.

---

# Packaging overview

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging

Declare the installer formats your app ships in the Nucleus Gradle DSL and build each one the host operating system supports.

The Nucleus Gradle plugin builds desktop installers from one `nativeDistributions { }` block. The
packaging DSL comes with the plugin, so you add no dependency.

## Declare the formats

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
nucleus.application {
    mainClass = "com.example.MainKt"
    nativeDistributions {
        packageName = "MyApp"
        packageVersion = "1.0.0"
        targetFormats(TargetFormat.Dmg, TargetFormat.Nsis, TargetFormat.Deb, TargetFormat.AppImage)
    }
}
```

```shell
./gradlew packageDistributionForCurrentOS
```

The task builds every format the host supports and skips the rest, so one script runs on all three
OSes. Output lands in `build/compose/binaries/main/<format>/`. Each format also has its own task
(`packageDmg`, `packageNsis`), and `packageReleaseDistributionForCurrentOS` runs ProGuard first.

## Supported formats

| OS | Direct distribution | Store | Archives |
|----|---------------------|-------|----------|
| macOS | DMG, PKG (Developer ID) | PKG (Mac App Store) | ZIP, TAR, 7z |
| Windows | Exe, NSIS, NSIS Web, MSI, Portable | AppX (Microsoft Store) | ZIP, TAR, 7z |
| Linux | DEB, RPM, AppImage, Pacman | Snap, Flatpak | ZIP, TAR, 7z |

`TargetFormat.RawAppImage` builds the bare app image with no installer. Store formats use a
[sandboxed layout](/docs/packaging/sandboxing).

## Provision Node.js

The plugin downloads Node.js on first use and caches it in `~/.gradle/nucleus/nodejs`. You install
nothing, and CI no longer needs `actions/setup-node`.

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
nativeDistributions {
    nodejs {
        version = "22"        // default: a major line, "lts", or a pinned release such as "22.11.0"
        autoDownload = true   // false: use node and npm from PATH
    }
}
```

The `compose.electronBuilder.nodePath` Gradle property and the `NUCLEUS_NODE_HOME` environment
variable take precedence over the download. A floating version stays on the release it first
downloaded: delete its cache directory to update.

## Native libraries next to the app

The plugin places the JNI libraries of Nucleus modules next to the app, so the packaged app
extracts nothing at startup. For fat JARs and IDE runs, see
[Native library loader](/docs/performance/native-library-loader).

Packaged apps no longer carry Nucleus JNI libraries inside their JARs. Code that read them as
classpath resources must load them through `NativeLibraryLoader`. See
[Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

## Trim the runtime image

`stripJreFonts` defaults to `true`: the runtime image drops the JRE fonts, since Compose draws text
with its own. An app that draws text with AWT or Swing must set `stripJreFonts = false`. See
[Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

With `includeAllModules = true`, the plugin leaves out `jdk.jlink`, which JDKs built without
`jmods/` (such as Temurin 24+) refuse to link.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- jpackage builds the app image. electron-builder 26.16.1 wraps it in every format except
  `RawAppImage`.
- Node.js resolution order: `nodePath`, `NUCLEUS_NODE_HOME`, the `nodejs { }` download (checked
  against `SHASUMS256.txt`), then `node` on `PATH`.
- Packaged apps get `-Dnucleus.native.libraryPath=$APPDIR`. GraalVM images keep the libraries next
  to the executable.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's next

- [macOS](/docs/packaging/macos), [Windows](/docs/packaging/windows), [Linux](/docs/packaging/linux): per-OS settings.
- [Code signing](/docs/packaging/code-signing): sign and notarize each platform's builds.
- [Auto-update](/docs/packaging/auto-update): ship updates to installed apps.
- [CI/CD](/docs/packaging/ci-cd): build every format on GitHub Actions.

---

# Building for macOS

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/macos

Package a Nucleus app for macOS as a DMG, a Developer ID PKG, or a Mac App Store PKG, embed app extensions, and build a universal binary.

This page covers the `macOS { }` block: DMG and PKG builds, app extensions, and universal
binaries. You need a macOS host with Xcode Command Line Tools and an Apple Developer account.

## Configure the macOS block

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
nativeDistributions {
    targetFormats(TargetFormat.Dmg, TargetFormat.Zip, TargetFormat.Pkg)
    macOS {
        bundleID = "com.example.myapp"
        appCategory = "public.app-category.utilities"
        minimumSystemVersion = "12.0"
        iconFile.set(project.file("icons/app.icns"))
        layeredIconDir.set(project.file("icons/MyApp.icon")) // macOS 26, needs Xcode CLT 26+

        signing {
            sign.set(true)
            identity.set("Developer ID Application: My Company (TEAMID)")
        }
        notarization {
            appleID.set("dev@example.com")
            password.set(System.getenv("MAC_NOTARIZATION_PASSWORD"))
            teamID.set("TEAMID")
        }
    }
}
```

The plugin picks the certificate each format needs from that one identity. For other notarization
modes, see [Code signing](/docs/packaging/code-signing#choose-a-notarization-mode).

| Format | Certificates |
|--------|--------------|
| DMG, ZIP | Developer ID Application |
| Developer ID PKG | Developer ID Application, Developer ID Installer |
| Mac App Store PKG | 3rd Party Mac Developer Application and Installer, provisioning profiles |

## Package a DMG

`./gradlew packageDmg` builds the DMG. With `notarization { }` credentials, `notarizeDmg`
notarizes and staples it, and `packageDistributionForCurrentOS` runs that task for you.

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
macOS {
    dmg {
        window { x = 400; y = 100; width = 540; height = 380 }
        background.set(project.file("packaging/dmg-bg.png"))
        content(x = 130, y = 220, type = DmgContentType.File, name = "MyApp.app")
        content(x = 410, y = 220, type = DmgContentType.Link, path = "/Applications")
    }
}
```

`nativeDistributions.compressionLevel = CompressionLevel.Ultra` requires `minimumSystemVersion`
10.15+ and no pinned `dmg.format`. Ship a `Zip`
next to the DMG if you use [auto-update](/docs/packaging/auto-update).

## Choose a PKG channel

`macOS { pkg { appStore } }` selects the channel. The default, `true`, targets the Mac App Store.

| | `appStore = true` (default) | `appStore = false` |
|---|---|---|
| Distribution | Mac App Store (Transporter) | Direct download, MDM |
| Pipeline | [Sandboxed](/docs/packaging/sandboxing) | Same as DMG |
| Notarized | No, Apple reviews the upload | Yes, by `notarizePkg` |
| Install scripts | Fail the build | `preInstall`, `postInstall` |
| Auto-update | Store-managed | Self-updatable |

`macOS.appStore` and `TargetFormat.isStoreFormat` no longer compile. Set `macOS { pkg { appStore = … } }`
explicitly. The old `appStore` property was ignored, so review which channel each build should
use. See [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

### Package for the Mac App Store

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
macOS {
    entitlementsFile.set(project.file("packaging/sandbox-entitlements.plist"))
    runtimeEntitlementsFile.set(project.file("packaging/sandbox-runtime-entitlements.plist"))
    provisioningProfile.set(project.file("packaging/MyApp.provisionprofile"))
    runtimeProvisioningProfile.set(project.file("packaging/MyApp_Runtime.provisionprofile"))
}
```

Run `./gradlew packagePkg`. At runtime, `ExecutableRuntime.isSandboxed()` tells you whether the
App Sandbox applies. See [Sandboxing](/docs/packaging/sandboxing#detect-the-sandbox-at-runtime).

### Package a Developer ID PKG

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
macOS {
    pkg {
        appStore = false
        preInstall.set(file("packaging/macos/preinstall"))
        postInstall.set(file("packaging/macos/postinstall"))
    }
}
```

Run `./gradlew packagePkg notarizePkg`. The Installer runs both scripts as root, once per install.
Each needs a shebang and receives `$1` package path, `$2` install target, `$3` target volume, `$4`
startup disk.

## Embed app extensions

Nucleus copies and signs prebuilt `.appex` bundles, such as a Network Extension, into
`Contents/PlugIns/`. You build the `.appex` with Xcode or Kotlin/Native.

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
macOS {
    entitlementsFile.set(file("packaging/app.entitlements"))
    appExtensions {
        extension("NetworkFilter") {
            appex(file("build/appex/NetworkFilter.appex"))
            entitlements(file("packaging/extension/NetworkExtension.entitlements"))
            provisioningProfile(file("packaging/NetworkFilter.provisionprofile")) // optional
        }
    }
}
```

- Point `entitlementsFile` at a plist with `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit` only. A host that keeps
  the default `allow-unsigned-executable-memory` and `disable-library-validation` next to a network
  extension has been reported not to launch.
- `run` cannot load extensions. Use `runDistributable`.
- A network extension needs an Apple-issued profile granting
  `com.apple.developer.networking.networkextension`.
- Nucleus does not activate the extension. Call `NEFilterManager` or `NETunnelProviderManager`.

## Enable Liquid Glass on SDK 26

macOS 26 enables Liquid Glass only for apps built against SDK 26.0. The plugin marks the launcher
with any JDK, including in `run`. Set `macOS { macOsSdkVersion = null }` to opt out. GraalVM native
images need Xcode 26 selected on the build host instead.

## Build a universal binary

Build `arm64` and `x86_64` on separate runners, then merge them with the `build-macos-universal`
action. See [CI/CD](/docs/packaging/ci-cd#merge-the-universal-macos-binary).

## Customize Info.plist and launch agents

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
macOS {
    infoPlist {
        extraKeysRawXml = """<key>NSMicrophoneUsageDescription</key><string>Voice notes.</string>"""
    }
    launchAgents {
        agent("com.example.myapp.indexer") { bundleProgram("Contents/MacOS/indexer") }
    }
}
```

Register launch agents at runtime with [Service management](/docs/lifecycle/background/service-management).

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Liquid Glass: the plugin patches the launcher's `LC_BUILD_VERSION` with `vtool`. For `run`,
  `nucleusPatchMacJvm` keeps a patched `java` in `build/nucleus/patched-jvm/`.
- Extensions are signed inside-out, and the app is sealed without `--deep`. GraalVM builds sign
  them ad hoc unless `signing { }` is set.
- Developer ID PKGs are checked with `pkgutil --check-signature`. `build-macos-universal` runs
  `lipo` and re-signs.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## Reference

`bundleName` renames the `.app` in every artifact. `installationPath` applies to PKG and the DMG's
`/Applications` link. The full `macOS { }` block is in the [Gradle DSL reference](/docs/reference/gradle-dsl).

## What's next

- [Code signing](/docs/packaging/code-signing): certificates, notarization modes, and CI secrets.
- [Sandboxing](/docs/packaging/sandboxing): the pipeline behind App Store PKG builds.
- [Auto-update](/docs/packaging/auto-update): update DMG, ZIP, and Developer ID PKG installs.

---

# Building for Windows

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/windows

Package a Nucleus app for Windows as an NSIS, MSI, AppX, or Portable build, and see how the Windows renderer's ANGLE libraries ship.

This page covers the `windows { }` block: NSIS, MSI, AppX, and Portable builds. Windows formats
build only on a Windows host. To sign them, see [Code signing](/docs/packaging/code-signing#sign-on-windows).

## Configure the Windows build

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
nativeDistributions {
    targetFormats(TargetFormat.Nsis, TargetFormat.Msi, TargetFormat.AppX, TargetFormat.Portable)
    windows {
        iconFile.set(project.file("icons/app.ico"))
        upgradeUuid = "d24e3b8d-3e9b-4cc7-a5d8-5e2d1f0c9f1b"
        menuGroup = "My Company"
    }
}
```

| Format | Output |
|--------|--------|
| `Nsis`, `Exe` | The standard NSIS installer. |
| `NsisWeb` | A small NSIS stub that downloads the payload at install time. |
| `Msi` | A Windows Installer package for managed deployment. |
| `AppX` | An MSIX/AppX package for the Microsoft Store and sideloading. |
| `Portable` | A single executable that runs without installation. |

## Customize the NSIS installer

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
windows {
    nsis {
        oneClick = false
        perMachine = true
        allowToChangeInstallationDirectory = true
        createDesktopShortcut = true
        installerLanguages = listOf("en_US", "fr_FR")
        license.set(project.file("LICENSE"))
        deleteAppDataOnUninstall = true
    }
}
```

`nsis { }` maps to electron-builder's NSIS options. `script` and `includeScript` take your own
`.nsi` and `.nsh` files. `deleteAppDataOnUninstall` removes `%APPDATA%\<appId>`. With a custom
`includeScript`, delete that directory from your own `customUnInstall` macro instead.

## Build an MSI for enterprise deployment

Keep `upgradeUuid` fixed across releases. Windows matches successor versions by that UUID; without
it, each build installs as a separate product.

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
windows {
    msi {
        perMachine = false        // per-user install; default is true
        oneClick = false          // assisted wizard
        createDesktopShortcut = true
    }
}
```

`perMachine`, `oneClick`, `runAfterFinish`, and both shortcut flags default to `true`.
`windows.perUserInstall` is deprecated. `windows.menu` and `windows.shortcut` do not apply to MSI.
For custom dialogs or registry changes, use NSIS.

## Build an AppX or MSIX package

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
windows {
    appx {
        identityName = "MyCompany.MyApp"
        publisher = "CN=D541E802-6D30-446A-864E-2E8ABD2DAA5E"
        publisherDisplayName = "My Company"
        applicationId = "MyApp"
        square150x150Logo.set(project.file("packaging/appx/Square150x150Logo.png"))
        minVersion = "10.0.17763.0" // the Store requires more than 10.0.17134.0
    }
}
```

For a Store submission, `identityName`, `publisher`, and `publisherDisplayName` must match the
values Partner Center assigned to your reservation. `publisher` is the `CN=<GUID>` from Partner
Center, not your signing certificate's subject.

Building AppX locally needs Windows Developer Mode (Settings, System, For developers). The app runs
with `runFullTrust` and keeps Win32 access. The `build-windows-appxbundle` CI action merges amd64
and arm64 into one `.msixbundle`. AppX uses the [sandboxed pipeline](/docs/packaging/sandboxing).

## Enable Portable mode

`TargetFormat.Portable` builds one executable that needs no installer, admin rights, or registry
entries. It unpacks at each launch, so a lower compression level starts faster:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
windows {
    portable { compressionLevel = CompressionLevel.Normal }
}
```

## Add file associations and deep links

Associations and protocols declared on `nativeDistributions` reach every Windows format:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
nativeDistributions {
    protocol("MyApp", "myapp") // myapp:// deep links
    fileAssociation(mimeType = "application/x-myapp", extension = "myapp", description = "MyApp Document")
}
```

Use `windows.fileAssociation(...)` to set a Windows-specific icon.

## Ship the ANGLE libraries

Nucleus renders through ANGLE on Direct3D 11 on Windows. The DLLs come with the window module as
the transitive dependency `dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.angle-natives` (x64 and arm64), so you add
nothing. They ship [next to the app](/docs/packaging#native-libraries-next-to-the-app).

## Reference

The plugin generates `latest.yml` for NSIS, NSIS Web, MSI, and Portable; AppX updates come from the
Store. Nucleus sets the AppUserModelID at startup, so taskbar grouping and notifications work. The
full `windows { }` block is in the [Gradle DSL reference](/docs/reference/gradle-dsl).

## What's next

- [Code signing](/docs/packaging/code-signing#sign-on-windows): PFX and Azure Artifact Signing.
- [Auto-update](/docs/packaging/auto-update): update NSIS and MSI installs in place.
- [CI/CD](/docs/packaging/ci-cd): build, bundle, and sign Windows packages on GitHub Actions.

---

# Building for Linux

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/linux

Build DEB, RPM, AppImage, and Pacman packages for a Nucleus app, add maintainer scripts, and package for the Snap Store and Flathub.

This page covers the `linux { }` block: DEB, RPM, AppImage, Pacman, Snap, and Flatpak. Linux
formats build only on a Linux host with `rpm` and `fakeroot` (RPM), `libfuse2` (AppImage), and
`flatpak` plus `flatpak-builder` (Flatpak). The `setup-nucleus` CI action installs them.

## Configure the target formats

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
nativeDistributions {
    targetFormats(TargetFormat.Deb, TargetFormat.Rpm, TargetFormat.AppImage, TargetFormat.Pacman)
    homepage = "https://myapp.example.com" // required by DEB and RPM

    linux {
        iconFile.set(project.file("icons/app.png"))
        packageName = "myapp"
        appCategory = "Utility"
        debMaintainer = "Your Name <dev@example.com>"
        debDepends = listOf("libgtk-3-0", "libasound2")
        rpmRequires = listOf("gtk3", "alsa-lib")
        pacmanDepends = listOf("gtk3", "alsa-lib")
    }
}
```

Build with `packageDeb`, `packageRpm`, or `packagePacman`. The `StartupWMClass` of the `.desktop`
entry defaults to `mainClass` with dots replaced by hyphens; set `startupWMClass` if the window
manager reports another class. Bump `appRelease` to re-release the same `packageVersion`.

## Build an AppImage

An AppImage is one executable that runs on most distributions without installation. Build it with
`packageAppImage`.

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
linux {
    appImage {
        category = AppImageCategory.Utility
        genericName = "My Application"
        compressionLevel = CompressionLevel.Normal
    }
}
```

`Maximum` and `Ultra` compression slow every AppImage launch, so keep `Normal` for the AppImage
even when `nativeDistributions.compressionLevel` is higher. `Ultra` also recompresses the DEB.

## Add install and remove scripts

DEB, RPM, and Pacman run maintainer scripts as root. AppImage, Snap, and Flatpak do not.

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
linux {
    afterInstall.set(project.file("packaging/linux/after-install.sh"))
    afterRemove.set(project.file("packaging/linux/after-remove.sh"))
    beforeInstall.set(project.file("packaging/linux/before-install.sh"))
    beforeRemove.set(project.file("packaging/linux/before-remove.sh"))
    // Pacman only: an upgrade runs these instead of the install and remove scripts
    afterUpgrade.set(project.file("packaging/linux/after-upgrade.sh"))
    beforeUpgrade.set(project.file("packaging/linux/before-upgrade.sh"))
}
```

The payload lives under `/opt/<packageName>`, a path with no spaces. To ship a systemd unit, enable
it in `afterInstall`, stop it in `beforeInstall`, and disable it in `afterRemove`.

In `afterInstall` and `afterRemove`, `${executable}` and `${sanitizedProductName}` expand only
inside single quotes. A double-quoted `"${executable}"` stays literal and fails silently. The other
four scripts get no substitution: write names out in full.

```shell title="packaging/linux/after-install.sh"
systemctl enable '${executable}-daemon.service'
```

A Pacman upgrade runs only `beforeUpgrade` and `afterUpgrade`. Stop the service in the first and
restart it in the second, or the upgrade leaves it stopped. DEB and RPM ignore the upgrade
properties.

## Publish to the Snap Store

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
linux {
    snap {
        confinement = SnapConfinement.Strict
        base = "core22"
        plugs = listOf(SnapPlug.Desktop, SnapPlug.Home, SnapPlug.Wayland, SnapPlug.Network)
    }
}
```

Build with `packageSnap`; the host needs no `snapcraft`. Setting `plugs` replaces the default list.
Snap packaging skips arm64 hosts.

## Publish to Flathub with Flatpak

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
linux {
    flatpak {
        runtime = "org.freedesktop.Platform"
        runtimeVersion = "23.08"
        sdk = "org.freedesktop.Sdk"
        finishArgs = listOf("--share=ipc", "--socket=wayland", "--device=dri", "--share=network")
    }
}
```

Build with `packageFlatpak`. `finishArgs` declares the sandbox permissions and replaces the
defaults (`--share=ipc`, `--socket=x11`, `--socket=wayland`, `--socket=pulseaudio`,
`--device=dri`). Without `flatpak` on the host, the task skips the format.

## Register deep links and file associations

The plugin adds `protocol(...)` and `fileAssociation(...)` to the `.desktop` file's `MimeType=`:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
nativeDistributions {
    protocol("MyApp URL", "myapp")
    fileAssociation(mimeType = "application/x-myapp", extension = "myapp", description = "MyApp Document")
}
```

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- `afterInstall` and `afterRemove` are appended to Nucleus's template (desktop integration,
  AppArmor, polkit policy for passwordless updates). The other four go raw to fpm.
- `Ultra` rebuilds the DEB with `xz -9e`. RPM and Pacman already use xz.
- electron-builder builds the snap from its own template, which has no arm64 build.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's next

- [Code signing](/docs/packaging/code-signing#sign-on-linux): GPG-sign DEB and RPM packages.
- [Auto-update](/docs/packaging/auto-update#set-up-passwordless-updates-on-linux): passwordless DEB and RPM updates.
- [Gradle DSL reference](/docs/reference/gradle-dsl): every `linux { }` property.

# Code signing

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/code-signing

Sign and notarize macOS builds, sign Windows installers with a PFX certificate or Azure Artifact Signing, and GPG-sign DEB and RPM packages.

Each OS has a `signing { }` block in `nativeDistributions`. You need an Apple Developer account on
macOS, a `.pfx`/`.p12` certificate or an Azure Artifact Signing account on Windows, and a GPG key
on Linux.

## Sign and notarize on macOS

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
macOS {
    signing {
        sign.set(true)
        identity.set("Developer ID Application: My Company (TEAMID)")
        // keychain.set("/path/to/signing.keychain-db")
    }
    notarization {
        appleID.set("dev@example.com")
        password.set(System.getenv("MAC_NOTARIZATION_PASSWORD"))
        teamID.set("TEAMID")
    }
}
```

The plugin picks the certificate type per format from that one identity:

| Format | App signature | Installer signature | Notarized |
|--------|---------------|---------------------|-----------|
| DMG, ZIP | Developer ID Application | None | Yes |
| Developer ID PKG (`pkg { appStore = false }`) | Developer ID Application | Developer ID Installer | Yes |
| App Store PKG (default) | 3rd Party Mac Developer Application | 3rd Party Mac Developer Installer | No |

A Developer ID PKG build fails when the keychain lacks a Developer ID Installer certificate for the
same team.

### Choose a notarization mode

Configure one mode only; the build rejects a mix. Without credentials, the notarization tasks skip.

```kotlin
notarization {
    // 1. Apple ID with an app-specific password
    appleID.set("dev@example.com"); password.set(System.getenv("MAC_NOTARIZATION_PASSWORD")); teamID.set("TEAMID")
    // 2. notarytool keychain profile, stored with `xcrun notarytool store-credentials AC_PASSWORD`
    keychainProfile.set("AC_PASSWORD") // keychainPath optional
    // 3. App Store Connect API key, the usual choice in CI
    apiKey.set("/path/to/AuthKey_ABC123.p8"); apiKeyId.set("ABC123"); apiIssuer.set("12345678-90ab-cdef-1234-567890abcdef")
}
```

A universal build must re-sign after `lipo`. The `build-macos-universal` action does it; see
[CI/CD](/docs/packaging/ci-cd#merge-the-universal-macos-binary).

## Sign on Windows

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
windows {
    signing {
        enabled = true
        certificateFile.set(file(System.getenv("WIN_CSC_LINK") ?: "certs/certificate.pfx"))
        certificatePassword = System.getenv("WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD")
        algorithm = SigningAlgorithm.Sha256 // default; also Sha1, Sha512
        timestampServer = "http://timestamp.digicert.com"
    }
}
```

To use a certificate from the Windows store, set `certificateSha1` or `certificateSubjectName`
instead of `certificateFile`. For a cloud HSM, use Azure Artifact Signing:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
windows {
    signing {
        enabled = true
        publisherName = "My Publisher"
        azureTenantId = System.getenv("AZURE_TENANT_ID")
        azureEndpoint = "https://eastus.codesigning.azure.net"
        azureCertificateProfileName = "my-profile"
        azureCodeSigningAccountName = "my-account"
    }
}
```

Renew a PFX before it expires: SmartScreen flags a binary with an expired signature until you apply
a fresh, timestamped one.

## Sign on Linux

A GPG signature lets users who download your `.deb` or `.rpm` outside a repository verify its
origin. Signing stays off until `enabled` is `true` and `keyId` is set.

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
linux {
    signing {
        enabled.set(true)
        keyId.set("AB12CD34EF56")   // from gpg --list-secret-keys --keyid-format=long
        // passphrase.set(System.getenv("LINUX_GPG_PASSPHRASE"))
        debMethod = DebSignMethod.Detached // default
        silentUpdate.set(true)      // passwordless self-update
    }
}
```

The build reads the key from your keyring, or from `keyFile` in CI. Each package gets a
`.pub.asc` public key, and DEB also a detached `.deb.asc`; publish them next to the packages. Users
verify with `gpg --verify <pkg>.deb.asc <pkg>.deb` or `rpm -K <pkg>.rpm` after importing the key.

`debMethod` also accepts `DpkgSig` (needs `dpkg-sig` on the build host) and `Debsig` (clients
verify with `debsig-verify`). `Detached` needs only `gpg`. For `silentUpdate`, see
[passwordless updates](/docs/packaging/auto-update#set-up-passwordless-updates-on-linux).

## Configure all platforms in one block

`nativeDistributions.signing { }` writes to the same per-OS blocks, so you can mix both styles:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
nativeDistributions {
    signing {
        macOS   { sign.set(true); identity.set("Developer ID Application: My Company (TEAMID)") }
        windows { enabled = true; certificateFile.set(file("certs/certificate.pfx")) }
        linux   { enabled.set(true); keyId.set("AB12CD34EF56") }
    }
}
```

## Manage signing secrets in CI

Keep certificates and keys out of the repository. On macOS, the `setup-macos-signing` action
imports a base64 `.p12` into a temporary keychain; see [CI/CD](/docs/packaging/ci-cd#sign-macos-builds).
macOS and Linux settings also read Gradle properties, which you pass with `-P` or `gradle.properties`:

| Setting | Gradle property |
|---------|-----------------|
| `macOS.signing.*` | `compose.desktop.mac.sign`, `compose.desktop.mac.signing.{identity,keychain,prefix}` |
| `macOS.notarization.*` | `compose.desktop.mac.notarization.{appleID,password,teamID,keychainProfile,keychainPath,apiKey,apiKeyId,apiIssuer}` |
| `linux.signing.*` | `compose.desktop.linux.sign`, `compose.desktop.linux.signing.{keyId,keyFile,passphrase,silentUpdate}` |

For Linux, store `gpg --armor --export-secret-keys <keyId>` as a secret, then write it to a file:

```yaml title=".github/workflows/release.yaml"
- name: Configure Linux GPG signing
  if: runner.os == 'Linux'
  shell: bash
  env:
    LINUX_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.LINUX_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
    LINUX_GPG_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.LINUX_GPG_KEY_ID }}
  run: |
    [ -z "$LINUX_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY" ] && exit 0
    KEY_FILE="$RUNNER_TEMP/signing-key.asc"
    printf '%s' "$LINUX_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY" > "$KEY_FILE"
    {
      echo "compose.desktop.linux.sign=true"
      echo "compose.desktop.linux.signing.keyId=$LINUX_GPG_KEY_ID"
      echo "compose.desktop.linux.signing.keyFile=$KEY_FILE"
    } >> gradle.properties
```

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Every `codesign` call uses `--options runtime --timestamp`. The plugin signs inside-out: native
  libraries, executables, the runtime bundle, then the `.app`, without `--deep`.
- Non-sandboxed builds get `allow-jit`, `allow-unsigned-executable-memory`, and
  `disable-library-validation`. See [Sandboxing](/docs/packaging/sandboxing#configure-macos-entitlements)
  for the App Store set.
- The Developer ID PKG check runs `pkgutil --check-signature`. The plugin turns off
  electron-builder's notarization of App Store PKGs.
- `keyFile` is imported into a throwaway `GNUPGHOME`. RPM signatures live in the package header.
  Repository signing (`Release.gpg`, `InRelease`) is out of scope.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's next

- [CI/CD](/docs/packaging/ci-cd): sign builds on GitHub Actions.
- [Auto-update](/docs/packaging/auto-update): ship signed updates.
- [Gradle DSL reference](/docs/reference/gradle-dsl): every `signing { }` property.

# Trusted CA certificates

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/trusted-certificates

Import private root CA certificates into the Java runtime bundled with your packaged app so its HTTPS calls trust them.

`nativeDistributions.trustedCertificates` imports CA certificates into the Java runtime your app
ships with. Use it when your users sit behind a corporate proxy, a ZTNA gateway, or a filter that
terminates TLS with a private root CA. Without that CA, HTTPS calls fail with
`SSLHandshakeException`.

## Declare the certificates

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
nucleus.application {
    nativeDistributions {
        trustedCertificates.from(
            files(
                "certs/company-ca.pem",
                "certs/vpn-root.crt",
            ),
        )
    }
}
```

The plugin accepts PEM and DER files, and packaging imports them for you. Only the bundled runtime
changes: the user's system, the user's JDK and the build JDK stay untouched.

`trustedCertificates` covers CAs you know at build time. To also trust CAs the user installed in
the OS store, add [`native-ssl`](/docs/performance/native-ssl).

## API reference

| Symbol | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nativeDistributions.trustedCertificates` | `ConfigurableFileCollection` | PEM or DER files to import into the bundled runtime's `cacerts`. |
| `patchCaCertificates` | Gradle task | Imports the certificates into a copy of the runtime image. Exists only when `trustedCertificates` is non-empty. |

## What's next

- [native-ssl](/docs/performance/native-ssl): trust the OS certificate stores at runtime.
- [Auto-update](/docs/packaging/auto-update#configure-enterprise-networks): update through a TLS-intercepting proxy.
- [Gradle DSL reference](/docs/reference/gradle-dsl): the full `nucleus { }` DSL.

---

# Sandboxing

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/sandboxing

Build the Mac App Store PKG, AppX, and Flatpak through the sandboxed pipeline, and detect the sandbox at runtime.

Three formats run sandboxed: the Mac App Store PKG ([App Sandbox](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/app-sandbox)),
`AppX` (MSIX, full trust), and `Flatpak` ([Flatpak sandbox](https://docs.flatpak.org/en/latest/sandbox-permissions.html)).
Add them to `targetFormats` next to your regular formats, and Nucleus bundles their native
libraries ahead of time.

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
targetFormats(
    TargetFormat.Dmg, TargetFormat.Nsis, TargetFormat.Deb,
    TargetFormat.Pkg,     // with macOS { pkg { appStore = true } }, the default
    TargetFormat.AppX,
    TargetFormat.Flatpak,
)
```

A PKG with `macOS { pkg { appStore = false } }` is a Developer ID PKG and builds like a DMG. See
[Choose a PKG channel](/docs/packaging/macos#choose-a-pkg-channel).

A PKG no longer implies the App Sandbox. `TargetFormat.isStoreFormat` and `macOS.appStore` no
longer compile, and runtime code that gated sandbox behavior on `ExecutableRuntime.isPkg()` should
call `ExecutableRuntime.isSandboxed()`. See [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

## Keep a library's natives in its JAR

A library whose loader checks the extracted bytes (magic number, checksum) fails in the sandboxed
build. Exempt its JAR by a name substring:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
nativeDistributions {
    sandboxing {
        keepNativeLibsInJars("some-validating-lib")
    }
}
```

On the Mac App Store, that load can still fail library validation. Prefer a library option that
takes an external library path when one exists.

## Configure macOS entitlements

| Default entitlement | DMG, ZIP, Developer ID PKG | App Store PKG |
|---|---|---|
| `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit` | yes | yes |
| `com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory` | yes | yes |
| `com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation` | yes | yes |
| `com.apple.security.app-sandbox` | | yes |
| `com.apple.security.network.client` | | yes |
| `com.apple.security.files.user-selected.read-write` | | yes |

The runtime entitlements, applied to the bundled JVM binaries, drop network and file access. Override
either file, and add the two provisioning profiles the Mac App Store requires:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
macOS {
    entitlementsFile.set(project.file("packaging/entitlements.plist"))
    runtimeEntitlementsFile.set(project.file("packaging/runtime-entitlements.plist"))
    provisioningProfile.set(project.file("packaging/MyApp.provisionprofile"))
    runtimeProvisioningProfile.set(project.file("packaging/MyApp_Runtime.provisionprofile"))
}
```

## Configure the Flatpak sandbox

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
linux {
    flatpak {
        finishArgs = listOf(
            "--share=ipc", "--socket=wayland", "--socket=pulseaudio",
            "--device=dri", "--filesystem=home", "--share=network",
        )
    }
}
```

See [Building for Linux](/docs/packaging/linux#publish-to-flathub-with-flatpak) for the other
Flatpak options.

## Detect the sandbox at runtime

```kotlin
import dev.nucleusframework.core.runtime.ExecutableRuntime

if (!ExecutableRuntime.isSandboxed()) {
    // Register a launch agent, write outside the container, self-update, ...
}
```

`isSandboxed()` returns `true` inside the macOS App Sandbox, an AppX container, or a Flatpak. It
follows the sandbox, not the installer format: a Developer ID PKG reports `false`.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- The sandboxed pipeline extracts `.dylib`, `.jnilib`, `.so`, and `.dll` files from the dependency
  JARs into `Contents/Frameworks/` (macOS) or the app's resources directory, replaces them with
  markers, and rewrites `System.load(String)` and `Runtime.load(String)` to load the bundled copy.
- It sets `java.library.path`, `jna.library.path`, `jna.boot.library.path`, `jna.nounpack=true`
  and `jna.nosys=true`. The image lands in `app-sandboxed/` next to `app/`.
- AppX joins this pipeline only because MSIX forbids extracting DLLs at runtime.
- On macOS, `isSandboxed()` reads `APP_SANDBOX_CONTAINER_ID`.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's next

- [Building for macOS](/docs/packaging/macos): PKG channels, entitlements, and provisioning profiles.
- [Code signing](/docs/packaging/code-signing): certificates for each macOS channel.
- [Executable type](/docs/lifecycle/executable-type): detect how the app was installed.

# Auto-update

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/auto-update

Check for, download, verify, and install application updates from Kotlin with updater-runtime, without a third-party service.

`updater-runtime` checks for, downloads, verifies, and installs updates from Kotlin. The build
writes `latest-*.yml` metadata next to your installers, in electron-builder's format; you choose
where it lives in [Publishing](/docs/packaging/publishing).

## Add the dependency

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.updater-runtime:<version>")
}
```

## Check and install an update

```kotlin
val updater = NucleusUpdater {
    provider = GitHubProvider(owner = "myorg", repo = "myapp")
}

when (val result = updater.checkForUpdates()) {
    is UpdateResult.Available -> {
        var installer: File? = null
        updater.downloadUpdate(result.info).collect { progress ->
            println("${progress.percent.toInt()}%")
            progress.file?.let { installer = it }
        }
        // Launches the installer, exits, and relaunches the app
        installer?.let(updater::installAndRestart)
    }
    UpdateResult.NotAvailable -> println("Up to date")
    is UpdateResult.Error -> println("Error: ${result.exception.message}")
}
```

`checkForUpdates()` suspends. In a dev run (`currentVersion` is `0.0.0-dev`) it returns
`NotAvailable`. The tag picks the channel: `v1.0.0` is `latest`, `v1.0.0-beta.1` is `beta`,
`v1.0.0-alpha.1` is `alpha`. A `beta` user sees `latest` and `beta`; an `alpha` user sees all three.

## Supported formats

| Platform | Self-updatable | Store-managed (`NotAvailable`) |
|----------|----------------|---------------|
| macOS | DMG, ZIP, Developer ID PKG | App Store PKG |
| Windows | NSIS, NSIS Web, Exe, MSI | AppX/MSIX |
| Linux | DEB, RPM, AppImage | Snap, Flatpak |

The updater replaces the `.app` from the release's ZIP, and falls back to the DMG. Add
`TargetFormat.Zip` next to `TargetFormat.Dmg` or `TargetFormat.Pkg` so `latest-mac.yml` lists it.

## Differential downloads

`downloadUpdate` fetches only the changed blocks, and falls back to a full download when it cannot.
An AppImage is differential from its first update; other formats from the second.
`progress.isDifferential` tells you which kind ran, and `totalBytes` counts bytes transferred. Turn
it off when your CDN does not serve range requests:

```kotlin
val updater = NucleusUpdater {
    provider = GitHubProvider(owner = "myorg", repo = "myapp")
    differentialDownload = false
}
```

## Post-update detection

After `installAndRestart` or `installAndQuit`, the next launch sees `wasJustUpdated()` return
`true`, and `consumeUpdateEvent()` returns an `UpdateEvent(previousVersion, newVersion, updateLevel)`
for a "What's new" screen.

## Configure enterprise networks

Behind a proxy with a private root CA, the JDK `HttpClient` fails the TLS handshake. Add
`dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.native-http` and pass a `NativeHttpClient`, which trusts the OS
certificate store:

```kotlin
val updater = NucleusUpdater {
    provider = GitHubProvider(owner = "myorg", repo = "myapp")
    httpClient = NativeHttpClient.create()
}
```

See also [Trusted CA certificates](/docs/packaging/trusted-certificates).

## Set up passwordless updates on Linux

A DEB or RPM update runs through `pkexec`, which asks for a password. With
[signed packages](/docs/packaging/code-signing#sign-on-linux), the app skips the prompt:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
linux {
    signing {
        enabled.set(true)
        keyId.set("AB12CD34EF56")
        silentUpdate.set(true) // requires enabled = true
    }
}
```

It needs an active local session. When the helper or the `.asc` signature is missing, the runtime
logs why and falls back to the password prompt.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Differential downloads compare electron-builder block maps with the previous artifact cached in
  `cacheDir` and fetch changed blocks with HTTP range requests. A missing map, a failed range
  request, or a digest mismatch falls back to a full download.
- The updater checks the SHA-512 after download. On Windows it runs NSIS with `/S` and MSI with
  `msiexec /passive` after the app exits.
- Silent Linux updates go through a root-owned `/opt/<App>/nucleus-update-helper` that verifies the
  detached `.asc` against your bundled public key before it runs `dpkg -i` or `rpm -U`.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## API reference

### Runtime methods

- `suspend fun checkForUpdates(): UpdateResult`
- `fun downloadUpdate(info: UpdateInfo): Flow<DownloadProgress>`: the last emission has `file != null`.
- `fun installAndRestart(installerFile: File)`: runs the installer, exits, and relaunches.
- `fun installAndQuit(installerFile: File)`: installs silently and exits without relaunching.
- `fun isUpdateSupported(): Boolean`: whether the current install can update itself.
- `fun wasJustUpdated(): Boolean`, `fun consumeUpdateEvent(): UpdateEvent?`
- `val currentVersion: String`

### Result and level types

- `UpdateResult.Available(info: UpdateInfo, level: UpdateLevel)`, `UpdateResult.NotAvailable`,
  `UpdateResult.Error(exception: UpdateException)`
- `UpdateLevel`: `MAJOR`, `MINOR`, `PATCH`, or `PRE_RELEASE`. Use it to force a dialog for a major
  version and install patches in the background.
- `UpdateException` subtypes: `NetworkException`, `ChecksumException`, `NoMatchingFileException`,
  `ParseException`.

### Builder fields

| Field | Default | Notes |
|-------|---------|-------|
| `currentVersion` | Detected from the packaged app | Compared with the remote version |
| `provider` | Required | `GitHubProvider` or `GenericProvider` |
| `channel` | `"latest"` | Release channel name |
| `allowDowngrade` | `false` | |
| `allowPrerelease` | `false` | Treated as `true` when `currentVersion` contains `-` |
| `executableType` | Detected | Forces the artifact type to download |
| `httpClient` | JDK client following redirects | `NativeHttpClient` for private CAs |
| `differentialDownload` | `true` | |
| `cacheDir` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%/nucleus/updates/<appId>` on Windows, `~/.cache/nucleus/updates/<appId>` elsewhere | Previous artifact and block map |

### Providers

- `GitHubProvider(owner, repo, token = null)`. The token travels in the `Authorization` header.
- `GenericProvider(baseUrl)`. `baseUrl` must use `https`, or construction throws
  `IllegalArgumentException`. Plain `http` works for loopback hosts only, for local tests.

## What's next

- [Publishing](/docs/packaging/publishing): configure where the metadata lives.
- [CI/CD](/docs/packaging/ci-cd#publish-the-release): generate and upload metadata in the release workflow.
- [Code signing](/docs/packaging/code-signing#sign-on-linux): GPG keys for passwordless Linux updates.

# Publishing

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/publishing

Configure where Nucleus publishes installers and auto-update metadata (GitHub Releases, S3, or a generic HTTPS host) and submit store builds.

`publish { }` inside `nativeDistributions { }` tells Nucleus where your installers and their
[auto-update](/docs/packaging/auto-update) metadata live. Enable one backend.

## Configure a publishing backend

**GitHub Releases**

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
publish {
    github {
        enabled = true
        owner = "myorg"
        repo = "myapp"
        token = System.getenv("GITHUB_TOKEN") // needs contents: write
        channel = ReleaseChannel.Latest
        releaseType = ReleaseType.Release // or Draft, Prerelease
    }
}
```

**S3**

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
publish {
    s3 {
        enabled = true
        bucket = "my-updates-bucket"
        region = "us-east-1"
        path = "releases/myapp"
        acl = "public-read"
    }
}
```

Provide `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, and `AWS_REGION` in the environment.

**Generic HTTPS**

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
publish {
    generic {
        enabled = true
        url = "https://updates.example.com/releases/"
        channel = ReleaseChannel.Latest
        useMultipleRangeRequest = true // default
    }
}
```

You upload the files to any static host. It must serve HTTP `Range` requests over `https`.

`channel` selects the YAML the updater reads: `Latest` (`latest-*.yml`, tag `v1.0.0`), `Beta`
(`beta-*.yml`, `v1.0.0-beta.1`), or `Alpha` (`alpha-*.yml`, `v1.0.0-alpha.1`).

## Set the publish mode

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
publish {
    publishMode = PublishMode.Auto
}
```

| Mode | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| `PublishMode.Never` (default) | No upload. The plugin still writes `latest-*.yml` for every updatable format. |
| `PublishMode.Auto` | Upload when the build runs from a git tag. |
| `PublishMode.Always` | Upload on every build. |

The `compose.electronBuilder.publishMode` Gradle property overrides the DSL value for one run. The
reference [CI/CD workflow](/docs/packaging/ci-cd#publish-the-release) keeps `Never` and uploads in
a separate job.

## Submit to a desktop store

Store builds skip `publish { }`. Upload the store format through the vendor:

- **Mac App Store**: the App Store PKG, with Transporter or `xcrun altool`. See
  [Package for the Mac App Store](/docs/packaging/macos#package-for-the-mac-app-store).
- **Microsoft Store**: the `.msixbundle`, in [Partner Center](https://partner.microsoft.com/).
  `identityName`, `publisher` (`CN=<GUID>`), and `publisherDisplayName` must match the reservation.
  See [Build an AppX or MSIX package](/docs/packaging/windows#build-an-appx-or-msix-package).
- **Snap Store**: `snapcraft upload` from CI. `classic` confinement needs Snap Store approval.
- **Flathub**: a manifest pull request on the [Flathub repository](https://github.com/flathub/flathub).

## What's next

- [Auto-update](/docs/packaging/auto-update): how the app reads the published YAML.
- [CI/CD](/docs/packaging/ci-cd): the workflow that builds, signs, and uploads.
- [Gradle DSL reference](/docs/reference/gradle-dsl): the full DSL.

---

# CI/CD

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/packaging/ci-cd

Build, sign, and publish a Nucleus desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux on GitHub Actions with the composite actions in the Nucleus repository.

In this tutorial, you'll set up a GitHub Actions pipeline that builds, signs, and publishes your
installers. The [`NucleusFramework/Nucleus`](https://github.com/NucleusFramework/Nucleus)
repository ships the composite actions: reference them as
`NucleusFramework/Nucleus/.github/actions/<name>@<ref>`, with `<ref>` pinned to a release tag in
production. Installers do not cross-compile, so you need one runner per OS and architecture.

## Build on every platform

```yaml title=".github/workflows/release.yaml"
name: Release
on:
  push:
    tags: ['v*']

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { os: ubuntu-22.04,     arch: amd64 }
          - { os: ubuntu-22.04-arm, arch: arm64 }
          - { os: windows-latest,   arch: amd64 }
          - { os: windows-11-arm,   arch: arm64 }
          - { os: macos-latest,     arch: arm64 }
          - { os: macos-15-intel,   arch: amd64 }
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: NucleusFramework/Nucleus/.github/actions/setup-nucleus@main
        with:
          java-version: '25'
          flatpak: 'true'
          snap: 'true'
      - run: ./gradlew packageReleaseDistributionForCurrentOS --stacktrace --no-daemon
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: release-assets-${{ runner.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          path: build/compose/binaries/**/*
```

Later jobs find the artifacts by their `release-assets-<os>-<arch>` names, so keep that scheme.
`setup-nucleus` installs a JDK, the Linux packaging tools, and Gradle:

| Input | Default | Purpose |
|-------|---------|---------|
| `java-version` | `25` | JDK that runs Gradle and that jpackage bundles. |
| `packaging-tools` | `true` | Install the Linux packaging tools. |
| `flatpak` / `snap` | `false` | Install Flatpak (Freedesktop 24.08) or Snapcraft. |
| `graalvm` | `false` | Prepare a native-image build: Xcode 26 on macOS, MSVC on Windows. |
| `graalvm-version` | `25i4` | Keep it equal to `graalvm { toolchain { version } }`. |
| `node-version` | `22` | Keep it equal to `nodejs { version }`. |

`setup-nucleus` no longer runs `actions/setup-node`, and the `setup-node` input is gone. Remove
`actions/setup-node` from your jobs and cache `~/.gradle/nucleus/nodejs` instead. See
[Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

## Sign macOS builds

```yaml
- uses: NucleusFramework/Nucleus/.github/actions/setup-macos-signing@main
  id: signing
  with:
    certificate-base64: ${{ secrets.MAC_CERTIFICATES_P12 }}
    certificate-password: ${{ secrets.MAC_CERTIFICATES_PASSWORD }}
```

| Secret | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `MAC_CERTIFICATES_P12`, `MAC_CERTIFICATES_PASSWORD` | Base64 `.p12` bundle and its password. |
| `MAC_DEVELOPER_ID_APPLICATION` | Developer ID Application identity (DMG, ZIP). |
| `MAC_APP_STORE_APPLICATION`, `MAC_APP_STORE_INSTALLER` | 3rd Party Mac Developer identities (App Store PKG). |
| `MAC_PROVISIONING_PROFILE`, `MAC_RUNTIME_PROVISIONING_PROFILE` | Base64 profiles for the app and the JVM runtime. |
| `MAC_NOTARIZATION_APPLE_ID`, `MAC_NOTARIZATION_PASSWORD`, `MAC_NOTARIZATION_TEAM_ID` | `notarytool` credentials. |

Without the `MAC_*` secrets, the pipeline signs ad hoc. See
[Code signing](/docs/packaging/code-signing#manage-signing-secrets-in-ci).

## Merge the universal macOS binary

`build-macos-universal` merges the arm64 and x64 builds and repackages a signed universal ZIP, DMG,
and PKG. Check out the Nucleus repository first, at the ref that matches your plugin version:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    repository: NucleusFramework/Nucleus
    ref: main
    path: nucleus
    sparse-checkout: plugin-build/plugin/src/main/resources/nucleus/electron-builder
- uses: NucleusFramework/Nucleus/.github/actions/build-macos-universal@main
  with:
    arm64-path: artifacts/release-assets-macOS-arm64
    x64-path: artifacts/release-assets-macOS-amd64
    output-path: artifacts/release-assets-macOS-universal
    signing-identity: ${{ secrets.MAC_DEVELOPER_ID_APPLICATION }}
    app-store-identity: ${{ secrets.MAC_APP_STORE_APPLICATION }}
    installer-identity: ${{ secrets.MAC_APP_STORE_INSTALLER }}
    keychain-path: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.keychain-path }}
    electron-builder-toolchain-dir: nucleus/plugin-build/plugin/src/main/resources/nucleus/electron-builder
```

Notarize with `xcrun notarytool submit --wait`. Staple the DMG and leave the ZIP unstapled, so the
[updater](/docs/packaging/auto-update)'s block map stays valid. On private repositories, macOS
minutes count ten times against your quota; a self-hosted macOS runner avoids that cost.

## Bundle Windows for the Microsoft Store

```yaml
- uses: NucleusFramework/Nucleus/.github/actions/build-windows-appxbundle@main
  with:
    amd64-path: artifacts/release-assets-Windows-amd64
    arm64-path: artifacts/release-assets-Windows-arm64
    output-path: artifacts/release-assets-Windows-bundle
```

## Publish the release

`generate-update-yml` writes `<channel>-mac.yml`, `<channel>.yml`, and `<channel>-linux.yml`.
`publish-release` creates the GitHub Release and uploads everything:

```yaml
- uses: NucleusFramework/Nucleus/.github/actions/generate-update-yml@main
  with:
    artifacts-path: artifacts
    version: ${{ env.VERSION }}
    channel: ${{ env.CHANNEL }} # latest, beta, or alpha
- uses: NucleusFramework/Nucleus/.github/actions/publish-release@main
  with:
    artifacts-path: artifacts
    tag: ${{ env.TAG }}
    release-type: ${{ env.RELEASE_TYPE }} # release, draft, or prerelease
```

The reference [`release-desktop.yaml`](https://github.com/NucleusFramework/Nucleus/blob/main/.github/workflows/release-desktop.yaml)
wires all these jobs together. It derives the version and channel from the tag with
`release-tag-info`, and `validate-release-ref` rejects an `-alpha`, `-beta`, or `-rc` tag that does
not point to a commit on a `nucleus-*` release branch.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- `setup-nucleus` installs Microsoft Build of OpenJDK on Windows and Temurin elsewhere. On Linux it
  installs `rpm`, `fakeroot`, `libarchive-tools`, `patchelf`, the GTK, GLib, D-Bus and X11
  headers, and starts a virtual display with `xvfb`.
- The Nucleus plugin downloads Node.js and the GraalVM JDK itself; `setup-nucleus` only caches
  `~/.gradle/nucleus/nodejs` and `~/.gradle/nucleus/graalvm`.
- `build-macos-universal` runs `lipo` on every Mach-O file, re-signs inside-out, and runs
  electron-builder outside Gradle, installed with `npm ci` from `electron-builder-toolchain-dir`.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's next

- [Code signing](/docs/packaging/code-signing): produce and store the signing secrets.
- [Publishing](/docs/packaging/publishing): the `publish { }` DSL.
- [Auto-update](/docs/packaging/auto-update): how the app reads the generated YAML.

# Compare

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/compare

How Nucleus compares with vanilla Compose Multiplatform, with other JVM packaging tools, and with Electron and Tauri.

This page sets Nucleus against Electron and Tauri. For the Kotlin and JVM alternatives, see
[Nucleus and vanilla Compose Multiplatform](/docs/compare/cmp-default) and
[Packaging compared](/docs/compare/packaging).

## Electron and Tauri

| | **Nucleus** | Electron | Tauri |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Languages | Kotlin | JavaScript and Node (C++ for native modules) | JavaScript and Rust |
| UI | Compose, Skia on the GPU | Chromium | OS WebView |
| OS APIs | Kotlin modules, one process | Node native modules, IPC | Rust commands over IPC |
| Shared with mobile | The same Kotlin as Android and iOS | Web bundle | Web bundle |
| Packaging formats | 18 | 5 to 7 through electron-builder | 5 through tauri-bundler |
| Cold start | ~0.2 s (GraalVM) | 2 to 3 s | under 1 s |
| Idle RAM | 30 to 120 MB | 200 to 500 MB | ~87 MB |

Pick Electron when shipping speed and a JavaScript hiring pool outweigh memory use. Pick Tauri
when you accept platform WebViews and a Rust and JavaScript split for small binaries. Pick Nucleus
when your team writes Kotlin and wants Compose from the UI down to the installer.

### Measured startup, RAM, and process count

A Hello World window in each stack, timed from process launch to the first window.

| Windows 11 | Stack | Cold start | Warm start | RAM (private WS) | Processes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Nucleus** | GraalVM native image | ~0.17 s | ~0.10 s | **~30 MB** | 1 |
| WinUI 3 | .NET 9 and Windows App SDK | ~0.20 s | ~0.28 s | ~32 MB | 1 |
| Flutter | Dart AOT and Skia | ~0.28 s | ~0.28 s | ~33 MB | 1 |
| Tauri | Rust and WebView2 | ~0.74 s | ~0.12 s | ~87 MB | 7 |

| macOS 26 (Apple silicon) | Stack | Cold start | Warm start | RAM (RSS, all processes) | Processes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Nucleus** | GraalVM native image | ~0.32 s | ~0.20 s | ~115 MB | 1 |
| SwiftUI | native reference | ~0.14 s | ~0.14 s | ~78 MB | 1 |
| Flutter | Dart AOT and Skia | ~0.79 s | ~0.17 s | ~100 MB | 1 |
| Tauri | Rust and WKWebView | ~0.91 s | ~0.19 s | ~173 MB | 4 |

The macOS RAM column counts shared framework pages, so compare rows within one table only. Cold
start and RAM grow with what your app loads. Electron figures come from public benchmarks; the
others were measured first-hand. See [Performance](/docs/performance).

## What's next

- [Nucleus and vanilla Compose Multiplatform](/docs/compare/cmp-default): what Nucleus adds to CMP.
- [Packaging compared](/docs/compare/packaging): Nucleus against the JVM packaging tools.
- [Benchmarks](/docs/performance/benchmarks): CPU, rendering and list-load results across stacks.
- [Migrate from JetBrains Compose Desktop](/docs/migrate/from-jb-compose): the steps.

# Nucleus and vanilla Compose Multiplatform

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/compare/cmp-default

What Nucleus adds to JetBrains Compose Desktop and what it changes, as a decision guide for Kotlin teams shipping desktop apps.

Nucleus extends the `org.jetbrains.compose` plugin. The Compose UI runtime, Skia rendering, Compose
Hot Reload, `compose.desktop.currentOs` and the Gradle tasks stay the same, and
`compose.desktop.application { }` becomes `nucleus.application { }`.

## What Nucleus replaces

Nucleus opens native windows and never creates an AWT window. Your composables run unchanged, but
the entry point, windows, dialogs, tray and `SwingPanel` change, and native callbacks run on the
host UI thread instead of the AWT event dispatch thread. The migration guide
[maps each AWT API](/docs/migrate/from-jb-compose#replace-the-entry-point-and-windows) to its
replacement.

## What Nucleus adds

| Area | Vanilla CMP | Nucleus |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Formats | DMG, PKG, MSI, EXE, DEB, RPM, raw app image | Those, plus NSIS, NSIS Web, AppX, Portable, AppImage, Pacman, Snap, Flatpak, ZIP, TAR, 7Z: 18 in total |
| Stores | | Mac App Store PKG, AppX and Flatpak through a [sandboxed pipeline](/docs/packaging/sandboxing), plus a Developer ID PKG |
| Auto-update | None | Differential updates from electron-builder `latest-*.yml` metadata. See [Auto-update](/docs/packaging/auto-update) |
| Runtime | JVM | [GraalVM native image](/docs/performance/graalvm), or JVM with the JDK 25+ [AOT cache](/docs/performance/aot-cache) (`enableAotCache = true`) |
| Code signing | | Windows PFX or Azure Artifact Signing, and universal macOS binaries through the `build-macos-universal` action |
| Deep links and file types | Per-OS configuration | `protocol(…)` and `fileAssociation(…)` reach NSIS, MSI, AppX, DEB, RPM and the macOS `Info.plist` |
| Installer options | | `splashImage`, `artifactName` template, `compressionLevel` |
| Runtime libraries | | `nucleusApplication` (single instance, deep links, GraalVM setup), decorated windows with macOS, Fluent, Yaru, Jewel and Material toolkits, and OS modules such as notifications, hotkeys, media controls and spell check |

DEB builds need `homepage`, where vanilla CMP did not:
[set it during the migration](/docs/migrate/from-jb-compose#move-the-build-to-the-nucleus-dsl).

Hello World on Windows 11:

| | Nucleus, GraalVM | Nucleus, JVM with AOT cache | Vanilla CMP |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cold start | ~0.2 s | ~1.0 s | 1 to 2 s |
| Installer size | ~40 MB | ~60 MB | 80 to 120 MB |

## Stay on vanilla CMP when

- DMG, MSI and DEB from jpackage cover your distribution.
- You don't need auto-update, GraalVM, store distribution, or native decorations.
- Your UI relies on `SwingPanel`, Swing components, or a library that needs an AWT window.
- Your pipeline already has signing and upload scripts you want to keep.

## Move to Nucleus when

- You ship to the Mac App Store, Microsoft Store, Snapcraft, or Flathub.
- You want auto-update or a GraalVM native image.
- You want native decorations, trackpad gestures, pen input, and native Wayland.
- You want OS integration modules without building them yourself.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Vanilla Compose Desktop draws into a `ComposeWindow`, which is a `JFrame`.
- The plugin builds the app image with jpackage, then hands it to electron-builder's
  `--prepackaged` mode for the other formats. It downloads the Node.js electron-builder needs.
- The store pipeline signs each native library, adds sandbox-aware JVM arguments, and applies the
  entitlements.
- The native build uses about 30 MB of RAM. Installer sizes come from NSIS at maximum compression.
- `core-runtime` provides `NucleusApp`, `ExecutableRuntime`, and the deep-link and single-instance
  primitives.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's next

- [Migrate from JetBrains Compose Desktop](/docs/migrate/from-jb-compose): the steps.
- [Windows](/docs/windows): `nucleusApplication` and `DecoratedWindow`.
- [Sandboxing](/docs/packaging/sandboxing): the store pipeline.
- [Auto-update](/docs/packaging/auto-update): update metadata and the Kotlin client.

# Packaging compared

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/compare/packaging

How Nucleus packaging compares with jpackage, Compose Multiplatform, Conveyor, install4j, jDeploy and JavaPackager on formats, auto-update, signing, CI, and stores.

Nucleus builds 18 formats and adds auto-update, signing, sandboxing, CI actions, and GraalVM
native images in one Gradle plugin under Apache 2 and MIT licenses. This page compares it with
jpackage, Compose Multiplatform, Conveyor, install4j, jDeploy, and JavaPackager.

## Format coverage

| Tool | DMG | PKG | NSIS | MSI | MSIX/AppX | Portable | DEB | RPM | AppImage | Snap | Flatpak | Archives | Total |
| --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **Nucleus** | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | ZIP, TAR, 7Z | **18** |
| Conveyor | | | | | Y | | Y | | | | | ZIP, TAR, custom EXE | 6 |
| install4j | Y | | | Y | | | Y | Y | | | | TAR, shell | 7 |
| jpackage | Y | Y | | Y | | | Y | Y | | | | | 6 |
| jDeploy | | | | | | | Y | | | | | EXE, TAR | 4 |
| Compose MP | Y | Y | | Y | | | Y | Y | | | | | 6 |
| JavaPackager | Y | Y | | Y | | | Y | Y | Y | | | ZIP | 8 |

The Nucleus total also counts `Exe`, `Pacman`, `NsisWeb`, and `RawAppImage`, which have no column.

## Auto-update

| Tool | Runtime library | Channels | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Nucleus** | `NucleusUpdater` | 3 (latest, beta, alpha) | SHA-512 |
| Conveyor | OS-native (Sparkle 2, MSIX, apt) | Yes | Yes |
| install4j | Updater API | Yes | Yes |
| jDeploy | Built in | No | No |
| jpackage, Compose MP | None | | |

Nucleus and Conveyor both ship delta updates. Nucleus downloads only the changed blocks from any
earlier version, and exposes progress, channel switching, post-update detection, and
restart-on-update.

## Signing, CI, and stores

| Tool | Windows signing | CI | Stores |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Nucleus** | `.pfx`, Azure Artifact Signing | Six GitHub Actions | Mac App Store, Microsoft Store, Snap Store, Flathub |
| Conveyor | Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS, SSL.com eSigner, DigiCert ONE, Google Cloud KMS, SafeNet or YubiKey HSMs | Examples, single-machine builds | Store-acceptable artifacts |
| install4j | `.pfx` | A CLI | |
| jpackage | None | None | |
| Compose MP | | None | Store-acceptable artifacts |

Every tool compared here signs and notarizes macOS builds. Nucleus also packages GraalVM native
images end to end as DMG, NSIS and DEB. See [GraalVM](/docs/performance/graalvm).

## Pick a tool

- A small CLI or single-window app that needs HSM signing and single-machine builds: **Conveyor**.
- An enterprise installer with custom dialogs and paid support: **install4j**.
- A DMG, MSI or DEB straight from jpackage: **Compose Multiplatform** or **jpackage**.
- One Kotlin codebase for every format and store, with auto-update, AOT and GraalVM: **Nucleus**.

Nucleus builds each OS on its own CI runner, with no cross-compilation. It is Gradle-only, and
younger than Conveyor and install4j.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- Nucleus builds the app image with jpackage, then runs electron-builder's `--prepackaged` mode on
  it for every installer. The plugin downloads the Node.js electron-builder needs.
- Delta updates match electron-builder block maps of the new artifact against a cached copy of
  the previous one, and fetch the missing blocks with HTTP range requests. No pairwise delta files
  exist. Conveyor ships deltas through Sparkle 2 (about 31 KB on macOS).

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's next

- [Auto-update](/docs/packaging/auto-update): configure `NucleusUpdater` and release channels.
- [Code signing](/docs/packaging/code-signing): sign and notarize builds for each OS.
- [CI/CD](/docs/packaging/ci-cd): the GitHub Actions for building and publishing.
- [GraalVM](/docs/performance/graalvm): package a JDK-less native binary.
