# Migrate from Nucleus 2.x to 3.0

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/migrate/from-2.x

Move a Nucleus 2.x app to 3.0. Remove the backend choice and the AWT windows, switch the window state import, and review the runtime and build changes.

In this tutorial, you'll move a Nucleus 2.x app to 3.0. Fix the compile errors first, then review
the runtime and build changes that alter behavior without breaking the build.

## Before you start

- Bump the plugin and every `dev.nucleusframework` artifact to `<version>`.
- Use JDK 17 or later and Compose Multiplatform 1.12. See [Compatibility](/docs/start/install).
- If your app uses `decorated-window-jbr` or `decorated-window-jni`, plan time for
  [the AWT removal](#replace-compose-desktop-windows-dialogs-and-tray). It is the largest step.

## Review the checklist

Every breaking or behavior change in 3.0, with the step on this page and the feature page.

**Compile errors and removed APIs**

| Change | What to do | Docs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `decorated-window-awt`, `-jbr`, `-jni` deleted. `NucleusBackend`, `LocalNucleusBackend`, `nucleusApplication(backend = …)` and `NucleusApplicationScope.backend` removed. | Drop the dependency and the `backend` argument. [Step](#remove-the-backend-selection) | [Windows](/docs/windows) |
| `NucleusWindowUnsafe.awtWindow` / `awtDialog` removed. Receiver-less AWT overloads of `MaterialDecoratedWindow`, `MaterialDecoratedDialog`, `JewelDecoratedWindow`, `JewelDecoratedDialog` removed. | Use `unsafe.taoWindow` and the `NucleusApplicationScope` receivers. [Step](#remove-the-backend-selection) | [Toolkits](/docs/toolkits) |
| Compose Desktop's AWT `Window`, `DialogWindow` and `Tray` are unsupported. `SwingPanel` and AWT `Canvas` embedding fail at runtime. | Use `DecoratedWindow`, `DecoratedDialog`, `HostedWindow` / `HostedDialog`, ComposeNativeTray, and `NativeView`. [Step](#replace-compose-desktop-windows-dialogs-and-tray) | [Dialogs and popups](/docs/windows/dialogs-popups) |
| Compose's `androidx.compose.ui.window.v2` types are not accepted. | Import `dev.nucleusframework.window.tao.v2` instead. [Step](#switch-window-state-to-the-nucleus-v2-package) | [Window state](/docs/windows/window-state) |
| `NucleusWindowHost.Window` takes two new parameters, `minimizable` and `maximizable`. | Add them to your themed host. [Step](#update-custom-window-hosts) | [Toolkits](/docs/toolkits) |
| Pre-release multi-window APIs renamed: `SatelliteDragKind` is `WorkspaceDragKind`, `TabDropGhost.title` is `TabDropGhost.tab`. The family requires an opt-in. | Rename, then opt in to `ExperimentalNucleusApi`. [Step](#opt-in-to-the-multi-window-apis) | [Multi-window](/docs/multi-window) |
| `macOS.appStore` and `TargetFormat.isStoreFormat` no longer compile. | Use `macOS { pkg { appStore = … } }` and `ExecutableRuntime.isSandboxed()`. [Step](#replace-the-pkg-store-flags) | [macOS packaging](/docs/packaging/macos) |

**Runtime behavior changes**

| Change | What to do | Docs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cmd+Q and Dock → Quit call every window's `onCloseRequest`. | Check that your close handlers exit or close. [Step](#check-your-close-handlers) | [Application](/docs/lifecycle/application) |
| Notification, media control and launcher callbacks run on the host UI thread, not the AWT EDT. | Remove Swing assumptions in those callbacks. [Step](#move-native-callbacks-off-the-awt-edt) | [Threading](/docs/concepts/threading) |
| Trackpad pinch arrives as `PointerEventType.ScaleStart` / `ScaleChange` / `ScaleEnd`. | Move pinch code to `Modifier.transformable` or a Scale listener. [Step](#handle-pinch-and-pan-events) | [Trackpad gestures](/docs/input/trackpad-gestures) |
| macOS trackpad scrolling arrives as `PanStart` / `PanMove` / `PanEnd`. | Handle Pan in custom `Scroll` handlers. [Step](#handle-pinch-and-pan-events) | [Trackpad gestures](/docs/input/trackpad-gestures) |
| Single instance is off in dev runs. | Pass `enableSingleInstance = true` to test it from `run`. [Step](#test-single-instance-in-dev-runs) | [Single instance](/docs/lifecycle/single-instance) |
| `nucleusApplication` initializes FileKit with `NucleusApp.appId`. | Check your FileKit data directory, or opt out. [Step](#check-the-filekit-initialization) | [File dialogs](/docs/os/file-dialogs) |
| Windows: a hung event loop logs `SEVERE` with a thread dump. | Hook the callbacks or mark long work. [Step](#handle-the-event-loop-watchdog) | [Application](/docs/lifecycle/application) |
| Windows: opaque windows render text with LCD (ClearType) antialiasing. | Update screenshot baselines, or opt out. [Step](#review-lcd-text-on-windows) | [HiDPI](/docs/windows/hidpi) |
| JRE fonts are stripped from jlink runtime images. | Keep them if you draw text through AWT or Swing. [Step](#keep-jre-fonts-for-awt-text) | [Configuration](/docs/start/configuration) |
| Nucleus JNI libraries ship next to the packaged app, not inside its JARs. | Load them through `NativeLibraryLoader`, not as resources. [Step](#load-nucleus-native-libraries-through-the-loader) | [Packaging](/docs/packaging) |

**Build and CI changes**

| Change | What to do | Docs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The plugin downloads Node.js for packaging. | Drop `setup-node` from CI and cache the download. [Step](#drop-nodejs-from-ci) | [CI/CD](/docs/packaging/ci-cd) |
| `nucleusOptimization` and its `lastJdk` knob are opt-in. `lastJdk` downloads OpenJDK 27. | Turn them on if you want them. [Step](#opt-in-to-the-startup-pack) | [Performance](/docs/performance) |

**New in 3.0, no action required**

| Change | When it matters | Docs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TaoWindow.canPlaceOnScreen` and `SatelliteScope.isCompositorPlaced` report native Wayland placement. | Chrome that reads window positions on Linux. [Step](#opt-in-to-the-multi-window-apis) | [Linux and Wayland](/docs/windows/linux-wayland) |
| `nucleusApplication(exitProcessOnExit = true)` is the default. | Pass `false` to keep running after the last window. | [Application](/docs/lifecycle/application) |
| `-Dnucleus.native.cacheDir` and `NativeLibraryLoader.cacheDirectory` relocate the native library cache. | Fat JARs, IDE runs, distributions built without the plugin. [Step](#load-nucleus-native-libraries-through-the-loader) | [Packaging](/docs/packaging) |

## Remove the backend selection

Tao is the only window runtime in 3.0, and `nucleus-application` brings it along.

1. Remove `decorated-window-jbr`, `decorated-window-jni`, `decorated-window-awt` and
   `decorated-window-tao` from every module's dependencies.
2. Drop the `backend` argument and the `NucleusBackend` import. Delete reads of
   `LocalNucleusBackend` and `NucleusApplicationScope.backend`, and keep the Tao branch of
   backend-specific code:

   ```diff
   -fun main(args: Array<String>) = nucleusApplication(args, backend = NucleusBackend.Tao) {
   +fun main(args: Array<String>) = nucleusApplication(args) {
   ```

3. Replace `nucleusWindow.unsafe.awtWindow` with `unsafe.taoWindow`, or `unsafe.taoHandle` for the
   native handle. Check `NucleusWindow` first: `toFront()`, `setMinimumSize()`, `setIcon()` and
   `boundsOnScreen()` cover most calls.
4. Call the Material and Jewel windows and dialogs on a `NucleusApplicationScope`, because the
   receiver-less AWT overloads are gone. Inside `nucleusApplication { }` nothing changes. Deeper in
   the composition, read the scope from `LocalNucleusApplicationScope`:

   ```kotlin
   val scope = LocalNucleusApplicationScope.current
   scope.MaterialDecoratedWindow(onCloseRequest = onClose, title = "Editor") { EditorContent() }
   ```

## Replace Compose Desktop windows, dialogs, and tray

Nucleus 3.0 never creates an AWT window, so Compose Desktop's `Window`, `DialogWindow` and `Tray`
fail under `nucleusApplication`. Swap each for its Nucleus counterpart:

| Compose Desktop (AWT) | Nucleus 3.0 |
| --- | --- |
| `Window(…)` | `DecoratedWindow(…)`, or `HostedWindow(…)` in library code |
| `DialogWindow(…)` | `DecoratedDialog(…)`, or `HostedDialog(…)` in library code |
| `Tray(…)` from `androidx.compose.ui.window` | `Tray(…)` from [ComposeNativeTray](/docs/os/tray) |
| `SwingPanel`, AWT `Canvas` | [`NativeView`](/docs/native-content/native-views) |
| `JFileChooser`, `java.awt.FileDialog` | [FileKit](/docs/os/file-dialogs) |
| `window.window` (`ComposeWindow`) | `nucleusWindow` and `LocalNucleusWindow` |

`DecoratedWindow` and `DecoratedDialog` take the same `onCloseRequest` and `title` arguments.
`HostedWindow` and `HostedDialog` wear the toolkit the app provides, so a library does not pick a
look.

For the tray, add `dev.nucleusframework:composenativetray:<version>` and import
`dev.nucleusframework.composenativetray.tray.api.Tray`. Its API differs from Compose's `Tray`, so
port the menu with the [tray menu DSL](/docs/os/tray/menu).

AWT classes that don't need a window keep working: `BufferedImage`, `ImageIO`, `java.awt.Font`,
and the AWT clipboard. APIs that need a window or the AWT event loop do not.

## Switch window state to the Nucleus v2 package

Compose 1.12's window API v2 depends on AWT, so Nucleus ships a copy with the same members.
Change the import of `rememberWindowState`, `WindowState`, `DialogState`, `Screen`, the geometry
providers and the `remember*` factories:

```diff
-import androidx.compose.ui.window.v2.rememberWindowState
+import dev.nucleusframework.window.tao.v2.rememberWindowState
```

The v1 `androidx.compose.ui.window.WindowState` keeps working. See
[Window state](/docs/windows/window-state).

## Update custom window hosts

`NucleusWindowHost.Window` takes `minimizable: Boolean` and `maximizable: Boolean` after
`resizable`. A themed host must add both and pass them on. They default to `true` on
`DecoratedWindow` and `HostedWindow`, and `DecoratedDialog` passes `false`. `NucleusDialogHost` is
unchanged.

## Opt in to the multi-window APIs

Satellites, the dock layout and tabs are `@ExperimentalNucleusApi` at `ERROR` level. Opt in per
call site or per module:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
kotlin {
    compilerOptions {
        optIn.add("dev.nucleusframework.window.ExperimentalNucleusApi")
    }
}
```

If you used a pre-release build, rename `SatelliteDragKind` to `WorkspaceDragKind` (it now serves
both workspaces) and `dropGhost.title` to `dropGhost.tab.title`.

On native Wayland, the app can neither read nor set window screen positions. Branch on
`TaoWindow.canPlaceOnScreen` (or `SatelliteScope.isCompositorPlaced` in a satellite), not on the
compositor name. See [Linux and Wayland](/docs/windows/linux-wayland).

## Replace the PKG store flags

A PKG now targets either the Mac App Store or Developer ID. Move the flag into the `pkg { }` block:

```diff title="build.gradle.kts"
 macOS {
-    appStore = true
+    pkg { appStore = true } // default; false builds a Developer ID PKG
 }
```

In runtime code, replace `ExecutableRuntime.isPkg()` and `isStoreFormat` checks with
`ExecutableRuntime.isSandboxed()`. A Developer ID PKG is not sandboxed, so it can update itself.
See [Sandboxing](/docs/packaging/sandboxing).

## Review runtime behavior changes

These changes compile without errors. Check each one against your app.

### Check your close handlers

On macOS, Cmd+Q and Dock → Quit now call `onCloseRequest` on every open window, as on Windows and
Linux. A handler that neither calls `exitApplication()` nor closes its window cancels the quit. A
hide-to-tray handler lets the quit through while `NucleusApplicationScope.isQuitting` is `true`.
See [Application](/docs/lifecycle/application).

### Move native callbacks off the AWT EDT

`notification-linux`, `notification-windows`, `media-control`, `launcher-linux` and
`launcher-macos` callbacks run on the host UI thread. Compose state writes keep working. Remove
`SwingUtilities.isEventDispatchThread()` checks and Swing calls from them. See
[Threading](/docs/concepts/threading).

### Handle pinch and pan events

A trackpad pinch or Ctrl+wheel arrives as `ScaleStart` / `ScaleChange` / `ScaleEnd`, which
`detectTransformGestures` does not see in Compose 1.12: use `Modifier.transformable`. On macOS,
trackpad scrolling arrives as `PanStart` / `PanMove` / `PanEnd`. `Modifier.scrollable` handles it,
but a custom `Scroll` handler must handle Pan too:

```kotlin
when (event.type) {
    PointerEventType.Scroll -> offset += change.scrollDelta * stepPx
    PointerEventType.PanMove -> offset += change.panOffset
    PointerEventType.ScaleChange -> zoom *= change.scaleFactor
}
```

`-Dnucleus.tao.trackpadPanEvents=false` sends trackpad scrolling as `Scroll`. See
[Trackpad gestures](/docs/input/trackpad-gestures).

### Test single instance in dev runs

A second `./gradlew run` or IDE launch now starts a separate instance. Packaged builds keep the
lock. To test the forwarding from `run`, pass `nucleusApplication(args, enableSingleInstance = true)`.

### Check the FileKit initialization

When FileKit is on the classpath, `nucleusApplication` calls `FileKit.init(NucleusApp.appId)`, so
dev runs, packaged apps and native images share one data directory. A `FileKit.init` call before
`nucleusApplication` keeps your configuration. Pass `initializeFileKit = false` to leave FileKit
untouched.

### Handle the event-loop watchdog

On Windows, a stuck event loop now logs `SEVERE` with a thread dump. Show your own UI from the
callbacks, and wrap known long synchronous work so it is not reported:

```kotlin
nucleusApplication(args) {
    onUnresponsive { showWaitOrQuit() }
    onResponsive { hideWaitOrQuit() }
    expectUnresponsive { importHugeProjectSynchronously() }
}
```

`-Dnucleus.tao.watchdog=false` disables the watchdog.

### Review LCD text on Windows

Opaque windows on Windows now render text with ClearType antialiasing, which changes screenshots.
Update your baselines, or opt out with `-Dnucleus.text.lcd=false` at run time or
`-Pnucleus.text.lcd.patch=false` at build time.

### Keep JRE fonts for AWT text

The jlink runtime image no longer ships the JRE fonts, because Compose draws with its own. If you
render text through AWT or Swing, set `stripJreFonts = false` in `nativeDistributions`.

### Load Nucleus native libraries through the loader

Packaged apps carry Nucleus JNI libraries next to the app instead of inside the module JARs. Code
that read them as JAR resources must call `NativeLibraryLoader.load(…)`. Your own libraries under
`nucleus/native/` stay in their JARs.

## Update the build and CI

### Drop Node.js from CI

The plugin downloads the Node.js that packaging needs. Remove `actions/setup-node` from your
workflows and add `~/.gradle/nucleus/nodejs` to your cache paths. To keep the `node` on `PATH`,
set `nodejs { autoDownload = false }` in `nativeDistributions`. See [CI/CD](/docs/packaging/ci-cd).

### Opt in to the startup pack

`nucleusOptimization` is off by default. One switch turns on Serial GC, a compact heap, a single
runtime JAR, idle GC and `lastJdk` (OpenJDK 27). Override single knobs in the block:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
nucleus.application {
    nucleusOptimization = true
    nucleusOptimization { lastJdk = false }
}
```

An explicit `javaHome` wins over `lastJdk`. See [Performance](/docs/performance).

## Retest the app

Run the app, then exercise each integration that used to depend on AWT:

- **Drag and drop.** Rewrite handlers that read AWT `TransferHandler` data. See
  [Drag and drop](/docs/input/drag-and-drop).
- **Deep links.** `onDeepLink { uri -> … }` is unchanged.
- **File dialogs and embedded views.** Check every FileKit picker and `NativeView`.
- **Window placement on Linux.** Wayland compositors ignore absolute positions.
- **Quit flows** on macOS, and every close handler.
- **Packaging.** Build each installer format once, and a native image if you ship one.

<Accordions>
<Accordion title="Under the hood">

- `core-runtime` still has `WindowBackend.Awt`. It describes a Compose Desktop or Swing app that
  embeds Nucleus libraries without `nucleusApplication`, and has no effect on a Nucleus app.
- `macOS.appStore` fails at `ERROR` level instead of acting as an alias: 2.x ignored it, so an
  alias would have switched existing builds to the other channel.
- Pinch used to arrive as two synthetic touch contacts. Rotation still does.
- A `FileKit.init` call inside `content` replaces the automatic one.
- The watchdog callbacks run on a dedicated thread. `-Dnucleus.tao.watchdogGraceMs=<ms>` changes
  the grace period, and `-Dnucleus.tao.watchdogDialog=true` also shows the native dialog.
- Transparent windows, popups, Mica and Acrylic keep grayscale text.
- Only the jlink image drops the JRE fonts. `run` and GraalVM native images are unaffected.
- Fat JARs, IDE runs and distributions built without the plugin still extract native libraries to
  a cache. Relocate it with `-Dnucleus.native.cacheDir=<dir>`, or set
  `NativeLibraryLoader.cacheDirectory` in `main()` before the first native library loads.
- `compose.electronBuilder.nodePath` and `NUCLEUS_NODE_HOME` take precedence over the Node.js
  download.
- `lastJdk` downloads the JDK the first time a packaging or `run` task needs it, and falls back to
  BellSoft Liberica on Intel Macs and Windows ARM.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's next

- [Windows](/docs/windows): `nucleusApplication` and `DecoratedWindow` in 3.0.
- [Window state](/docs/windows/window-state): the AWT-free window API v2.
- [Multi-window](/docs/multi-window): satellites, docking and tabs.
- [Migrate with an AI agent](/docs/migrate/ai-agent): let an agent apply this checklist.

# Migrate with an AI agent

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/migrate/ai-agent

Point an AI coding agent at the Nucleus migration playbook or at the 3.0 upgrade guide, and let it migrate your app one verified step at a time.

Paste one prompt into an AI coding agent such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex, inside your
project, and review each step it makes.

## Upgrade a Nucleus 2.x app to 3.0

The prompt applies the [2.x to 3.0 checklist](/docs/migrate/from-2.x):

```text
Fetch https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/migrate/from-2.x and apply it to this project.
Work through the checklist group by group: compile errors first, then runtime behavior
changes, then build and CI. After each group, run ./gradlew build and stop so I can check
the app before you continue.
```

Ask the agent to list the rows that don't apply, so you can confirm them. Retest quit flows on
macOS, trackpad gestures, and close handlers yourself.

## Migrate a JetBrains Compose Desktop app

```text
Fetch https://nucleusframework.dev/nucleus-migrate.md and follow its instructions to
analyze this app and migrate it to Nucleus step by step.
```

The agent scans the app for AWT, Swing and packaging usage, asks which design system and native
features you want, then migrates one phase at a time: Gradle DSL, window shell, AWT removal,
features, packaging, GraalVM, CI. Each phase ends with a checkpoint, and a final report lists what
changed.

Nucleus 3.0 has no AWT window backend. If the agent adds `decorated-window-jbr` or
`decorated-window-jni`, refuse and point it at [Migrate from Nucleus 2.x to 3.0](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

## Install the playbook as a Claude Code skill

Download [nucleus-migrate.skill](https://nucleusframework.dev/nucleus-migrate.skill) and unzip it
into your skills directory:

```shell
cd ~/.claude/skills && unzip ~/Downloads/nucleus-migrate.skill
```

Run `/nucleus-migrate`, or ask Claude Code to migrate the app to Nucleus.

## What's next

- [Migrate from Nucleus 2.x to 3.0](/docs/migrate/from-2.x): the checklist the first prompt applies.
- [Migrate from JetBrains Compose Desktop](/docs/migrate/from-jb-compose): the build migration by hand.
- [Migrate from Nucleus 1.x](/docs/migrate/from-1.x): the namespace move to 2.0.

# Migrate from JetBrains Compose Desktop

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/migrate/from-jb-compose

Move a JetBrains Compose Desktop app to Nucleus. Apply the plugin, rename the DSL block, and replace the AWT windows, dialogs, and tray with their Nucleus equivalents.

Move a JetBrains Compose Desktop app to Nucleus: add the plugin, rename the application block,
and replace the AWT windows with `DecoratedWindow`.

An AI coding agent can run the whole migration. See [Migrate with an AI agent](/docs/migrate/ai-agent).

## Before you start

- Compose Multiplatform 1.12 or later and JDK 17 or later.
- The list of AWT and Swing APIs your UI uses (`Window`, `DialogWindow`, `Tray`, `SwingPanel`,
  `JFileChooser`, `MenuBar`). Nucleus windows are not AWT windows, so each one needs a replacement.

## Add the plugin

Keep the JetBrains Compose plugin: Nucleus extends it.

```diff title="build.gradle.kts"
 plugins {
     id("org.jetbrains.compose") version "1.12.0"
+    id("dev.nucleusframework") version "<version>"
 }
```

## Move the build to the Nucleus DSL

1. Swap the DSL imports (`TargetFormat`, `CompressionLevel`, `SigningAlgorithm`, and the others):
   `org.jetbrains.compose.desktop.application.dsl` becomes `dev.nucleusframework.desktop.application.dsl`.
2. Rename `compose.desktop.application { }` to `nucleus.application { }`. The two blocks cannot
   coexist. Every setting inside stays the same.
3. Set `homepage`. Without it, `packageDeb` and `packageGraalvmDeb` fail with
   `Please specify project homepage`.

```diff title="build.gradle.kts"
-compose.desktop.application {
+nucleus.application {
     mainClass = "com.example.MainKt"
     nativeDistributions {
+        homepage = "https://myapp.example.com"
     }
 }
```

The rest of the build and the existing Gradle tasks (`run`, `packageDmg`, `packageDeb`) work
unchanged, [Compose Hot Reload](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/multiplatform/compose-hot-reload.html)
included.

## Replace the entry point and windows

Add `nucleus-application`, which brings the entry point and the window runtime. See
[Modules](/docs/concepts/modules) for the optional ones.

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
dependencies {
    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.nucleus-application:<version>")
}
```

Swap `application { }` for `nucleusApplication { }` and `Window` for `DecoratedWindow`. Keep
command-line early exits above `nucleusApplication`.

```diff
-import androidx.compose.ui.window.Window
-import androidx.compose.ui.window.application
+import dev.nucleusframework.application.DecoratedWindow
+import dev.nucleusframework.application.nucleusApplication
+import dev.nucleusframework.window.TitleBar

-fun main() = application {
-    Window(onCloseRequest = ::exitApplication, title = "MyApp") {
+fun main(args: Array<String>) = nucleusApplication(args) {
+    DecoratedWindow(onCloseRequest = ::exitApplication, title = "MyApp") {
+        TitleBar { Text(title) }
         App()
     }
 }
```

Then replace each AWT API. Compose Desktop's `Window`, `DialogWindow` and `Tray` fail under
`nucleusApplication`:

| Compose Desktop (AWT) | Nucleus |
| --- | --- |
| `Window(…)` | [`DecoratedWindow(…)`](/docs/windows) |
| `DialogWindow(…)` | [`DecoratedDialog(…)`](/docs/windows/dialogs-popups) |
| `Tray(…)` | `Tray(…)` from [ComposeNativeTray](/docs/os/tray) |
| `MenuBar { }` | [`menu-macos`](/docs/os/menus/menu-bar) for the macOS app menu |
| `SwingPanel`, AWT `Canvas` | [`NativeView`](/docs/native-content/native-views) |
| `JFileChooser`, `java.awt.FileDialog` | [FileKit](/docs/os/file-dialogs) |
| `window.window` (`ComposeWindow`) | `nucleusWindow` and `LocalNucleusWindow` |
| `rememberWindowState()` from `androidx.compose.ui.window.v2` | the same function from [`dev.nucleusframework.window.tao.v2`](/docs/windows/window-state) |

For a Material 3, Material 2 or Jewel look, use `MaterialDecoratedWindow` or
`JewelDecoratedWindow` ([Toolkits](/docs/toolkits)). AWT classes that need no window keep
working: `BufferedImage`, `ImageIO`, `java.awt.Font`, and the AWT clipboard.

## Run the app

Run `./gradlew run`, then check the title bar, window drag, minimize and fullscreen, secondary
windows, and each dialog you ported.

## Enable Nucleus packaging features

These settings are opt-in. Packaging needs no Node.js on the machine.

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
nucleus.application {
    nativeDistributions {
        targetFormats(TargetFormat.Dmg, TargetFormat.Nsis, TargetFormat.AppImage, TargetFormat.Flatpak)
        cleanupNativeLibs = true
        enableAotCache = true
        splashImage = "splash.png"
        protocol("MyApp", "myapp")
        publish { github { enabled = true; owner = "myorg"; repo = "myapp" } }
    }
}
```

See [Packaging](/docs/packaging) for every option, and
[Nucleus and vanilla Compose Multiplatform](/docs/compare/cmp-default#what-nucleus-adds) for
what each feature adds over Compose Desktop.

## What's next

- [Windows](/docs/windows): `nucleusApplication`, `DecoratedWindow` and the title bar.
- [Configuration](/docs/start/configuration): the full `nucleus { }` DSL.
- [Auto-update](/docs/packaging/auto-update): ship updates with YAML metadata.
- [GraalVM](/docs/performance/graalvm): package a native image.

# Migrating from Nucleus 1.x to 2.0

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/migrate/from-1.x

Port a Nucleus 1.x desktop app to 2.0 by renaming the project namespace and moving bootstrap into nucleusApplication.

In this tutorial, you'll migrate a Nucleus 1.x desktop app to 2.0. Nucleus 2.0 uses a single
entry point, `nucleusApplication`, and moves the project namespace to `dev.nucleusframework`.
The migration is mostly mechanical: rename the namespace, then move your `application { }` block
into `nucleusApplication(args) { }`, which removes about 30 lines of bootstrap from a typical `main()`.

This guide stops at Nucleus 2.0. After it, follow
[Migrate from Nucleus 2.x to 3.0](/docs/migrate/from-2.x): 3.0 removes the AWT backend and
`NucleusBackend`, which the steps below still mention.

## Before you start

Nucleus 2.0 needs two build changes before you touch any application code.

### Set the JDK toolchain to 25 (only if you use Jewel)

The core 2.0 artifacts — `core-runtime`, `nucleus-application`, `decorated-window-core`,
`decorated-window-material3`, `decorated-window-tao` — target a JDK 17 baseline. The **Jewel** stack
is the exception: `decorated-window-jewel` and the IntelliJ platform libraries it pulls are
published for **JDK 25**. So the toolchain bump is a Jewel requirement, not a blanket Nucleus one.

If your app uses `JewelDecoratedWindow` / `JewelDecoratedDialog`, set the toolchain on **every**
module that pulls the Jewel stack:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
kotlin { jvmToolchain(25) }
```

The failing module is where Jewel is on the classpath — often a shared UI module, not just the
desktop app. In a Kotlin Multiplatform project the `jvm()` target defaults to your Gradle JDK
(commonly 21), so set the toolchain in the `shared` module too:

```kotlin title="shared/build.gradle.kts"
kotlin {
    jvmToolchain(25)     // the jvm() target needs it; the Android target keeps its own bytecode level
    // ...
}
```

Skip this and dependency resolution fails with (the version is whatever toolchain you're on today —
often 21): `Dependency resolution is looking for a library compatible with JVM runtime version 21,
but 'dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.decorated-window-jewel' is only compatible with JVM runtime
version 25 or newer.`

If you don't use Jewel, you can stay on your current toolchain (JDK 17 or newer).

### Add the IntelliJ snapshots repository

Nucleus 2.x pulls Jewel `0.39.1-262.9437.29`, which lives only in the IntelliJ snapshots
repository. Add it to `settings.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin title="settings.gradle.kts"
dependencyResolutionManagement {
    repositories {
        google()
        mavenCentral()
        maven("https://www.jetbrains.com/intellij-repository/releases")
        maven("https://www.jetbrains.com/intellij-repository/snapshots") // new
    }
}
```

If you declare Jewel directly, pin it to the same coordinate Nucleus brings in transitively:

```toml
intellijIcons = "262.9437.16"
jewel        = "0.39.1-262.9437.29"
```

## What changed in 2.0

| Area | 1.x | 2.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin ID | `io.github.kdroidfilter.nucleus` | `dev.nucleusframework` |
| Maven group | `io.github.kdroidfilter` | `dev.nucleusframework` |
| Kotlin package root | `io.github.kdroidfilter.nucleus.*` | `dev.nucleusframework.*` |
| Entry point | `application { }` | `nucleusApplication(args) { }` |
| Window | `Window(...)` | `DecoratedWindow(...)` |
| GraalVM bootstrap | Manual `GraalVmInitializer.initialize()` | Automatic |
| Single instance | Manual `SingleInstanceManager.isSingleInstance(...)` | Automatic |
| Restore on second launch | Manual `LaunchedEffect` + `toFront()` | Automatic |
| AOT training timer | Manual `Thread` + `exitProcess` | `aotTraining(duration = ...)` |
| AutoLaunch cache prime | Manual | Automatic |
| Windows AUMID | Manual | Automatic |

## Update the plugin ID and Maven coordinates

Change the plugin ID and version:

```diff
 plugins {
-    id("io.github.kdroidfilter.nucleus") version "1.3.0"
+    id("dev.nucleusframework") version "<version>"
 }
```

Update the dependency coordinates:

```diff
 dependencies {
-    implementation("io.github.kdroidfilter:nucleus.core-runtime:1.3.0")
-    implementation("io.github.kdroidfilter:nucleus.nucleus-application:1.3.0")
+    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.core-runtime:<version>")
+    implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.nucleus-application:<version>")
 }
```

Update any Gradle DSL imports:

```diff
-import io.github.kdroidfilter.nucleus.desktop.application.dsl.TargetFormat
+import dev.nucleusframework.desktop.application.dsl.TargetFormat
```

## Rename the Kotlin imports

Run a project-wide find and replace:

```
io.github.kdroidfilter.nucleus  →  dev.nucleusframework
```

No classes are renamed — only the package prefix changes.

## Switch to nucleusApplication

In 1.x you wrapped Compose Desktop's `application { }` in Nucleus init helpers. In 2.0,
`nucleusApplication` runs the bootstrap in the correct order and exposes a unified
`NucleusApplicationScope`.

### Before: main() in 1.x

```kotlin
fun main(args: Array<String>) {
    GraalVmInitializer.initialize()
    AutoLaunch.wasStartedAtLogin(args)
    if (Platform.Current == Platform.Windows) {
        WindowsJumpListManager.setProcessAppId()
    }

    if (AotRuntime.isTraining()) {
        Thread({ Thread.sleep(45_000); exitProcess(0) }, "aot-timer")
            .apply { isDaemon = false }.start()
    }

    application {
        val isFirstInstance = remember {
            SingleInstanceManager.isSingleInstance(
                onRestoreFileCreated = { DeepLinkHandler.writeUriTo(this) },
                onRestoreRequest = { /* hand-rolled restore state */ },
            )
        }
        if (!isFirstInstance) { exitApplication(); return@application }

        DeepLinkHandler.register(args) { uri -> handleDeepLink(uri) }

        Window(onCloseRequest = ::exitApplication, title = "My App") { App() }
    }
}
```

### After: main() in 2.0

```kotlin
import dev.nucleusframework.application.nucleusApplication
import dev.nucleusframework.application.aotTraining
import kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.seconds

fun main(args: Array<String>) = nucleusApplication(args) {
    aotTraining(duration = 45.seconds)

    onDeepLink { uri -> handleDeepLink(uri) }

    MaterialDecoratedWindow(onCloseRequest = ::exitApplication, title = "My App") {
        App()
    }
}
```

### Keep early exits above nucleusApplication

`nucleusApplication` runs the full bootstrap: GraalVM init, the single-instance lock, and the
Compose loop. For invocation modes that must bypass all of that — a desktop scheduler re-launch
or a boot receiver — keep the check above the call:

```kotlin
fun main(args: Array<String>) {
    if (DesktopBootReceiver.isSchedulerInvocation(args)) {
        DesktopBootReceiver.handle(args, registry = MyTaskRegistry.registry)
        exitProcess(0)
    }

    nucleusApplication(args) { /* ... */ }
}
```

Putting these checks inside the scope acquires the single-instance lock first — the opposite of
what you want for a bypass path.

### What nucleusApplication runs, in order

1. `GraalVmInitializer.initialize()` — fonts, charsets, HiDPI, `java.home`.
2. The AOT training timer, when `-Dnucleus.aot.mode=training` is set and you call `aotTraining(…)`.
3. The single-instance lock. A second instance relays its CLI deep link to the primary and exits with code 0.
4. Platform priming: the `AutoLaunch.wasStartedAtLogin(args)` cache is warmed, and on Windows
   `WindowsJumpListManager.setProcessAppId()` runs before any window. Both are reflective — they
   fire only if the modules are on the classpath.
5. Backend resolution: `NucleusBackend.Auto` picks AWT or Tao.
6. The Compose application loop.

**Don't initialize COM on the main thread before `nucleusApplication` (Tao / Windows).** The Tao
backend runs the Win32 message loop as a single-threaded COM apartment (STA) on the main thread.
If something already put that thread into a multithreaded apartment (MTA) — a common culprit is
calling `WindowsNotificationCenter.initialize()` yourself in `main()` — Tao's `OleInitialize` fails
and the process aborts natively:

```
thread '<unnamed>' panicked at tao/.../windows/window.rs:
OleInitialize failed! Result was: `RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE`.
```

The bootstrap already primes the AUMID and notification center on the right thread, so drop the
manual call in the GUI path. If a headless bypass path (a scheduler invocation) still needs it,
keep that call there — it has no Tao window to conflict with.

## Replace Window with DecoratedWindow

Pick the variant that matches your design system:

| Composable | Module |
|---|---|
| `DecoratedWindow(…)` | `nucleus.decorated-window-core` |
| `MaterialDecoratedWindow(…)` | `nucleus.decorated-window-material3` |
| `JewelDecoratedWindow(…)` | `nucleus.decorated-window-jewel` |

All three expose `nucleusWindow` inside their content — a backend-agnostic handle for `show()`,
`toFront()`, `setMinimized()`, and similar calls.

### Window composables are extension functions now

This is the most common breakage. In 1.x, `JewelDecoratedWindow` was a plain `@Composable`. In
2.0 it is an extension on `NucleusApplicationScope`:

```kotlin
fun NucleusApplicationScope.JewelDecoratedWindow(
    onCloseRequest: () -> Unit, ...,
    content: @Composable NucleusDecoratedWindowScope.() -> Unit,
)
```

Any wrapper composable you wrote in 1.x must become an extension on the same scope:

```diff
 @Composable
-fun MyOnboardingWindow(vmFactory: ViewModelFactory) {
+fun NucleusApplicationScope.MyOnboardingWindow(vmFactory: ViewModelFactory) {
     JewelDecoratedWindow(onCloseRequest = {}, title = "...") { /* ... */ }
 }
```

The call site inside `nucleusApplication { … }` does not change — the receiver is implicit.

### Dialogs follow the same rule

| Receiver | Backend support |
|---|---|
| `JewelDecoratedDialog(…)` (no receiver) | AWT only. Its implementation module isn't on the Tao classpath, so it fails at render with `ClassNotFoundException: dev.nucleusframework.window.DecoratedDialogKt`. |
| `NucleusApplicationScope.JewelDecoratedDialog(…)` | Backend-agnostic. Dispatches to AWT or Tao. |

Both overloads exist, so the plain call still **compiles** — it only fails at runtime on Tao. Use
the scoped variant for anything composed inside `nucleusApplication { … }`.

The catch: dialogs are usually opened deep in your UI tree (an event editor, a settings sheet),
far from the `NucleusApplicationScope` receiver. Rather than thread the scope through every
signature, expose it with a `CompositionLocal`:

```kotlin
// 1. Declare it once.
val LocalNucleusApplicationScope = staticCompositionLocalOf<NucleusApplicationScope> {
    error("LocalNucleusApplicationScope not provided")
}

fun main(args: Array<String>) = nucleusApplication(args) {
    val nucleusScope = this
    JewelDecoratedWindow(onCloseRequest = ::exitApplication, title = "My App") {
        // 2. Provide it inside the window content.
        CompositionLocalProvider(LocalNucleusApplicationScope provides nucleusScope) {
            App()
        }
    }
}

// 3. Read it at the dialog call site. The explicit receiver also disambiguates the two overloads.
@Composable
fun SettingsDialog(/* ... */) {
    LocalNucleusApplicationScope.current.JewelDecoratedDialog(onCloseRequest = { /* ... */ }) {
        // JewelDialogTitleBar and other DecoratedDialogScope extensions work here:
        // NucleusDecoratedDialogScope extends DecoratedDialogScope.
    }
}
```

### CompositionLocals propagate across the Tao scene

The Tao backend opens a fresh `ComposeScene` per window and dialog. As of 2.0, the full parent
`CompositionLocalContext` is bridged automatically, so you no longer need to wrap content twice:

```kotlin
// Before — needed on Tao
IntUiTheme(theme, styling) {
    JewelDecoratedWindow(...) {
        IntUiTheme(theme, styling) { /* duplicate */ }
    }
}

// After — a single wrap is enough on every backend
IntUiTheme(theme, styling) {
    JewelDecoratedWindow(...) { /* content */ }
}
```

## Remove the manual single-instance block

Single instance is automatic in 2.0. Delete the 1.x manual block:

```diff
-val isFirstInstance = remember {
-    SingleInstanceManager.isSingleInstance(...)
-}
-if (!isFirstInstance) { exitApplication(); return@application }
```

The primary instance restores its `DecoratedWindow` (`show()` + `setMinimized(false)` +
`toFront()` + `requestFocus()`) on every second launch. The secondary instance's CLI deep link is
delivered to the primary through `onDeepLink { }`, then it exits with code 0.

Opt out for editor-style apps that allow multiple windows:

```kotlin
nucleusApplication(args, enableSingleInstance = false) { /* ... */ }
```

## Move AOT training into aotTraining

```diff
-if (AotRuntime.isTraining()) {
-    Thread({ Thread.sleep(45_000); exitProcess(0) }, "aot-timer")
-        .apply { isDaemon = false }.start()
-}

 nucleusApplication(args) {
+    aotTraining(duration = 45.seconds)
+
+    if (isAotTraining) {
+        preloadNavigationScreens()
+        preloadFontsAndImages()
+    }
 }
```

`aotTraining` is a no-op outside training mode. The scope also exposes `aotMode`, `isAotTraining`,
and `isAotRuntime`. See [AOT cache](/docs/performance/aot-cache).

## Register deep links with onDeepLink

```diff
-DeepLinkHandler.register(args) { uri -> handleDeepLink(uri) }
+onDeepLink { uri -> handleDeepLink(uri) }
```

URIs delivered before the handler is registered are buffered and replayed. `DeepLinkHandler`
remains public for low-level work.

## Drop the explicit GraalVmInitializer call

```diff
-GraalVmInitializer.initialize()
-application { /* ... */ }
+nucleusApplication(args) { /* ... */ }
```

It runs as the first bootstrap step now.

## Review the final result

```kotlin
fun main(args: Array<String>) = nucleusApplication(args) {
    remember {
        AutoLaunch.wasStartedAtLogin(args)
        if (Platform.Current == Platform.Windows) {
            WindowsJumpListManager.setProcessAppId()
        }
        true
    }

    aotTraining(duration = 45.seconds)
    onDeepLink { uri -> handleDeepLink(uri) }

    MaterialDecoratedWindow(onCloseRequest = ::exitApplication, title = "My App") {
        App()
    }
}
```

No ordered init list, no `SingleInstanceManager` plumbing, and no restore counter with a
`LaunchedEffect` to bring the window back.

## Troubleshooting

- **Imports won't resolve after the rename.** Search for `io.github.kdroidfilter.nucleus` — anything
  left is stale. Replace it with `dev.nucleusframework`.
- **`nucleusApplication` is unresolved.** Add `implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.nucleus-application:<version>")`.
- **The window doesn't restore on second launch with a plain `Window`.** That behavior lives in
  `DecoratedWindow`. Switch to a `DecoratedWindow` variant.
- **`Unresolved reference 'JewelDecoratedWindow'`.** The composable became a scope extension.
  Propagate the receiver — see [Replace Window with DecoratedWindow](#replace-window-with-decoratedwindow).
- **`ClassNotFoundException: …DecoratedDialogKt` at render on Tao.** You're calling the AWT-only
  dialog (it compiles, but its impl module isn't on the Tao classpath). Use
  `NucleusApplicationScope.JewelDecoratedDialog` — see [Dialogs follow the same rule](#dialogs-follow-the-same-rule).
- **Native abort `OleInitialize failed! RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE` / exit code `0xC0000409` on Windows.**
  Something initialized COM in MTA on the main thread before Tao. Don't call
  `WindowsNotificationCenter.initialize()` (or other COM setup) in the GUI `main()` path — the
  bootstrap handles it. See the callout in [What nucleusApplication runs, in order](#what-nucleusapplication-runs-in-order).
- **`Could not find org.jetbrains.jewel:jewel-foundation:0.37.…`** The IntelliJ snapshots repository
  is missing. See [Before you start](#before-you-start).
- **`Dependency resolution is looking for a library compatible with JVM runtime version 21`ish.** A
  module that pulls the Jewel stack isn't on the JDK 25 toolchain (check shared/UI modules and the
  KMP `jvm()` target). See [Set the JDK toolchain to 25](#set-the-jdk-toolchain-to-25-only-if-you-use-jewel).

- [Configuration](/docs/start/configuration) — the full `nucleus { }` DSL.
- [AOT cache](/docs/performance/aot-cache) — how `aotTraining` primes startup.
- [Migrate from Nucleus 2.x to 3.0](/docs/migrate/from-2.x) — the next step after this guide.

# Gradle DSL reference

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/reference/gradle-dsl

Every property and sub-block of the nucleus { } Gradle extension, checked against the plugin source.

The Nucleus Gradle plugin (`id("dev.nucleusframework")`) adds one extension, `nucleus { }`, that configures the run task, packaging, signing, publishing and GraalVM native images. This page lists its properties block by block, in source order; [Configuration](/docs/start/configuration) shows them in a working build script.

All DSL types live in `dev.nucleusframework.desktop.application.dsl`.

## `nucleus { }` [#nucleus]

`dev.nucleusframework.NucleusExtension`:

| Member | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `application { }` | `JvmApplication` | JVM app: run task, packaging, GraalVM |
| `nativeApplication { }` | `NativeApplication` | Kotlin/Native macOS app |
| `dependencies` | `NucleusPlugin.Dependencies` | Runtime module coordinates |

## `application { }` [#application----jvmapplication]

`JvmApplication`:

| Member | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from(SourceSet)`, `from(KotlinTarget)` | | Source of the app classes |
| `disableDefaultConfiguration()` | | Skip the default source wiring |
| `dependsOn(vararg Task)`, `dependsOn(vararg String)` | | Extra task dependencies |
| `fromFiles(vararg Any)` | | Extra files on the classpath |
| `mainClass` | `String?` | Entry point |
| `mainJar` | `RegularFileProperty` | Entry JAR |
| `javaHome` | `String` | JDK used to run and package. Always wins over `lastJdk` |
| `args`, `args(vararg)` | `MutableList<String>` | App arguments |
| `jvmArgs`, `jvmArgs(vararg)` | `MutableList<String>` | JVM arguments. The defaults already contain `--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED` (JEP 472) |
| `garbageCollector` | `GarbageCollector?` | HotSpot collector: `SERIAL`, `PARALLEL`, `G1`, `Z`, `SHENANDOAH`, `EPSILON`. Unset keeps JDK ergonomics. An explicit `-XX:+Use…GC` in `jvmArgs` still wins |
| `nucleusOptimization` | `Boolean` (`false`) | Startup pack. See [below](#nucleusoptimization) |
| `nucleusOptimization { }` | `NucleusOptimizationSettings` | Per-knob overrides |
| `nativeDistributions { }` | `JvmApplicationDistributions` | See [`nativeDistributions { }`](#nativedistributions) |
| `buildTypes { }` | `JvmApplicationBuildTypes` | See [`buildTypes { }`](#buildtypes) |
| `graalvm { }` | `GraalvmSettings` | See [`graalvm { }`](#graalvm--graalvmsettings) |
| `additionalLaunchers { }` | `NamedDomainObjectContainer<AdditionalLauncher>` | See [`additionalLaunchers { }`](#additionallaunchers) |

### `nucleusOptimization { }` [#nucleusoptimization]

`nucleusOptimization = true` turns on five startup knobs at once. Each knob in the block is a `Boolean?`: `null` follows the master switch, `true` or `false` forces that knob regardless of the others.

```kotlin
nucleus.application {
    nucleusOptimization = true
    nucleusOptimization { idleGc = false }
}
```

| Knob | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `serialGc` | Serial GC when `garbageCollector` is unset. An explicit collector wins |
| `compactHeap` | Adds `-Xms32m` and `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=25`, unless `jvmArgs` already sets them |
| `singleJar` | Flattens the runtime JARs (or sets `joinOutputJars` when ProGuard is on) so the jpackage image holds one JAR |
| `idleGc` | Requests a GC 3 s after the last window loses focus, or at once when a window is minimized. Also baked into GraalVM images |
| `lastJdk` | Packages and runs with OpenJDK 27, downloaded to `<gradle-user-home>/nucleus/jdk` (BellSoft Liberica JDK 27 on Intel macOS and Windows ARM). `javaHome` wins. The Gradle compile JDK does not change |

The pack leaves `enableAotCache` and ProGuard alone. See [Startup optimization](/docs/performance/startup).

### `additionalLaunchers { }` [#additionallaunchers]

Each named `AdditionalLauncher` adds a second executable to the jpackage image. The container name becomes the launcher name.

| Property | Type |
| --- | --- |
| `appVersion` | `String?` |
| `module` | `String?` (JPMS module) |
| `mainClass` | `String?` |
| `mainJar` | `String?` |
| `jvmArgs`, `jvmArgs(vararg)` | `MutableList<String>?` |
| `args`, `args(vararg)` | `MutableList<String>?` |
| `icon` | `RegularFileProperty` |
| `winConsole` | `Boolean?` (Windows only) |

### `buildTypes { }` [#buildtypes]

`buildTypes { release { proguard { } } }` configures `ProguardSettings` for the release tasks:

| Property | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `Property<String>` | `"7.10.0"` |
| `maxHeapSize` | `Property<String>` | unset |
| `configurationFiles` | `ConfigurableFileCollection` | empty |
| `isEnabled` | `Property<Boolean>` | `false` |
| `obfuscate` | `Property<Boolean>` | `false` |
| `optimize` | `Property<Boolean>` | `true` |
| `joinOutputJars` | `Property<Boolean>` | `false` |

## `nativeDistributions { }` [#nativedistributions]

`JvmApplicationDistributions`, which extends `AbstractDistributions`.

### Shared metadata [#shared-metadata]

From `AbstractDistributions`, also available under `nativeApplication { distributions { } }`:

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `outputBaseDir` | `DirectoryProperty` | Default `build/compose/binaries` |
| `appName`, `packageName`, `packageVersion` | `String?` | |
| `copyright`, `description`, `vendor`, `homepage` | `String?` | |
| `appResourcesRootDir` | `DirectoryProperty` | Per-OS resources copied into the app |
| `licenseFile` | `RegularFileProperty` | |
| `targetFormats`, `targetFormats(vararg)` | `Set<TargetFormat>` | See [`TargetFormat`](#targetformat) |

### Runtime image and packaging [#runtime-image]

| Property | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modules`, `modules(vararg)` | `ArrayList<String>` | `java.base`, `java.desktop`, `java.logging`, `java.net.http`, `jdk.accessibility`, `jdk.crypto.ec`, `jdk.unsupported` | JDK modules passed to jlink |
| `includeAllModules` | `Boolean` | `false` | Every module the JDK lists, minus `jdk.jlink` |
| `stripJreFonts` | `Boolean` | `true` | Drops `java.desktop/lib/fonts` from the runtime image |
| `cleanupNativeLibs` | `Boolean` | `false` | Strips native libraries built for other platforms |
| `splashImage` | `String?` | | Splash screen image |
| `enableAotCache` | `Boolean` | `false` | Shortcut for `aotCache.enabled` |
| `aotCache { }` | `AotCacheSettings` | | See [below](#aotcache) |
| `compressionLevel` | `CompressionLevel?` | | `Store`, `Normal`, `Maximum`, `Ultra`. `linux.appImage.compressionLevel` and `windows.portable.compressionLevel` override it for their format |
| `artifactName` | `String` | `"${name}-${version}-${os}-${arch}.${ext}"` | Output file name template |
| `trustedCertificates` | `ConfigurableFileCollection` | | CA certificates added to the bundled `cacerts`. See [Trusted certificates](/docs/packaging/trusted-certificates) |
| `protocols`, `protocol(name, vararg schemes)` | `MutableList<UrlProtocol>` | | Deep-link URL schemes |
| `fileAssociation(mimeType, extension, description, linuxIconFile?, windowsIconFile?, macOSIconFile?)` | | | Registers the association on all three OSes |
| `sandboxing { }` | `SandboxingSettings` | | `keepNativeLibsInJars(vararg)`: JAR name substrings whose native libraries stay untouched in sandboxed builds |
| `signing { }` | `UnifiedSigningSettings` | | `macOS { }`, `windows { }`, `linux { }` in one place. Same objects as the per-OS `signing` blocks |
| `nodejs { }` | `NodeJsSettings` | | See [`nodejs { }`](#nodejs) |
| `publish { }` | `PublishSettings` | | See [`publish { }`](#publish) |
| `macOS { }`, `windows { }`, `linux { }` | | | See [macOS](#macos), [Windows](#windows), [Linux](#linux) |

`stripJreFonts` defaults to `true`, so jlink images ship without the JRE fonts. Compose draws with its own fonts. An app that renders text through AWT or Swing sets `stripJreFonts = false`. See [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

### `aotCache { }` [#aotcache]

| Property | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `Boolean` | `false` | JDK 25+ AOT cache |
| `compatibility` | `AotCacheCompatibility` | `COMPATIBILITY` | `COMPATIBILITY` stores class metadata only and runs on any CPU of the architecture. `NATIVE` also caches machine code for the build machine's CPU |
| `extraTrainingJvmArgs`, `extraTrainingJvmArgs(vararg)` | `MutableList<String>` | empty | JVM arguments for the training run only |

See [AOT cache](/docs/performance/aot-cache).

### `nodejs { }` [#nodejs]

`NodeJsSettings` controls the Node.js that runs electron-builder, which every format except `RawAppImage` needs.

| Property | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `autoDownload` | `Property<Boolean>` | `true` | Download from `nodejs.org` and cache it. `false` uses `node` and `npm` from `PATH` |
| `version` | `Property<String>` | `"22"` | A major line (`"22"`), `"lts"`, or a pinned release (`"22.11.0"`) |
| `installDir` | `DirectoryProperty` | `<gradle-user-home>/nucleus/nodejs` | Download cache |

The plugin looks for Node.js in this order: the `compose.electronBuilder.nodePath` Gradle property, the `NUCLEUS_NODE_HOME` environment variable, this block, then `PATH` (also the fallback when the download fails). A floating version stays pinned once downloaded; delete its directory under `installDir` to pick up a newer release. See [Provision Node.js](/docs/packaging#provision-nodejs).

### `TargetFormat` [#targetformat]

18 formats, in source order:

`RawAppImage`, `Pkg`, `Deb`, `Rpm`, `Dmg`, `Exe`, `Msi`, `Nsis`, `NsisWeb`, `Portable`, `AppX`, `AppImage`, `Pacman`, `Snap`, `Flatpak`, `Zip`, `Tar`, `SevenZ`.

jpackage builds `RawAppImage`, the bare app image. electron-builder builds every other format from it. `AppX` and `Flatpak` always go through the sandboxed pipeline; `Pkg` does only when `macOS { pkg { appStore = true } }`, the default.

`TargetFormat.isStoreFormat` is deprecated at `ERROR` level and no longer compiles. A PKG is a store format only when `pkg.appStore` is `true`, so branch on the DSL value instead. See [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

## `macOS { }` [#macos]

`JvmMacOSPlatformSettings`, which extends `AbstractMacOSPlatformSettings`. See [macOS packaging](/docs/packaging/macos) for the procedures.

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `iconFile` | `RegularFileProperty` | `.icns` |
| `layeredIconDir` | `DirectoryProperty` | macOS 26 `.icon` directory |
| `packageName`, `packageVersion`, `packageBuildVersion` | `String?` | |
| `bundleName` | `String?` | Name of the `.app` in every macOS format. Defaults to `appName`, then `packageName` |
| `dmgPackageVersion`, `dmgPackageBuildVersion` | `String?` | DMG-only overrides |
| `pkgPackageVersion`, `pkgPackageBuildVersion` | `String?` | PKG-only overrides |
| `bundleID`, `appCategory`, `minimumSystemVersion` | `String?` | |
| `installationPath` | `String?` | Unset installs to `/Applications` |
| `dockName` | `String?` | |
| `setDockNameSameAsPackageName` | `Boolean` | Default `true` |
| `entitlementsFile`, `runtimeEntitlementsFile` | `RegularFileProperty` | App and JVM runtime entitlements |
| `provisioningProfile`, `runtimeProvisioningProfile` | `RegularFileProperty` | |
| `macOsSdkVersion` | `String?` | Default `"26.0"`. `vtool` writes it into the launcher's `LC_BUILD_VERSION`, which gates Liquid Glass |
| `fileAssociation(mimeType, extension, description, iconFile?)` | | |
| `signing { }`, `notarization { }`, `dmg { }` | | See below |
| `pkg { }` | `PkgSettings` | See [`pkg { }`](#macos-pkg) |
| `appExtensions { }` | `MacAppExtensionSettings` | See [`appExtensions { }`](#macos-app-extensions) |
| `launchAgents { }` | `LaunchAgentSettings` | See [`launchAgents { }`](#macos-launch-agents) |
| `infoPlist { extraKeysRawXml }` | `InfoPlistSettings` | Extra keys, as raw XML, added to `Info.plist` |

`macOS.appStore` is deprecated at `ERROR` level and no longer compiles. The 2.x property was ignored (PKG always targeted the App Store), so it was not aliased. Set `macOS { pkg { appStore = … } }` after choosing the channel you want. See [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

### `pkg { }` [#macos-pkg]

`PkgSettings` picks the PKG distribution channel.

| Property | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `appStore` | `Boolean` | `true` | `true`: Mac App Store build, sandboxed, re-signed with `productsign`, not notarized. `false`: Developer ID build, same pipeline as DMG, installer signed with the Developer ID Installer certificate and notarized by `notarizePkg` |
| `preInstall` | `RegularFileProperty` | unset | Script run as root before the payload is copied. Needs a shebang |
| `postInstall` | `RegularFileProperty` | unset | Script run as root after the payload is copied |

The App Store rejects packages that carry install scripts, so the plugin fails configuration when `preInstall` or `postInstall` is set with `appStore = true`. Each script runs once per install.

```kotlin
macOS {
    pkg {
        appStore = false
        preInstall.set(file("packaging/macos/preinstall"))
        postInstall.set(file("packaging/macos/postinstall"))
    }
}
```

See [Choose a PKG channel](/docs/packaging/macos#choose-a-pkg-channel).

### `appExtensions { }` [#macos-app-extensions]

`MacAppExtensionSettings` embeds prebuilt `.appex` bundles in `Contents/PlugIns/`. Nucleus copies and signs them; it does not build them.

| Member | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `extension(name) { }` | Declares one `MacAppExtension`. `name` appears in diagnostics only |
| `appex(File)` | The `.appex` bundle to embed |
| `entitlements(File)` | Entitlements for the extension, separate from the app's |
| `provisioningProfile(File)` | Optional, embedded as `Contents/embedded.provisionprofile` inside the extension |

```kotlin
macOS {
    appExtensions {
        extension("NetworkFilter") {
            appex(file("build/appex/NetworkFilter.appex"))
            entitlements(file("packaging/extension/NetworkExtension.entitlements"))
            provisioningProfile(file("packaging/NetworkFilter.provisionprofile"))
        }
    }
}
```

Each extension is signed with its own entitlements, then the app is sealed without `--deep`. The extension exists only inside a signed `.app`: use `runDistributable`, not `run`. See [Embed app extensions](/docs/packaging/macos#embed-app-extensions).

### `signing { }` [#macos-signing]

`MacOSSigningSettings`: `sign: Property<Boolean>` (default `false`), `identity`, `keychain`, `prefix` (all `Property<String>`).

### `notarization { }` [#macos-notarization]

`MacOSNotarizationSettings` accepts one of three credential sets, all `Property<String>`:

- Apple ID: `appleID`, `password`, `teamID`
- `notarytool` keychain profile: `keychainProfile`, optional `keychainPath`
- App Store Connect API key: `apiKey`, `apiKeyId`, `apiIssuer`

`ascProvider` is deprecated at `ERROR` level; use `teamID`.

### `dmg { }` [#macos-dmg]

`DmgSettings`:

| Property | Type |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | `String?` |
| `iconSize`, `iconTextSize` | `Int?` |
| `format` | `DmgFormat?`: `UDRW`, `UDRO`, `UDCO`, `UDZO`, `UDBZ`, `ULFO` |
| `size` | `String?` |
| `shrink` | `Boolean?` |
| `sign` | `Boolean` (default `false`) |
| `background`, `icon`, `badgeIcon` | `RegularFileProperty` |
| `backgroundColor` | `String?` |
| `window { x; y; width; height }` | `Int?` each |
| `content(x, y, type?, name?, path?)` | `type` is `DmgContentType`: `Link`, `File`, `Dir` |

### `launchAgents { }` [#macos-launch-agents]

`agent(label) { }` declares a `LaunchAgentDefinition`, written to `<label>.plist`:

| Member | Notes |
| --- | --- |

| `arguments(vararg)` | |
| `startInterval(seconds)` | |
| `runAtLoad(enabled = true)` | Run when launchd loads the agent |
| `keepAlive(enabled = true)` | Restart the agent when it exits |
| `processType(type)` | `Background` (default), `Standard`, `Adaptive` |
| `calendar { month; day; weekday; hour; minute }` | `CalendarInterval`, `Int?` each |

### `toolchain { }` [#graalvm-toolchain]

| Property | Type | Default | Notes |

## `nativeApplication { }` [#native-application]

`NativeApplication` packages a Kotlin/Native app. Only macOS targets are supported.

- `targets(vararg KotlinTarget)`: each must be a `KotlinNativeTarget` of `Family.OSX`.
- `distributions { }`: `NativeApplicationDistributions`, with the [shared metadata](#shared-metadata) and a `macOS { }` block limited to the `AbstractMacOSPlatformSettings` members (no `pkg`, `appExtensions`, `launchAgents` or entitlements).

## Other types [#other-types]

| Type | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `CompressionLevel` | `Store`, `Normal`, `Maximum`, `Ultra` |
| `GarbageCollector` | `SERIAL`, `PARALLEL`, `G1`, `Z`, `SHENANDOAH`, `EPSILON` |
| `NativeImageGarbageCollector` | `SERIAL`, `G1`, `EPSILON` |
| `NativeImageMarch` | `NATIVE`, `COMPATIBILITY` |
| `NativeImageOptimization` | `QUICK_BUILD`, `NONE`, `LEVEL_1`, `LEVEL_2`, `LEVEL_3`, `SIZE` |
| `GraalvmChannel` | `INNOVATION` (`25i4`), `LTS` (`25`) |
| `GraalvmDistribution` | `COMMUNITY`, `ORACLE` |
| `ExactReachabilityMetadata` | `OFF`, `APP_PACKAGES`, `packages(...)` |
| `AotCacheCompatibility` | `COMPATIBILITY`, `NATIVE` |
| `PackagingBackend` | `JPACKAGE`, `ELECTRON_BUILDER` (`TargetFormat.backend`) |
| `UrlProtocol` | `data class UrlProtocol(name, schemes: List<String>)` |

`@ExperimentalNucleusLibrary` marks unstable members of `nucleus.dependencies`.

## Generated app properties [#app-properties]

The plugin writes `nucleus/nucleus-app.properties` into the app resources. The `NucleusApp` runtime object reads it at startup, which is how DSL values reach the runtime libraries. Keys: `app.id`, `app.version`, `app.vendor`, `app.description`, `app.name`, `app.aumid`, `startup.wm.class`, `startup.task.id`, and `optimization.idleGc` when the `idleGc` knob is on.

- [macOS packaging](/docs/packaging/macos): PKG channels and app extensions.
- [Packaging](/docs/packaging): what each `TargetFormat` produces.

# Troubleshooting

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/reference/troubleshooting

Common build, packaging, signing, and runtime problems in Nucleus, with the cause and fix for each.

This page lists recurring problems when you build, package, sign, and run a Nucleus app.
Entries are grouped by area, and each one gives the symptom, the cause, and the fix.

## macOS signing and notarization

### Notarization fails: "does not include a secure timestamp"

**Symptom.** `xcrun notarytool submit` returns `Invalid` with a status detail about a
missing or invalid timestamp.

**Cause.** Code signing ran without `--timestamp`, or the machine could not reach Apple's
timestamp server at sign time.

**Fix.** Nucleus signs with `--options runtime --timestamp` by default. If you added a
custom `codesign` step (for example, to sign `lipo`-merged universal binaries outside the
`build-macos-universal` action), pass `--timestamp` and re-sign. Verify with
`codesign -dv --verbose=4 <Your.app>` and check for a `Timestamp=` entry.

### Notarization fails: "does not include a hardened runtime"

**Symptom.** `Status: Invalid`, with the log referencing the hardened runtime.

**Cause.** A custom `codesign` step is missing `--options runtime`.

**Fix.** Add `--options runtime` to every `codesign` invocation. The default Nucleus
pipeline already does this, so only custom CI scripts hit this error.

### Notarization fails: "code object is not signed at all"

**Symptom.** `packageGraalvmDmg` (or `notarizeGraalvmDmg`) with
`compose.desktop.mac.sign=true` aborts with
`code object is not signed at all` in subcomponent
`<App>.app/Contents/MacOS/.nucleus-executable-type`. Or the bundle notarizes, but
`spctl -a -t exec` answers a bare `rejected`.

**Cause.** Before 2.5.17, GraalVM bundles put non-code files under `Contents/MacOS/`: the
executable-type marker and `lib/fontconfig.bfc`. `codesign` treats every file there as
nested code, and Gatekeeper rejects non-Mach-O files anywhere under `Contents/MacOS/`. The
GraalVM dylibs there also kept their ad-hoc signature.

**Fix.** Upgrade to 2.5.17 or later. The marker and `fontconfig.bfc` now live in
`Contents/Resources/`, and every dylib under `Contents/MacOS/` is re-signed with your
Developer ID. Files you add through `appResourcesRootDir` still land in `Contents/MacOS/`
on macOS. Ship only Mach-O binaries there, or Gatekeeper rejects the notarized bundle the
same way.

## Microsoft Store

### Upload rejected: "MinVersion &lt;= 10.0.17134.0"

**Symptom.** Partner Center rejects the upload:

> Package acceptance validation error: bundle is not valid. You can't upload
> msix/msixbundle/msixupload packages that target Windows with a
> MinVersion &lt;= 10.0.17134.0.

**Cause.** No explicit `minVersion` is set in `appx { }`. The default is `10.0.14316.0`,
which is below the Store's floor.

**Fix.** Set a `minVersion` at or above the Store's floor:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
appx {
    minVersion = "10.0.17763.0"        // Windows 10 1809
    maxVersionTested = "10.0.22621.0"  // Windows 11 22H2
}
```

### Upload rejected: publisher or identity mismatch

**Symptom.** Upload validation fails with an identity mismatch.

**Cause.** `identityName`, `publisher`, or `publisherDisplayName` do not match the Partner
Center reservation.

**Fix.** Copy the exact values from Partner Center under Product identity. `publisher` is
the `CN=<GUID>` issued by the Store, not the CN of your local signing certificate. See
[Windows targets](/docs/packaging/windows).

## Networking

### SSLHandshakeException on a corporate network

**Symptom.** HTTPS calls from the app fail with
`SSLHandshakeException: PKIX path building failed`.

**Cause.** A corporate proxy or VPN gateway intercepts TLS with a private root CA that the
bundled JDK trust store does not know.

**Fix.** Use either approach, or both.

Ship the CA inside the bundled JDK's `cacerts` at build time:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
nativeDistributions {
    trustedCertificates.from(files("certs/corp-ca.pem"))
}
```

See [trusted certificates](/docs/packaging/trusted-certificates).

Or route HTTPS through the OS trust store at runtime with `native-ssl` and `native-http`:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.native-ssl:<version>")
implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.native-http:<version>")
```

`NativeHttpClient.create()` returns a `java.net.http.HttpClient` backed by the OS trust
store. For OkHttp or Ktor, use the `nucleus.native-http-okhttp` and
`nucleus.native-http-ktor` integrations.

## Auto-update

### "no matching file" on macOS

**Symptom.** A check returns `UpdateResult.Error` wrapping a `NoMatchingFileException` on
macOS.

**Cause.** The release contains only a `.dmg`. Auto-update on macOS downloads a ZIP.

**Fix.** Add `TargetFormat.Zip` alongside `TargetFormat.Dmg`. Both belong in the same
release, and `latest-mac.yml` references both. See [auto-update](/docs/packaging/auto-update).

## GraalVM native image

### ClassNotFoundException or NoSuchMethodError at runtime

**Symptom.** The app runs on the JVM but crashes under `native-image` with reflection
errors or missing methods.

**Cause.** GraalVM uses closed-world analysis. Reflection, resources, and dynamic proxies
must be registered ahead of time.

**Fix.** The Nucleus plugin ships GraalVM reachability metadata for itself, FileKit, and
other common libraries (see [automatic metadata](/docs/performance/graalvm/automatic-metadata)).
For your own code:

1. Run with `-agentlib:native-image-agent=config-output-dir=...` on a representative
   workload.
2. Commit the generated `reachability-metadata.json` next to `META-INF/native-image/`.

For unsupported libraries, see [GraalVM configuration](/docs/performance/graalvm/configuration).

## Packaging

### Node.js download fails during packaging

**Symptom.** A `package*` task logs `Could not provision Node.js (…) — falling back to the one on
PATH`, then fails with `node not found. Node.js 18+ is required for electron-builder packaging`.

**Cause.** electron-builder runs on Node.js, and the plugin downloads one from `nodejs.org` on
first use. The build host is offline or a proxy blocks the download, and no `node` sits on `PATH`
either. The plugin picks Node.js in this order:

1. The `compose.electronBuilder.nodePath` Gradle property (the `node` binary or its directory).
2. The `NUCLEUS_NODE_HOME` environment variable.
3. The installation the plugin provisions from `nativeDistributions { nodejs { } }`.
4. `node` on `PATH`, used when `autoDownload` is `false` or the download fails.

**Fix.** Point the plugin at a local install with the Gradle property or `NUCLEUS_NODE_HOME`. To
use the `node` on `PATH` and skip the download attempt, turn provisioning off:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
nativeDistributions {
    nodejs {
        autoDownload = false
    }
}
```

See [Provision Node.js](/docs/packaging#provision-nodejs).

## Linux packaging

### AppImage takes about 60 seconds to start

**Symptom.** The app opens quickly in development but takes about a minute when packaged
as an AppImage.

**Cause.** `compressionLevel = CompressionLevel.Maximum` or `Ultra`. AppImage uses squashfs,
and maximum compression triggers FUSE decompression on every launch.

**Fix.** Use `CompressionLevel.Normal` (the default) for AppImage. Prefer a format-local
override so DEB/DMG can stay on a higher global level:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
nativeDistributions {
    compressionLevel = CompressionLevel.Ultra
    linux {
        appImage {
            compressionLevel = CompressionLevel.Normal
        }
    }
}
```

### DEB or RPM fails: "Please specify project homepage"

**Symptom.** `packageDeb` or `packageGraalvmDeb` fails immediately.

**Cause.** Unlike jpackage, electron-builder requires `homepage` for DEB.

**Fix.** Set the homepage on the distribution:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
nativeDistributions {
    homepage = "https://myapp.example.com"
}
```

### Flatpak task skips silently

**Symptom.** `packageFlatpak` reports "skipped" with no error.

**Cause.** `flatpak-builder` or the `org.freedesktop.Platform//23.08` runtime is missing
on the build host.

**Fix.** Install the tooling and runtime:

```shell
sudo apt-get install -y flatpak flatpak-builder
flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists flathub https://flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo
flatpak install -y flathub org.freedesktop.Platform//23.08
flatpak install -y flathub org.freedesktop.Sdk//23.08
```

In CI, use `setup-nucleus` with `flatpak: 'true'`.

### Snap fails: "snapcraft: command not found"

**Symptom.** `packageSnap` fails before producing anything.

**Cause.** `snapd` or `snapcraft` is missing on the build host.

**Fix.** Install both:

```shell
sudo apt-get install -y snapd
sudo snap install snapcraft --classic
```

In CI, use `setup-nucleus` with `snap: 'true'`.

## Native libraries

### Module reports `isAvailable == false` or silent no-ops

**Symptom.** System tray, system color, notifications, or another OS-integration module
does nothing on a platform where you expect it to work. Public APIs return `null` /
`false`, or `isAvailable` is `false`.

**Cause.** The JNI shared library for that module did not load. Common reasons: no binary
for this OS/arch in the dependency JAR, the module is missing from the runtime classpath,
or extraction into the content-addressed cache failed.

**Fix.** Confirm the module dependency is on the runtime classpath and that the JAR
contains `/nucleus/native/<os>-<arch>/…` for your platform. Clear the loader cache and
relaunch if an upgrade left a partial extract:

| Platform | Cache path |
|----------|------------|
| macOS | `~/Library/Caches/nucleus/native/` |
| Linux | `~/.cache/nucleus/native/` (or `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/nucleus/native/`) |
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\nucleus\native\` |

See [Native library loader](/docs/performance/native-library-loader) for the full load
order, JAR layout, and sidecar rules.

### Native library fails to load on an older Linux distribution

**Symptom.** On Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Devuan 5, or another distribution older than
Ubuntu 24.04, the app crashes at launch or a module reports `isAvailable == false`. stderr
shows `version 'GLIBC_2.3x' not found` for a `libnucleus_*.so` library.

**Cause.** Up to 2.5.17 the Linux natives were built on `ubuntu-latest` (Ubuntu 24.04), so
they required glibc 2.39.

**Fix.** Upgrade to 2.5.18 or later. The natives are built on Ubuntu 22.04 and need
glibc 2.35 or newer. Check your system's version with `ldd --version`.

## Rendering

### Crash on launch with an older Linux GPU

**Symptom.** A window aborts at open on Linux. stderr mentions a failed GL 3.3 context, or the
process exits from `TaoComposeSceneHostLinux` with a `require()` failure.

**Cause.** Before 2.5.16, the Linux EGL attach requested only a GL 3.3 **compatibility**
profile. Some drivers (Mesa r600 on AMD RV610, for example) cap the compat profile at 3.0 while
the **core** profile reaches 3.3. The request could never succeed, and the window aborted.

**Fix.** Upgrade to 2.5.16 or later. Attach tries 3.3 compat, then 3.3 core, then Mesa llvmpipe
(`LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`, once, skipped if you already set that variable). Each fallback logs
one line on stderr. Hardware that accepts the compat request behaves as before. Set
`LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` yourself to force llvmpipe from the start.

## Event loop

### Window hangs and the log shows a thread dump

**Symptom.** On Windows, a window turns to "Not responding", and the log holds a `SEVERE` entry:
`Tao event loop has not pumped messages for at least <n> ms — the UI is frozen. Thread dump
follows.`

**Cause.** The UI thread is blocked. A deadlock or long synchronous work keeps the event loop
from pumping messages. The event-loop watchdog detects it and dumps every thread, event-loop
thread first.

**Fix.** Read the event-loop thread's stack at the top of the dump and move the blocking call
off the UI thread. For work that has to stay there, wrap it in `expectUnresponsive { }` so the
watchdog ignores it. Register `onUnresponsive` to report hangs from the field. See
[Detect a stalled event loop](/docs/concepts/threading#detect-a-stalled-event-loop).

## Input

### Custom scroll handler ignores the macOS trackpad

**Symptom.** On macOS, a `pointerInput` handler that reacts to `PointerEventType.Scroll` works
with a mouse wheel but not with a two-finger trackpad swipe. `LazyColumn` and
`Modifier.scrollable` still scroll.

A trackpad swipe on macOS now arrives as `PanStart`, `PanMove`, and `PanEnd`. In 2.x it arrived
as `Scroll`. See [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

**Cause.** Your handler listens only for `Scroll`, so it never sees the pan events.

**Fix.** Handle `PointerEventType.PanMove` and read `change.panOffset` next to your `Scroll`
branch. To get every trackpad step back as `Scroll`, start the JVM with
`-Dnucleus.tao.trackpadPanEvents=false`. See
[Scroll with a trackpad on macOS](/docs/input/trackpad-gestures#scroll).

### Pinch no longer reaches detectTransformGestures

**Symptom.** A trackpad pinch no longer zooms content that uses `detectTransformGestures`.

A pinch now reaches Compose as `ScaleStart`, `ScaleChange`, and `ScaleEnd`. In 2.x it was two
synthetic touch pointers. See [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

**Cause.** `detectTransformGestures` tracks touch pointers and does not see Scale events.

**Fix.** Move pinch handling to `Modifier.transformable` or to a listener for the `Scale*`
events. See [Zoom with a pinch](/docs/input/trackpad-gestures#zoom-with-a-pinch).

## Application lifecycle

### Cmd+Q no longer quits the app

**Symptom.** On macOS, Cmd+Q, Dock → Quit, or a logout leaves the app running.

A system quit on macOS now calls `onCloseRequest` on every open window. In 2.x it terminated the
app without asking. See [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

**Cause.** One of your windows has an `onCloseRequest` that neither calls `exitApplication()`
nor closes the window, for example one that hides the window to the tray. A window that stays
open vetoes the quit.

**Fix.** Let a real quit through. Check `isQuitting` on the application scope:

```kotlin
DecoratedWindow(
    onCloseRequest = {
        if (isQuitting) exitApplication() else visible = false
    },
    visible = visible,
) { /* ... */ }
```

See [Handle a system quit](/docs/lifecycle/application#handle-a-system-quit).

### Second instance is not forwarded in dev runs

**Symptom.** Under `./gradlew run` or an IDE launch, a second copy starts its own window instead
of handing its arguments to the first one.

`enableSingleInstance` now defaults to `!ExecutableRuntime.isDev()`. In 2.x it was on in dev
runs too. See [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

**Cause.** The single-instance lock is off in dev runs, so a debug copy can start next to a
packaged one.

**Fix.** Pass `enableSingleInstance = true` to `nucleusApplication` while you test the hand-off.
See [Enable it in dev runs](/docs/lifecycle/single-instance#enable-it-in-dev-runs).

## Development

### Hot Reload window does not open on macOS

**Symptom.** A Compose Hot Reload run on macOS starts the process, but no window appears.
`./gradlew run` works.

**Cause.** The window event loop must run on macOS thread 0, and Hot Reload's `JavaExec` task
does not pass `-XstartOnFirstThread`. The Nucleus plugin adds the flag, but only when the
project declares `nucleus.decorated-window-tao` itself. An app that gets it through
`nucleus-application` has it only as a transitive dependency, so the plugin skips the flag.

**Fix.** Declare the dependency explicitly:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
implementation("dev.nucleusframework:nucleus.decorated-window-tao:<version>")
```

## Migration

### Unresolved reference: NucleusBackend

**Symptom.** After an upgrade to 3.0, compilation fails on `NucleusBackend`,
`LocalNucleusBackend`, or the `backend =` argument of `nucleusApplication`.

**Cause.** 3.0 has a single window backend. The AWT, JBR, and JNI window modules are deleted,
and the backend selection API went with them.

**Fix.** Drop the `NucleusBackend` import, the `backend` argument, and the
`decorated-window-awt`, `-jbr`, or `-jni` dependency. See
[Remove the backend selection](/docs/migrate/from-2.x#remove-the-backend-selection).

### Unresolved reference 'JewelDecoratedWindow'

**Symptom.** The import is correct and the IDE resolves the function, but compilation fails.

**Cause.** `JewelDecoratedWindow` is an extension on `NucleusApplicationScope`. A wrapper
composable without that receiver cannot call it.

**Fix.** Make your wrapper an extension as well:

```kotlin
@Composable
fun NucleusApplicationScope.MyOnboardingWindow() {
    JewelDecoratedWindow(/* ... */) { /* content */ }
}
```

See [Migrate from 1.x](/docs/migrate/from-1.x).

### Jewel dependency fails to resolve on an older JDK

**Symptom.** Gradle refuses the `nucleus.decorated-window-jewel` artifact with a message about
an incompatible Java version.

**Cause.** The Jewel toolkit is compiled for JDK 25, and your build targets an older one.

**Fix.** Set the Kotlin JVM toolchain to 25:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
kotlin { jvmToolchain(25) }
```

See [Install](/docs/start/install).

- [Migrate from 2.x](/docs/migrate/from-2.x): every breaking change in 3.0 and how to adapt.
- [Threading](/docs/concepts/threading): the UI thread, native callbacks, and the watchdog.
- [Packaging](/docs/packaging): per-OS packaging, signing, and store targets.
- [Performance](/docs/performance): GraalVM native image and AOT details.

# Roadmap

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/roadmap

Planned Nucleus modules, APIs still experimental, work that waits on upstream projects, and features under consideration.

This page lists work that has not shipped yet. For what each release contains, see the
[changelog](/docs/changelog). To upgrade to 3.0, follow
[Migrate from Nucleus 2.x to 3.0](/docs/migrate/from-2.x).

## Stabilize the multi-window APIs

Satellites, `DockLayout`, and the tab workspace are `@ExperimentalNucleusApi` in 3.0, and their
surface may change without a deprecation cycle. The opt-in goes away once the API holds across
real apps. See [Multi-window](/docs/multi-window).

## Planned modules

| Module | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `secure-storage` | Hardware-backed storage for tokens, passwords and keys |
| `biometric-auth` | Fingerprint or face authentication prompt (Touch ID, Windows Hello, `fprintd`) |
| `share-sheet` | OS share sheet for URLs, files and text |
| `power-events` | Sleep, wake, lock, unlock, screen off, battery state |

## Waiting on upstream

- **Compose window API v2 types.** Nucleus ships an AWT-free copy in
  `dev.nucleusframework.window.tao.v2`. If JetBrains decouples the upstream types from AWT, you
  will import those instead.
- **Pinch and rotation in Compose gestures.** In Compose 1.12, `detectTransformGestures` does not
  see `Scale` events, and Compose has no rotation event.
- **Tao updates.** Fixes from Tao releases after 0.35 reach Nucleus by hand.

## Under consideration

No commitment and no date. Open an issue if you need one of these:

| Module | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `clipboard` | HTML and RTF clipboard flavors and a change watcher. Text, images and file lists already work, see [Linux and Wayland](/docs/windows/linux-wayland). |
| `screen-capture` | Screenshots and screen recording |

## Influence the order

Open an issue that describes your use case, link a sample app that needs the module, or sponsor
the implementation for one platform. The modules more people ask for ship first.

## What's next

- [Changelog](/docs/changelog): released versions and their contents.
- [Modules](/docs/concepts/modules): the modules available today.
- [Migrate from Nucleus 2.x to 3.0](/docs/migrate/from-2.x): upgrade to the latest release.
