# Changelog

URL: https://nucleusframework.dev/en/docs/changelog

Release notes for every Nucleus release, newest first.

This page lists the changes in each Nucleus release, newest first. Every entry records
the new modules, features, bug fixes, and breaking changes in that version.

## v3.0.0

**Released: TBD**

Nucleus 3.0 keeps one window backend, Tao, and removes the AWT, JBR and JNI window modules.
The major version marks the API breaks: read the
[migration guide](/docs/migrate/from-2.x) before you upgrade, and work through its checklist.

### Breaking changes

- **Tao is the only window backend** (#593). `decorated-window-awt`, `decorated-window-jbr` and
  `decorated-window-jni` are gone, along with `NucleusBackend`, `LocalNucleusBackend`,
  `nucleusApplication(backend = …)` and `NucleusApplicationScope.backend`.
  `nucleus-application` now brings `decorated-window-tao` itself. See
  [Remove the backend selection](/docs/migrate/from-2.x#remove-the-backend-selection).
- **No AWT windows** (#593). Compose Desktop's `Window`, `Dialog` and `Tray` are unsupported,
  `NucleusWindowUnsafe.awtWindow` / `awtDialog` are removed, and the receiver-less AWT overloads
  of `MaterialDecoratedWindow`, `MaterialDecoratedDialog`, `JewelDecoratedWindow` and
  `JewelDecoratedDialog` are gone. See
  [Replace Compose Desktop windows, dialogs and tray](/docs/migrate/from-2.x#replace-compose-desktop-windows-dialogs-and-tray)
  and [toolkit windows](/docs/toolkits#open-a-toolkit-window).
- **Window API v2 lives in a Nucleus package** (#634). Import
  `dev.nucleusframework.window.tao.v2` instead of `androidx.compose.ui.window.v2`; Nucleus
  accepts none of Compose's v2 types. See [Window state](/docs/windows/window-state#use-the-window-api-v2).
- **`NucleusWindowHost.Window` takes `minimizable` and `maximizable`** (#680, #684). Custom
  hosts must add both parameters. See
  [Update custom window hosts](/docs/migrate/from-2.x#update-custom-window-hosts).
- **PKG store flags fail to compile** (#688). `macOS.appStore` and `TargetFormat.isStoreFormat`
  are deprecated at ERROR. Pick the channel with `macOS { pkg { appStore = … } }` and detect the
  sandbox with `ExecutableRuntime.isSandboxed()`. See
  [Choose a PKG channel](/docs/packaging/macos#choose-a-pkg-channel).

### Behavior changes

- **Cmd+Q and Dock → Quit call `onCloseRequest`** (#696). Every open window gets the request,
  so a handler that never exits vetoes the quit. See
  [Handle a system quit](/docs/lifecycle/application#handle-a-system-quit).
- **Native callbacks run on the host UI thread** (#687). Notifications, media controls and the
  launchers post through the new `NucleusUiThread` instead of the AWT EDT. See
  [Native callbacks on the UI thread](/docs/concepts/threading#native-callbacks-on-the-ui-thread).
- **Pinch arrives as Compose `Scale` events** (#662). `detectTransformGestures` no longer sees
  it; use `Modifier.transformable` or a `PointerEventType.Scale*` listener. See
  [Zoom with a pinch](/docs/input/trackpad-gestures#zoom-with-a-pinch).
- **Single instance is off in dev runs** (#717). `enableSingleInstance` defaults to
  `!ExecutableRuntime.isDev()`. See
  [Enable it in dev runs](/docs/lifecycle/single-instance#enable-it-in-dev-runs).
- **FileKit is initialized for you** (#718) with `NucleusApp.appId` when it is on the classpath.
  Opt out with `initializeFileKit = false`. See
  [Initialize FileKit](/docs/lifecycle/application#initialize-filekit).
- **LCD / ClearType text on Windows** (#626). Opaque windows render subpixel text by default.
  See [Render ClearType text on Windows](/docs/windows/hidpi#render-cleartype-text-on-windows).
- **JRE fonts are stripped from the runtime image** (#694). Apps that draw text through AWT or
  Swing set `stripJreFonts = false`. See
  [Trim the runtime image](/docs/packaging#trim-the-runtime-image).
- **Nucleus JNI libraries ship next to the app** (#712) instead of inside its JARs, and
  packaged apps extract nothing on first launch. See
  [Native libraries next to the app](/docs/packaging#native-libraries-next-to-the-app).
- **No system-theme polling** (#716). `nucleusApplication` turns off Compose's once-a-second
  theme poll and serves `LocalSystemTheme` from its own detector. See
  [Dark mode](/docs/os/theme/dark-mode#how-nucleusapplication-provides-the-theme).

### New features

- **Satellite windows and docking** (#635, #663, #695, `@ExperimentalNucleusApi`). Palettes
  follow the focused document, dock into a `DockLayout` and float back out. Split or layered
  sides, per-panel sizes, `dockSides`, `floatable`, `reorderable` and extent limits. See
  [Satellites](/docs/multi-window/satellites) and [Docking](/docs/multi-window/docking).
- **Chrome-like tabs** (#635, #663, #695, `@ExperimentalNucleusApi`). `Tab` and `TabWindows`
  tear tabs off into new windows and merge them back, with custom previews and RTL strips. See
  [Tabs](/docs/multi-window/tabs).
- **Window API v2** (#634, #647, #674, #675). `WindowState` / `DialogState` with
  `requestSize`, `requestScreen`, `TaoMonitors`, and wrap-content windows centred once measured.
  See [Window state](/docs/windows/window-state).
- **`minimizable` and `maximizable`** (#680, #684) on `DecoratedWindow` and `HostedWindow`, for
  close-only windows. See [Set the window chrome](/docs/windows#set-the-window-chrome).
- **`exitProcessOnExit`** (#676) on `nucleusApplication`. See
  [Choose what happens on exit](/docs/lifecycle/application#choose-what-happens-on-exit).
- **Event-loop watchdog on Windows** (#710). A hung loop logs `SEVERE` with a thread dump;
  hook `onUnresponsive`, `onResponsive` and `expectUnresponsive`. See
  [Detect a stalled event loop](/docs/concepts/threading#detect-a-stalled-event-loop).
- **Popup layers placed against the screen** (#651) and `NativePopupLayers { }` for one
  subtree. See [Dialogs and popups](/docs/windows/dialogs-popups#how-popups-meet-the-screen).
- **`TaoPointerIcons`** for Grab, Move, NotAllowed, Wait and the resize cursors. See
  [Pointer icons](/docs/input/pointer-icons#available-icons).
- **Startup pack** (#639, #669, #715). `nucleusOptimization` turns on Serial GC, a compact
  heap, a single JAR, idle GC and `lastJdk` (OpenJDK 27). See [Startup](/docs/performance/startup).
- **Node.js provisioning** (#709, #711). The plugin downloads Node.js for electron-builder
  (now 26.16.1); CI drops `setup-node`. See [Provision Node.js](/docs/packaging#provision-nodejs).
- **macOS app extensions** (#396). Embed and sign prebuilt `.appex` bundles. See
  [Embed app extensions](/docs/packaging/macos#embed-app-extensions).
- **Developer ID PKG with install scripts** (#688). See
  [Package a Developer ID PKG](/docs/packaging/macos#package-a-developer-id-pkg).
- **Native library cache directory** (#686). `-Dnucleus.native.cacheDir` or
  `NativeLibraryLoader.cacheDirectory`. See
  [Relocate the cache](/docs/performance/native-library-loader#relocate-the-cache).
- **GraalVM 25i4 by default** (#698) and **G1 in native images on Windows and macOS** (#708)
  from GraalVM 25.4. See
  [Choose a garbage collector](/docs/performance/graalvm/configuration#choose-a-garbage-collector).
- **ANGLE from Maven, D3D11 only** (#707). See
  [Ship the ANGLE libraries](/docs/packaging/windows#ship-the-angle-libraries).

### Bug fixes

- **App Store PKG is no longer notarized** (#681).
- **`jdk.jlink` is filtered out of `includeAllModules`** (#682) on JEP 493 JDKs.
- **`FsWatcher` shares one native watcher per instance** (#683) and reports macOS renames as
  `Moved`. See [Handle renames](/docs/lifecycle/fs-watcher#handle-renames).
- **NSIS** (#718): `deleteAppDataOnUninstall` covers custom GraalVM image names, a
  `packageName` change reaches the installer, and repackaging no longer fails on the read-only
  launcher. See [Customize the NSIS installer](/docs/packaging/windows#customize-the-nsis-installer).
- **Resize without trembling** on macOS, Windows and Linux (#678, #689, #691, #693, #704).
- **Context menu flyouts** (#651): on Linux the menu maps as an `xdg_popup`, and a second right
  click moves it. See [Context menus](/docs/os/menus/context-menu#how-the-flyout-behaves-on-screen).
- **JNI exceptions are logged before they are cleared** (#677).
- **Window content stays on the UI applier** (#649) when a non-UI composable runs in the
  `nucleusApplication` scope.
- **NativeView and TextureView embed fixes** (#659) on all three OSes.
- **Linux: closed windows no longer stay mapped** after `nucleusApplication` returns (#714).

---

## v2.5.18

**Released: 2026-09-23**

### Bug fixes

- **Linux natives require glibc 2.39** (#699) — the Linux JNI libraries (Tao, decorated
  window, notifications, tray helpers, …) were built on `ubuntu-latest`, which GitHub moved
  to Ubuntu 24.04, so every published `.so` needed glibc 2.39 and failed to load on
  still-supported distributions such as Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (2.35), Debian 12, and Devuan 5
  (2.36). The native build is now pinned to `ubuntu-22.04` / `ubuntu-22.04-arm`, bringing
  the floor back to glibc 2.35. See
  [Native library fails to load on an older Linux distribution](/docs/reference/troubleshooting#native-library-fails-to-load-on-an-older-linux-distribution).

---

## v2.5.17

**Released: 2026-09-22**

### New features

- **Pacman upgrade hooks** (#685) — `linux { }` gains `afterUpgrade` and `beforeUpgrade`
  file properties, passed raw to fpm (`--after-upgrade` / `--before-upgrade`). On Pacman,
  an upgrade runs only `pre_upgrade` / `post_upgrade`: none of the four install/remove
  scripts fire, so a service set up in `afterInstall` died on the first upgrade. Register or
  restart it in `afterUpgrade` too. Deb and Rpm ignore both properties — their install
  scriptlets already run on upgrades. See
  [Add install and remove scripts](/docs/packaging/linux#add-install-and-remove-scripts).

### Bug fixes

- **Linux install directory no longer contains spaces** (#685) — Deb, Rpm, and Pacman
  installed the payload under `/opt/${sanitizedProductName}`, derived from `appName`.
  electron-builder's sanitizer keeps spaces, so a display name such as `My App` broke every
  unquoted path in install scripts and systemd `ExecStart=` lines. On Linux the product name
  now comes from `linux.packageName ?: packageName`, so the payload lands in
  `/opt/<packageName>`. Scripts that hardcode the old `/opt/<App Name>` path must be updated.
- **Developer ID signing of GraalVM macOS bundles** (#692) — `packageGraalvmDmg` with
  `compose.desktop.mac.sign=true` aborted with `code object is not signed at all` on
  `Contents/MacOS/.nucleus-executable-type`, and even a manually fixed bundle was rejected by
  Gatekeeper after notarization. Three fixes: the executable-type marker is written to
  `Contents/Resources/` (the runtime still reads the old location); every dylib and
  executable under `Contents/MacOS/` is re-signed with the Developer ID identity; and
  `fontconfig.bfc` moves from `Contents/MacOS/lib/` to `Contents/Resources/`, with
  `sun.awt.fontconfig` pointed at it at startup. JVM (jpackage) bundles are unaffected. See
  [Notarization fails: "code object is not signed at all"](/docs/reference/troubleshooting#notarization-fails-code-object-is-not-signed-at-all).

---

## v2.5.16

**Released: 2026-09-17**

### New features

- **Linux install and remove scripts** (#664) — `linux { }` now takes `afterInstall`,
  `afterRemove`, `beforeInstall`, and `beforeRemove` file properties. User after-scripts
  are concatenated after Nucleus's own template (desktop integration, AppArmor, optional
  polkit silent-update helper) and run through electron-builder for Deb, Rpm, and Pacman;
  before-scripts are passed raw to fpm (`--before-install` / `--before-remove`). GraalVM
  native-image packages honor the same four properties. electron-builder substitutes
  `${sanitizedProductName}` / `${executable}` only in single-quoted tokens; a double-quoted
  `"${executable}"` is left literal, so a systemd `systemctl enable "${executable}.service"`
  line silently no-ops. Pacman `pre_remove` does not get deb-style `$1=upgrade` — stop and
  disable the unit unconditionally and re-enable it in `afterInstall`. See
  [Add install and remove scripts](/docs/packaging/linux#add-install-and-remove-scripts).
- **Headless GraalVM images** (#665) — `graalvm { headless = true }` skips L3 AWT/Java2D
  platform metadata, the always-on L1 GUI packs (`jdk-awt`, `jdk-fonts`, `jdk-graphics2d`,
  Skiko/Compose/tray), and the companion GUI native libs (`libawt`, `libfontmanager`,
  Skiko, …), and bakes `-Djava.awt.headless=true`. Default is `false` (GUI). Without this,
  JNI registration of AWT types makes `native-image` pull `libawt` / `libawt_xawt` even
  when app code never references `java.awt`. Use it for daemons and CLIs. See
  [Build a headless image](/docs/performance/graalvm/configuration#build-a-headless-image).

### Bug fixes

- **Linux EGL crash on GPUs without GL 3.3 compatibility** (#670) — the X11 and Wayland
  attach paths asked for one thing only: a GL 3.3 compatibility-profile context. Mesa's
  r600 driver on AMD RV610 caps the compat profile at 3.0 (core reaches 3.3), so the
  request failed and the app aborted. Attach now tries 3.3 compat, then 3.3 core
  (hardware-accelerated on that GPU), then Mesa llvmpipe via `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`
  (Mesa reads that variable at `eglInitialize`, so the display is terminated and attach
  re-enters once). Existing hardware that accepts the compat request is untouched. Both
  fallbacks log one line on stderr. See
  [Crash on launch with an older Linux GPU](/docs/reference/troubleshooting#crash-on-launch-with-an-older-linux-gpu).

---

## v2.5.15

**Released: 2026-09-07**

### New features

- **Trackpad pan events on macOS** (#654) — two-finger trackpad gestures arrived as ordinary
  Compose `Scroll` events, indistinguishable from wheel notches, so a map could not bind panning
  to the trackpad and zoom to the wheel. Phased AppKit scroll steps now become
  `PointerEventType.PanStart` / `PanMove` / `PanEnd` with `panOffset` in pixels (AWT
  `preciseWheelRotation` × 10.dp). Wheel notches and phase-less precise scrolls stay `Scroll`.
  The pan stays open across AppKit's momentum tail so Compose does not stack its own fling.
  `Modifier.scrollable` handles both; a custom `pointerInput` that only listens for `Scroll`
  must also handle Pan, or start the process with `-Dnucleus.tao.trackpadPanEvents=false` to
  get AWT-style `Scroll` for everything. Native views consume the pan and forward it so the
  embedded scroll view rubber-bands; popups share the same router. See
  [Read trackpad pans from Compose](/docs/input/trackpad-gestures#scroll).

### Bug fixes

- **Horizontal trackpad scroll reversed on macOS** (#652) — tao negated `scrollingDeltaX` in
  the macOS `scroll_wheel` handler, then Nucleus negated both axes assuming raw AppKit deltas,
  so a two-finger swipe left panned the wrong way relative to AWT. AppKit already follows the
  `MouseScrollDelta` convention (as winit does); the extra X negation is gone, and popup
  conversion flips both axes without a second guess. See
  [Read trackpad pans from Compose](/docs/input/trackpad-gestures#scroll).
- **Trackpad scroll magnitude included display scale** (#653) — Tao converted AppKit logical
  deltas to physical pixels before dividing by 10, so a 10-point swipe moved twice as far on a
  2× display as under AWT (which uses `scrollingDelta * 0.1` with no scale). Precise deltas are
  now handed over in logical points. See
  [How it works](/docs/input/trackpad-gestures).

---

## v2.5.14

**Released: 2026-09-04**

### Bug fixes

- **Window content reclassified by a non-UI composable** (#636) — the window and dialog
  openers had their composition target inferred, so a single unmarked factory called in the
  `nucleusApplication` block (the Compose compiler bakes `@ComposableTarget` onto any unmarked
  function that forwards a target-marked content lambda) reclassified the whole scope — nested
  windows included — and every `@UiComposable` call in it warned, which is fatal under
  `-Werror`. The reported case was MapLibre Compose's `rememberMapState`. Each opener is now
  `@ComposableOpenTarget(-1)` with a `@UiComposable` content lambda, matching Compose Desktop's
  `Window`/`Dialog`: callable from any applier, always composing UI in the new window's own
  composition. Covers `DecoratedWindow`/`DecoratedDialog`, `NucleusWindowHost` /
  `NucleusDialogHost`, `HostedWindow`/`HostedDialog`, and Tao's `DecoratedWindow`,
  `DecoratedDialog`, and `TaoStandalonePopup`. The Material/Jewel wrappers inherit the same
  scheme through inference. See [Notes](/docs/windows#notes).

---

## v2.5.13

**Released: 2026-09-04**

### Bug fixes

- **Windows freeze on IME commit and taskbar restart** (#644) — two more instances of the
  #640 lock class: the window-state lock was held across `ImeHandler::process_message`, which
  peeks the queue on `WM_IME_ENDCOMPOSITION` (the Korean IME sends the committed string after
  the end message, so the queue decides whether to defer), and across `set_skip_taskbar` on
  `TaskbarCreated`, where the `CoCreateInstance` + `ITaskbarList` STA call pumps the queue
  while it waits. Both re-entered the window procedure and re-locked a non-reentrant mutex,
  parking the event-loop thread in `WaitOnAddress` for good. The IME commit-pending flag is
  now computed before the lock is taken and passed in, and the skip-taskbar flag is read out
  before the COM call. Wider blast radius than #640: nearly every IME arm took that lock.
  Ported from tauri-apps/tao#1215 and #1264. See
  [Text input](/docs/windows#text-input).
- **Windows freeze on a keyboard-triggered nested message** (#640) — `PeekMessageW` delivers
  pending cross-thread *sent* messages inline, re-entering the window procedure before the
  peek returns. The keyboard callback held the global `KEY_EVENT_BUILDERS` map and the
  key-press/release arms held `LAYOUT_CACHE` across such a peek, so the nested dispatch
  deadlocked the event-loop thread against itself and the window stayed "Not Responding".
  Reported as a freeze when moving a window between Windows 11 virtual desktops. The builder
  is now taken out of the map for the duration and put back only if the slot still exists, and
  the layout-cache guard ends before the peek. Only injected or sent key messages can nest
  here, and they are now dropped instead of hanging the process.

---

## v2.5.12

**Released: 2026-09-01**

### Bug fixes

- **`alwaysOnTop` dropped on Windows** (#631) — three layers lost `WS_EX_TOPMOST`:
  `DecoratedWindowComposable` created every window with a hardcoded `alwaysOnTop = false` and
  applied the real value from a later `LaunchedEffect`, losing the race against creation-time
  style rewrites (acrylic, skip-taskbar); tao only issues its z-order `SetWindowPos` on a
  `WindowFlags` cache diff, and asynchronously, so an external rewrite that dropped the
  topmost band was never repaired. The initial value is now passed at window creation,
  `setAlwaysOnTop` also applies the z-order synchronously, and the band is re-asserted after
  the known clobber sites — every resize, and the backdrop apply, teardown, and
  survivor-restore paths. See
  [Platform behavior](/docs/windows/overlay-windows#platform-behavior).
- **Input starving with two windows open on Windows** (#632) — any snapshot write in the
  process wakes every scene's `Recomposer` through the global apply observer, and the Windows
  host rendered and presented those frames unconditionally. Each `eglSwapBuffers` at interval
  1 parks the shared event-loop thread until the next VBlank, so every visible window
  re-presented at the animating window's rate and the VBlank waits serialized (a dashboard
  lagging while a small always-on-top window was visible). The scene bundle now tracks a
  visual-dirty flag fed by its `invalidateLayout` / `invalidateDraw` callbacks and the host
  skips the present for a frame with no visual change. Presents that must swap regardless are
  kept: a size or scale apply, the OS modal resize/move loop, a resolved clear-colour change,
  and the first swap after `show()`. See
  [How it works](/docs/windows).

---

## v2.5.11

**Released: 2026-08-31**

### New features

- **`menuCategory` and `shortcutName` on the NSIS targets** (#630) — follow-up to #629. The
  NSIS targets exposed most installer settings but not these two, so a start-menu group could
  not be declared at all and the shortcut always landed in the start menu root — a blocker for
  projects moving their MSI packaging to the recommended NSIS format while keeping the folder
  they had under jpackage. Both are emitted for `nsis` and `nsis-web`, default to `null`
  (nothing emitted, so existing installers are unchanged), and `windows.menuGroup` acts as the
  default `menuCategory` exactly as it does for MSI. See
  [Customize the NSIS installer](/docs/packaging/windows#customize-the-nsis-installer).

---

## v2.5.10

**Released: 2026-08-31**

### Bug fixes

- **MSI installer options** (#629) — the MSI target only forwarded `upgradeCode` and
  `perMachine` to electron-builder, so every other Windows installer setting fell back to
  an electron-builder default: `windows.menuGroup` was ignored and the shortcut landed in
  the start menu root, `oneClick` defaulted to `true` so the installer ran with no UI, and
  `runAfterFinish` launched the app as soon as the install finished. `MsiSettings` now
  emits `oneClick`, `runAfterFinish`, `createDesktopShortcut`, `createStartMenuShortcut`,
  `menuCategory`, and `shortcutName`. Defaults match electron-builder unless a project
  opts in; `windows.menuGroup` is the default `menuCategory`. `windows.menu` /
  `windows.shortcut` stay unmapped (jpackage `false` vs electron-builder `true`). See
  [Build an MSI for enterprise deployment](/docs/packaging/windows#build-an-msi-for-enterprise-deployment).

## v2.5.9

**Released: 2026-08-31**

### Bug fixes

- **Fatal dialog stack trace** (#627) — the 2.5.8 native dialog stuffed the throwable into
  the message line. On Linux that doubled the title ("Fatal Error" twice on WMs that draw
  dialog titlebars) and the unbounded secondary label sized the dialog to the whole screen.
  The payload is now a short message plus `Throwable.stackTraceToString()`: all three
  platforms render the trace in a bounded scrollable monospace view with a Copy button
  (`NSAlert` via an out-of-process `osascript` child on macOS, an in-memory `DLGTEMPLATE`
  on a fresh thread on Windows, `GtkMessageDialog` on Linux). Compact fallbacks
  (`CFUserNotification` / `MessageBoxW`) keep the `toString()` summary, capped at 2000
  chars so a `VerifyError` bytecode dump cannot silently hide the box. See
  [Handle uncaught exceptions](/docs/windows#handle-uncaught-exceptions).

---

## v2.5.8

**Released: 2026-08-31**

### New features

- **Native fatal-error dialog** (#622 / #623) — an exception that escaped a Tao event
  dispatch used to be cleared at the JNI boundary, leaving a frozen, silent, unclosable
  window. The default path now logs the stack at `SEVERE`, shows a blocking native dialog
  (`CFUserNotification` on macOS, `MessageBoxW` on a dedicated thread on Windows,
  `GtkMessageDialog` on Linux), exits the Tao loop, and rethrows so `nucleusApplication` /
  `taoApplication` end with exit code 1. The dialog is shown after the loop has exited — a
  modal pump inside a tao callback deadlocks the main thread. Skip it with
  `-Dnucleus.tao.fatalErrorDialog=false` for unattended runs. See
  [Handle uncaught exceptions](/docs/windows#handle-uncaught-exceptions).
- **`WindowExceptionHandlerFactory`** (#621 / #625) — Tao mirror of Compose Desktop's AWT
  factory. Provide `LocalWindowExceptionHandlerFactory` to catch failures during layout,
  draw, input, IME, and accessibility; a handler that returns normally drops the frame and
  keeps the window alive. Composition failures still kill the recomposer (Compose's own
  design); swallowing one logs at `SEVERE` instead of leaving a window that never updates.
  The default factory rethrows into the fatal dialog. `@ExperimentalComposeUiApi`. See
  [Handle uncaught exceptions](/docs/windows#handle-uncaught-exceptions).

---

## v2.5.7

**Released: 2026-08-30**

### Bug fixes

- **Popup render re-entry on a scrollbar drag** (#620) — dragging a scrollbar inside a `TrayApp`
  popup scrolls synchronously inside the pointer event, and the `LaunchedEffect`s of the lazy
  items subcomposed by that scroll scheduled a frame the standalone pump rendered inline. Measure
  and layout re-entered while the first pass was still on the stack, throwing
  `performMeasureAndLayout called during measure layout` and leaving the drag with a non-zero
  pending scroll. Every scene entry point of the standalone hosts — pointer, scroll, key dispatch,
  and `setContent` — now runs under the pump's re-entrancy guard, so a frame scheduled mid-pass is
  posted to the Tao main queue instead. See [Notes](/docs/os/tray/tray-app#notes).

---

## v2.5.6

**Released: 2026-08-30**

### Bug fixes

- **Linux IME preedit** (#558 / #613) — the Linux backend pinned `gtk::IMContextSimple`, GTK's
  built-in fallback, which never reaches the system input method: CJK input was not degraded but
  impossible, and typing `aiueo` then confirming left a stray `a`. The backend now uses
  `gtk::IMMulticontext` — ibus or fcitx5 through the GTK immodule on X11, the text-input-v3 client
  on Wayland — and routes its signals into the same `ImePreedit` / `ImeCommit` events as macOS and
  Windows. Keys the input method consumed no longer reach Compose, including the orphan key
  releases Wayland delivers for a filtered press, and the candidate window follows the caret. See
  [Text input](/docs/windows#text-input).
- **Linux candidate window covering the caret** (#613) — GTK places its windows around a cursor
  *area* in logical pixels relative to the toplevel `GdkWindow`, not a point in physical pixels
  relative to the client area, so the candidate list landed on the composition it described. The
  caret rect is scaled and translated by the content widget's allocation, matching the correction
  the Wayland subsurface already applies. See
  [Text input](/docs/windows#text-input).
- **Linux modifier state drift** (#613) — `ModifiersChanged` was emitted only when the key itself
  was a modifier, so Compose tracked Ctrl, Shift, Alt, and Super from press and release
  bookkeeping. Input methods on X11 re-inject the events they forward, and a dropped Control
  release left Compose believing Ctrl was held for the rest of the session: a plain Return read as
  Ctrl+Return. The state is now derived from the GDK modifier mask carried by every event, so it
  self-heals on the next keystroke.
- **macOS press-and-hold accents** (#611 / #612 / #617) — Nucleus forced `ApplePressAndHoldEnabled`
  in four preference domains and guessed from a state machine when the accent picker was active.
  A held letter then did nothing at all on keyboards where the picker cannot engage, and ordinary
  fast typing armed the picker flag and routed the next commit into the replace path, deleting the
  character just committed ("Xcode" landing as "Xcde"). Nucleus no longer reads or writes the user
  default — the OS decides whether a held letter repeats or opens the picker — and the pick is
  applied from the `replacementRange` AppKit sends with `insertText:`, select-then-insert. See
  [Text input](/docs/windows#text-input).
- **Sub-pixel pointer jitter eating clicks** (#615 / #619) — Tao reports cursor positions in
  1/1024 px and macOS emits a `CursorMoved` before every `mouseDown` and `mouseUp`, so a click
  drifting a fraction of a pixel produced a real move delta, started a parent drag gesture, and
  cancelled the tap: selections needed two clicks. Moves under 1 dp from the last dispatched
  position are now suppressed, and `viewConfiguration.touchSlop` is density-scaled to 18.dp
  instead of 18 raw pixels, which had halved every drag and scroll threshold on 2x displays. See
  [How it works](/docs/input/trackpad-gestures).
- **Linux tray popup scroll** (#610) — standalone, overlay, and owner-based popups now feed wheel
  events through the same AWT-shaped dispatch as `TaoWindow`, with the Windows lines-per-notch
  value from `LocalScrollConfig`. Standalone popup frames paint inline when the caller is already
  on the main thread, so a wheel flood cannot starve `MainEventsCleared`. See
  [Notes](/docs/os/tray/tray-app#notes).
- **Auto-launch at half size on GNOME** (#614 / #616) — `graphical-session.target` is reached
  before `gsd-xsettings` writes `Xft.dpi` into the X resource database, so a HiDPI app started at
  login froze `sun.java2d.uiScale` at 1.0 while a manual launch was always correct. The generated
  systemd user unit is ordered after `gnome-session-x11-services-ready.target`. systemd ignores
  ordering on units that are not loaded, so this is a no-op on other desktops. See
  [Notes](/docs/lifecycle/background/launch-at-login#notes).

---

## v2.5.5

**Released: 2026-08-28**

### Bug fixes

- **macOS tray popup and Show Desktop** (#609) — the standalone `NSPanel` had the default
  collection behavior, so "Click wallpaper to reveal desktop" on Sonoma and later Exposé-slid the
  popup away while Compose was already fading it. The panel is now stationary, joins all spaces,
  is fullscreen-auxiliary, and is ignored by window cycling, so `TrayApp` dismisses it itself. See
  [Notes](/docs/os/tray/tray-app#notes).
- **macOS tray popup dismissed by its own icon** (#609) — the outside-click monitor counted a
  `mouseDown` on the `NSStatusItem` and on its native context menu as a click outside the panel,
  so a right-click hid the popup before the menu appeared. Those windows are skipped for
  standalone panels; the left-click toggle stays with the tray callback. See
  [Notes](/docs/os/tray/tray-app#notes).

---

## v2.5.4

**Released: 2026-08-27**

### Bug fixes

- **Linux inbound drop on tray popups** (#605 / #607) — a `TrayApp` popup on Linux is an
  override-redirect X11 window, so GTK `gtk_drag_dest_set` cannot attach. Inbound XDND 5 is
  implemented on the panel event thread and dispatched through `TaoSceneDnD`, matching
  `DecoratedWindow`. See [How it works](/docs/input/drag-and-drop).
- **macOS tray popup scroll** (#608) — popup `NSPanel`s forwarded raw AppKit
  `scrollingDelta`. `TaoWindow` already reshapes those to AWT `preciseWheelRotation` (negate Y,
  physical /10 for precise deltas). Tray and overlay popups now use the same mapping, so wheel
  sign and trackpad magnitude match the main window. See [Notes](/docs/os/tray/tray-app#notes).

---

## v2.5.3

**Released: 2026-08-27**

### Bug fixes

- **Inbound drop on Windows and macOS tray popups** (#604) — `TrayApp` popups are ownerless
  native panels (`WS_POPUP` / `NSPanel`), not `TaoWindow`s, so they had no drop target. Inbound
  file drops now reach Compose `dragAndDropTarget` through `TaoSceneDnD`. Windows native-image
  builds include the JNI metadata for that path. See
  [How it works](/docs/input/drag-and-drop).
- **Windows IME preedit** (#558 / #603) — composition was never forwarded, so the IME painted
  its own floating window near the top-left of the window, and keys the IME had consumed
  (`VK_PROCESSKEY`) still reached Compose: conversion Enter inserted a newline, candidate arrows
  moved the caret, Backspace deleted committed text. Preedit now renders inline, the candidate
  list follows the caret, and consumed keys are dropped. See
  [Text input](/docs/windows#text-input).

## v2.5.2

**Released: 2026-08-27**

### Bug fixes

- **Windows tray popup scroll** (#601) — popup and overlay `WndProc`s reported raw Win32 wheel
  units. `TaoWindow` already negates those to AWT `preciseWheelRotation`; standalone and owned
  popup layers now do the same, so `TrayApp` scrolling is no longer inverted. See
  [Notes](/docs/os/tray/tray-app#notes).
- **Hidden Windows tray popup GPU frames** (#602) — a hidden standalone tray popup no longer
  submits GPU frames.
- **UTF-8 javac/javadoc encoding** (#600) — the compiler and javadoc tasks pin `-encoding UTF-8`,
  so non-ASCII KDoc no longer fails the Windows build.

## v2.5.1

**Released: 2026-08-27**

### New features

- **GraalVM innovation channel defaults to 25.3** (#598) — `GraalvmChannel.INNOVATION` resolves
  to `25i3`. See
  [Provision the toolchain](/docs/performance/graalvm/configuration#provision-the-toolchain).

### Bug fixes

- **Animated `WindowState.size` tremble** (#576 / #597) — programmatic height animation left the
  HWND/NSWindow a frame ahead of the Compose scene, and native resize echoes wrote
  `WindowState.size` backwards. Inner size is applied synchronously, `EVENT_RESIZED` is pushed
  in the same turn, and in-flight programmatic echoes are ignored. See
  [DecoratedWindow parameters](/docs/windows#decoratedwindow-parameters).
- **macOS IME preedit** (#595 / #596 / #599) — CJK composition was invisible and the committing
  Enter leaked as a newline. `setMarkedText` / `unmarkText` are forwarded as preedit, commit
  goes through `commitText`, and keys the IME consumed are dropped. The PressAndHold accent
  picker stays gated while a composition is live, so a segment commit cannot arm the picker and
  hijack the next commit (duplicated segments, U+F7xx tofu). See
  [Text input](/docs/windows#text-input).

## v2.5.0

**Released: 2026-08-26**

### New modules

- **Spell check** (`nucleus.spellcheck`) — checks spelling through the engine each OS already
  ships: Hunspell on Linux (loaded with `dlopen`, no compile-time dependency), `NSSpellChecker`
  on macOS, and the Windows Spell Checking API. Ships a `SpellcheckContextMenu` wrapper that adds
  suggestions and "Add to dictionary" to a Compose text field's context menu, plus an engine API
  (`SpellChecker`, `SpellcheckSession`) usable without Compose. `nucleus-application` exposes it
  as an `api` dependency, so no extra Gradle line is needed. Where no engine is available every
  operation is a no-op rather than an error. See
  [Spell check](/docs/os/spell-check#check-a-text-field).
    - Per-field and process-wide language override via `locale` / `SpellChecker.locale`. See
      [Choose the check language](/docs/os/spell-check#choose-the-check-language).
    - `SpellcheckMenuPlacement` puts suggestions above or below Cut/Copy/Paste. See
      [Place the menu items](/docs/os/spell-check#place-the-menu-items).
    - The "Add to dictionary" label is localized for 45+ locales; user words persist to
      `~/.config/nucleus/spellcheck/<tag>.dic`.

### New features

- **Native context menus** (#542, #544, #545, #547) — `nativeContextMenu = true` on
  `DecoratedWindow` / `HostedWindow` replaces the Compose-drawn context menu with the platform's:
  a real `NSMenu` on macOS, and a Compose flyout styled as Fluent on Windows, Adwaita on GTK
  desktops, and Breeze on Qt desktops. Covers `ContextMenuArea`, text-field Cut/Copy/Paste, and
  spellcheck items. Tao backend only; accepted and ignored on AWT. See
  [Context menus](/docs/os/menus/context-menu#turn-on-the-native-menu).
    - `NucleusContextMenuItem`, `NucleusContextMenuDivider`, and `NucleusContextMenuSubmenu` build
      items with icons and lazy submenus. See
      [Add your own items](/docs/os/menus/context-menu#add-your-own-items).
    - Stock icons carry their platform shortcut label (`⌘C` / `Ctrl+C`), overridable per item.
      Drawn on the Windows and Linux flyouts. See
      [Show keyboard shortcuts](/docs/os/menus/context-menu#show-keyboard-shortcuts).
    - New `LinuxUiToolkit` in `core-runtime` reports whether the session is Gtk or Qt, which is
      also how the Linux menu style is chosen. See
      [Detect the Linux toolkit](/docs/os/menus/context-menu#detect-the-linux-toolkit).
    - `menu-macos` gained the popup primitives behind it: `NativePopupMenuItem`,
      `popUpNativeMenu`, `isNativePopupMenuAvailable`.
- **Overlay windows** (#564, #568) — new window flags for watermarks, desktop widgets, and
  heads-up overlays: `clickThrough` (pointer events pass through), `alwaysOnBottom` (below normal
  windows, mutually exclusive with `alwaysOnTop`), and `visibleOnAllWorkspaces`. All three are
  reactive, with imperative `TaoWindow` setters alongside. See
  [Overlay windows](/docs/windows/overlay-windows#build-a-click-through-watermark).
    - `transparent` is now exposed on the backend-agnostic `DecoratedWindow` and the Material and
      Jewel window wrappers, not just the Tao composable. A fully transparent window drops the
      contour that traced the rectangular window instead of the content, and Compose scenes are
      told the window is transparent so dialog scrims blend against alpha (#559, #561).
    - `forceX11` gives one window an XWayland surface without moving the whole process off
      Wayland, and `TaoWindow.isNativeWaylandSurface` reports what it actually got. Flags that
      cannot work on a native Wayland surface log once per window with the reason. See
      [Take an X11 surface on Wayland](/docs/windows/overlay-windows#take-an-x11-surface-on-wayland).
- **Compose over native views** (#587) — the `NativeView` `content` slot now draws in the
  window's own Compose scene on all three platforms, so Compose siblings declared after the view
  and in-scene `Popup`s paint over it, and overlay content claims its own pointer events. Linux
  supports the `content` slot at all for the first time (Wayland only).
  `Modifier.consumeOverlayPointerEvents()` is deprecated and no longer needed. See
  [Overlay Compose content](/docs/native-content/native-views#overlay-compose-content).
- **Linux clipboard through GTK** (#582, #583) — the Tao clipboard on Linux goes through GDK
  instead of AWT, so copy and paste work in a Wayland-native window and in a session with no
  XWayland. Images (as PNG) and file lists (`text/uri-list` plus the GNOME copied-files target)
  are carried in both directions alongside plain text. No API change: use Compose's
  `LocalClipboard`. See [Copy and paste](/docs/windows/linux-wayland#copy-and-paste).
- **`EnergyManager.acquireAwake`** — returns an `AwakeHandle` that holds one awake request until
  it is closed, so independent features can each keep the machine awake without releasing each
  other. `keepAwake` keeps its single last-writer-wins slot. This also backs Compose's
  `Modifier.keepScreenOn`, which the Tao backend now implements. See
  [Hold several awake requests at once](/docs/lifecycle/energy-manager#hold-several-awake-requests-at-once).
- **Custom scheduler command** (#540) — `SchedulerConfig.executablePath` and
  `executableArguments` point the OS scheduler at a custom launcher instead of the current
  executable. Set them before the first `enqueue`; values are baked into the generated
  plist, unit, or task. See [SchedulerConfig](/docs/lifecycle/background/scheduler#schedulerconfig).
- **Compose 1.12** (#354, #550, #551, #555) — `decorated-window-tao` moves to Compose
  Multiplatform 1.12, with frames driven through `SingleComposeSceneRenderingScope` and the new
  `RectManager` delayed dispatch kept off the AWT event thread.
- **`jdk.unsupported` in the default runtime modules** — `sun.misc.Unsafe` is required by JNA,
  Jewel, and many common libraries, so the module is included by default rather than discovered
  through a runtime failure. See the
  [`nativeDistributions { }` reference](/docs/reference/gradle-dsl#nativedistributions).

### Breaking changes

- **`GenericProvider` requires `https`** — a non-`https` update origin now throws
  `IllegalArgumentException` at construction. The manifest, checksums, and artifact all come from
  that one origin, so plain `http` lets an on-path attacker rewrite the three together and the
  SHA-512 protects nothing. `http` is still accepted for loopback hosts so integration tests can
  serve fixtures without TLS. See [Providers](/docs/packaging/auto-update#providers).

### Bug fixes

- **Self-update scripts written to a private directory** — the detached update script and its log
  went to a fixed path in the shared temp directory (`/tmp/nucleus-update.sh` on Linux), which
  another local user can pre-create as a symlink or a file they own, turning the update into local
  code execution as the app's user. Each run now gets a fresh owner-only (`0700`) directory.
- **Windows update script escaping** — manifest-derived paths are escaped before they reach
  PowerShell.
- **Linux root update helper** — closed a time-of-check/time-of-use window and a downgrade path
  in the privileged helper.
- **Linux update helper leaked a gpg-agent** — the signature check no longer leaves a gpg-agent
  running inside the app's systemd scope.
- **MPRIS invalid D-Bus name** (#548) — an app id that is not a valid D-Bus name no longer hangs
  media-control startup on Linux.
- **Context menu dismissal and first right-click** — the flyout closes when the owning window
  loses focus, and the macOS menu opens on the first right-click in an app that is not yet
  active.
- **Tao fixes** — the dialog close button animates its hover like `DecoratedWindow`; a native
  session that swallows a mouse-up no longer leaves a stuck button; Adwaita separators follow
  libadwaita's `currentColor` rule.

---

## v2.4.5

**Released: 2026-08-16**

### Bug fixes

- **`Dp.Unspecified` wrap-content window size** (#535) — `DecoratedWindow` no longer
  passes NaN through to the native surface when a `WindowState` / `DialogState` axis is
  `Dp.Unspecified`. Wrap-content axes are measured after the first composition and
  applied, matching Compose Desktop. See
  [DecoratedWindow parameters](/docs/windows#decoratedwindow-parameters).
- **Linux discrete mouse-wheel scroll** (#533) — GDK only fills `delta_x` / `delta_y`
  for smooth (trackpad) events. A discrete wheel notch arrived with a zero delta, so
  Compose never scrolled. Direction is now mapped to a unit delta.
- **Win11 caption-button hover fade** (#537) — platform caption buttons use the system
  hover fade duration. See
  [Window controls](/docs/windows/window-scaffold#place-the-window-controls).

---

## v2.4.4

**Released: 2026-08-14**

### Bug fixes

- **Win11 CSD corners clipped** (#527) — windowed CSD draws the 8px rounded contour
  through DWM so the Compose frame is not clipped at the corners. See
  [DecoratedWindow notes](/docs/windows#notes).
- **macOS press-and-hold accent picker** (#529 / #530) — key-repeat now reaches
  `interpretKeyEvents:`, so AppKit's PressAndHold menu opens. Picking an accent
  replaces the already-committed base letter (`e` → `é`) instead of appending.
- **Windows multi-monitor popup DPI** (#528) — popups and `DecoratedDialog` pick up
  the target monitor's DPI and work-area constraints when they open on a different
  display from the owner. See [Per-monitor HiDPI notes](/docs/windows/hidpi#notes).

## v2.4.3

**Released: 2026-08-13**

### Bug fixes

- **Windows CSD frame hidden by DWM** (#523 / #522 / #520) — windowed CSD (no Mica/Acrylic)
  clears only the DWM border fill so the Compose frame stroke is visible, while the Win11
  8px rounded clip and drop shadow stay. See
  [DecoratedWindow notes](/docs/windows#notes).
- **`appResources` missing from GraalVM native packages** (#524) — `prepareAppResources` is
  copied next to the native binary and `compose.application.resources.dir` is set for
  `packageGraalvmNative` and `runWithNativeAgent`. Sidecars such as Dawn's `dxil.dll` load
  the same way as `run` / jpackage. See
  [GraalVM tasks — metadata, installers, and helpers](/docs/performance/graalvm/tasks-ci#metadata-installers-and-helpers).

## v2.4.2

**Released: 2026-08-12**

### Bug fixes

- **Windows sibling GPU cache purge** (#519 / #514) — resize-path Skia cache purges bind
  the host's own ANGLE context first, so a sibling window's `WM_PAINT` cannot leave another
  unshared context current and delete that window's glyph atlas and icons. See
  [GPU render context notes](/docs/native-content/gpu-render-context).
- **`nativeLinuxHandles` on Windows and macOS** (#518) — the Linux-only JNI entry is now
  platform-guarded. Detaching a tab into a popup with `WindowPosition.Absolute` no longer
  throws `UnsatisfiedLinkError`. See
  [DecoratedWindow parameters](/docs/windows#decoratedwindow-parameters).

## v2.4.1

**Released: 2026-08-12**

### Bug fixes

- **White region on Windows off-screen windows** (#516) — a window created partly off-screen
  no longer stays white in the previously clipped area after you drag it into view. Each
  `WM_MOVE` requests a full present so newly exposed pixels are filled.

## v2.4.0

**Released: 2026-08-11**

### Highlights

- **`TaoGpuRenderContext` — in-process GPU on the scene's device.** Map engines, 3D viewports,
  and charting can allocate render targets on the window's own Skia `DirectContext` and native
  device (Metal / ANGLE GLES / native EGL) with no second GPU, no shareable handle, and no
  per-frame cross-device copy. `TextureView` remains the contract for foreign producers. See
  [GPU render context](/docs/native-content/gpu-render-context).
- **`AwakeMode` — keep the system awake without forcing the display.**
  `EnergyManager.keepAwake(AwakeMode.SYSTEM_ONLY)` lets the screen saver and display sleep behave
  normally during long background work. `keepScreenAwake()` remains as a deprecated forwarder.
  See [Keep the system awake](/docs/lifecycle/energy-manager#keep-the-system-awake).
- **Public ABI freeze.** Published runtime modules run under Kotlin `explicitApi()` with
  kotlinx binary-compatibility-validator baselines (`api/*.api`); `apiCheck` is part of
  `check` / `preMerge`. Exception: `decorated-window-jewel` until BCV can read JVM 25 class files.

### New features

- **`windows.msi { perMachine }`** (#480) — install-scope DSL aligned with `nsis { perMachine }`.
  `windows.perUserInstall` is deprecated (inverted meaning) but still works when `msi.perMachine`
  is unset. MSI remains per-machine by default. See
  [Build an MSI](/docs/packaging/windows#build-an-msi-for-enterprise-deployment).

### Improvements

- **Unified JUL logging and renamed tray log API** (#491) — runtime modules log through
  `java.util.logging`; `composeNativeTrayLoggingLevel` → `nucleusLoggingLevel` /
  `NucleusLoggingLevel` (deprecated aliases retained).
- **Safer updater construction** (#493) — provider validated at construction, config snapshotted,
  downloads staged privately instead of a predictable shared temp path. See
  [Auto-update](/docs/packaging/auto-update).
- **Windows outbound drag** (#482) — `DoDragDrop` deferred off Compose pointer dispatch so
  outbound drag frames paint without reentrancy. See
  [Drag and drop](/docs/input/drag-and-drop).

### Bug fixes

- **macOS live-resize trembling** (#476) — content no longer trails AppKit bounds during corner
  resize.
- **Windows interactive resize lag** (#479) — VSync dropped through the modal resize loop so
  content tracks the border drag.
- **Frame-paced GPU through modal loops** (#489, #505) — keep VSync on Windows move/resize and
  Linux resize bursts when the scene hosts `TextureView` imports or `TaoGpuRenderContext`
  consumers. See [GPU render context](/docs/native-content/gpu-render-context#pace-frames).
- **macOS Metal render-thread leak** (#495) — autorelease pool around every render-thread task.
- **`LocalComposeSceneContext` under `DecoratedWindow`** (#499) — Popup / Dialog / DropdownMenu
  / Tooltip inside decorated window content no longer throw. See
  [DecoratedWindow](/docs/windows).
- **macOS overlay detach / focusable retain** (#496), **Wayland popup buffer_scale** (#508),
  **macOS scene density from the window's display** (#509), **zoom-button tiling hover menu**
  (#511), **RTL title-bar constraints while fullscreen** (#512).

---

## v2.3.2

**Released: 2026-08-07**

### New features

- **`HostedWindow` / `HostedDialog` composition hosts** (#473) — libraries and navigation
  open secondary windows without hard-coding Compose Desktop's AWT `Window`/`Dialog` or a
  specific design-system chrome. `nucleusApplication` provides
  `LocalNucleusWindowHost` / `LocalNucleusDialogHost` (defaults: `DecoratedWindow` /
  `DecoratedDialog`); override the host to inject Material, Jewel, or app chrome. See
  [Hosted windows](/docs/windows#route-windows-through-a-host).

### Bug fixes

- **Secondary window drag and system controls** (#472) — re-provide `LocalTaoWindow` and
  `LocalTitleBarInfo` after bridging parent locals into a secondary Tao scene so title-bar
  drag, double-click maximize, and min/max/close bind to the child window. `BasicTitleBar`
  uses `Modifier.windowDragArea(window)` so drag does not depend on a parent
  `LocalTaoWindow`. See
  [Open a window from composition](/docs/windows#open-a-window-from-composition)
  and [Drag areas](/docs/windows/window-scaffold#add-drag-areas).
- **Wayland `popupFor` CSD content origin** (#474) — `TaoWindow.setOuterPosition` adds the
  parent hidden-titlebar CSD content origin for native Wayland popup overlays, so
  content-space coordinates (tab ghosts, HUDs) no longer drift by the theme shadow margin.
  In-scene popup layers no longer double-apply that offset. See
  [DecoratedWindow parameters](/docs/windows#decoratedwindow-parameters).

## v2.3.1

**Released: 2026-08-06**

### New features

- **XDG Desktop Portal parent for Tao windows** (#466) — `TaoWindow.xdgPortalParent()`,
  `x11PortalParent` / `x11WindowId`, and `exportXdgForeignHandle()` / `XdgForeignExport`
  so FileKit and other portal clients can parent file choosers on X11 and Wayland
  (`x11:<hex>` / `wayland:<token>`). See [Native file dialogs](/docs/os/file-dialogs#attach-the-dialog-to-a-window).
- **`TaoWindow.nsWindowHandle` on macOS** (#469) — owning `NSWindow*` for sheet /
  dialog parenting (`beginSheetModalForWindow:`); distinct from `nativeHandle` which is
  the Compose host `NSView*`. See
  [Native file dialogs](/docs/os/file-dialogs#attach-the-dialog-to-a-window).
- **Per-format compression for AppImage and Windows portable** (#468) —
  `linux.appImage { compressionLevel }` and `windows.portable { compressionLevel }`
  override the root `nativeDistributions.compressionLevel`, so DEB/DMG can stay on
  `Ultra` while AppImage/portable use `Normal` or `Store`. See
  [Build an AppImage](/docs/packaging/linux#build-an-appimage) and
  [Portable mode](/docs/packaging/windows#enable-portable-mode).

### Improvements

- **L1 GraalVM metadata expansion** (#470) — richer ktor (client plugins, server,
  websockets), new `androidx-sqlite-bundled` pack, broader JDK FFM/VarHandle/Module
  coverage, `AtomicInt` / `AtomicRef` and `kotlin.kotlin_builtins`. See
  [Automatic metadata](/docs/performance/graalvm/automatic-metadata).
- **Kotlin agent phantoms always dropped on cleanup** (#470) — tracing-agent mapped
  types (`kotlin.Any`, `kotlin.Int`, `FunctionN`, collections) are removed during
  `cleanupGraalvmMetadata` without needing `removeUnresolvable`. See
  [Clean up manual entries](/docs/performance/graalvm/automatic-metadata#clean-up-manual-entries).

### Bug fixes

- **KMP named JVM targets and orphan detection** (#467) — project-class / orphan
  detection uses the application target's compilation outputs
  (`jvm("desktop")` → `desktopMainClasses`) instead of hardcoded `jvm`/`main` paths;
  nest-internal edges no longer hide real Room `*_Impl` classes. See
  [Detect orphan project classes](/docs/performance/graalvm/automatic-metadata#detect-orphan-project-classes).
- **Linux NativeView opaque region** (#471) — clear the full-surface opaque region while
  a `NativeView` is attached so GTK (e.g. WebKit) shows through the EGL subsurface again
  after #447. See [Native views](/docs/native-content/native-views).
- **Linux NativeView overlay click offset** (#471) — `consumeOverlayPointerEvents` maps
  pointer events into content coordinates (window bin), matching CSD shadow-margin
  normalisation. See
  [Overlay Compose content](/docs/native-content/native-views#overlay-compose-content).

## v2.3.0

**Released: 2026-08-06**

### Highlights

- **`TextureView` — external GPU textures in the Compose scene.** Composite decoder or engine
  frames with real z-order, clipping, and `graphicsLayer` transforms, and no CPU frame copy.
  Windows uses ANGLE/D3D11 shared handles, macOS Metal/`IOSurface`, Linux DMA-BUF/`EGLImage`
  (including planar YUV I420/YV12). Frame updates go through `TextureViewController.markFrameAvailable`
  (draw-only invalidation). See [TextureView](/docs/native-content/texture-view),
  [platform sources](/docs/native-content/texture-view#platform-sources), and
  [how it works](/docs/native-content/texture-view#platform-sources).
- **Per-platform notification options on the common DSL.** `notification { }` accepts
  `linux { }`, `macos { }`, and `windows { }` blocks applied only on the matching OS
  (urgency, interruption level, toast scenario, …). See
  [Platform-specific options](/docs/os/notifications#platform-specific-options).
- **Differential auto-update downloads.** `updater-runtime` reassembles installers from the
  previous artifact plus HTTP range requests for changed blocks (electron-builder block maps).
  On by default via `differentialDownload`. See
  [Differential downloads](/docs/packaging/auto-update#differential-downloads).
- **`LocalNucleusApplicationScope` and receiver-less windows.** Open secondary
  `DecoratedWindow` / `DecoratedDialog` from deep in the composition without threading the
  application receiver. See
  [Open a window from composition](/docs/windows#open-a-window-from-composition).
- **Live `isSystemInDarkTheme()` under `nucleusApplication`.** Compose's `LocalSystemTheme` is
  fed from `darkmode-detector`, so official and library call sites track OS theme changes.
  See [Bridge to Compose `isSystemInDarkTheme`](/docs/os/theme/dark-mode#how-nucleusapplication-provides-the-theme).

### New features

- **`TextureView` + platform source factories** (#429 / #338) — `TextureView`,
  `TextureViewController`, `rememberTextureViewController`,
  `nucleusD3D11SharedTextureSource`, `nucleusIOSurfaceTextureSource` /
  `nucleusMetalTextureSource`, `nucleusDmaBufTextureSource` /
  `nucleusEglImageTextureSource` / `nucleusYuvDmaBufTextureSource`, plus Linux acquire-fence
  signalling. Samples: mediafoundation-demo, avfoundation-demo, gstreamer-demo. See
  [TextureView](/docs/native-content/texture-view#show-a-texture).
- **Platform blocks on `notification { }`** (#436 / #397) — `LinuxNotificationScope`
  (`urgency`, `category`, `transient`, `resident`, `expireTimeout`),
  `MacNotificationScope` (`interruptionLevel`, `relevanceScore`, `subtitle`),
  `WindowsNotificationScope` (`scenario`, `duration`). See
  [Platform-specific options](/docs/os/notifications#platform-specific-options).
- **Differential downloads in `NucleusUpdater`** (#428) — uses published `.blockmap` companions
  (NSIS, macOS ZIP/DMG) and AppImage-embedded maps; `DownloadProgress.isDifferential`;
  `UpdaterConfig.differentialDownload` (default `true`) and `cacheDir`. See
  [Differential downloads](/docs/packaging/auto-update#differential-downloads) and
  [Builder fields](/docs/packaging/auto-update#builder-fields).
- **`LocalNucleusApplicationScope`** (#449 / #438) — CompositionLocal provided by
  `nucleusApplication` on AWT and Tao; receiver-less `DecoratedWindow` / `DecoratedDialog`
  overloads. See
  [Open a window from composition](/docs/windows#open-a-window-from-composition).
- **System theme bridge** (#463) — `ProvideNucleusSystemTheme` wires `isSystemInDarkMode()` into
  `LocalSystemTheme`; `darkmode-detector` is an `api` dependency of `nucleus-application`. See
  [Bridge to Compose `isSystemInDarkTheme`](/docs/os/theme/dark-mode#how-nucleusapplication-provides-the-theme).
- **Exact reachability metadata on the GraalVM dev loop** (#453 / #440) —
  `graalvm { exactReachabilityMetadata = ExactReachabilityMetadata.APP_PACKAGES }` (default)
  on `runGraalvmNative` only; `-Pnucleus.graalvm.missingRegistration=warn|exit|throw`. See
  [Exact reachability on the dev loop](/docs/performance/graalvm/configuration#catch-missing-registrations-in-the-dev-loop).
- **Orphan project-class detection** (#460 / #441) —
  `detectOrphanProjectClasses` (default `true`) registers public no-arg constructors for
  reflectively-only types (Room `*_Impl`, …); opt-in `reflectionForProjectClasses`. See
  [Detect orphan project classes](/docs/performance/graalvm/automatic-metadata#detect-orphan-project-classes).
- **GraalVM innovation channel defaults to 25.2** (#432) — `GraalvmChannel.INNOVATION` resolves
  to `25i2`. See [Provision the toolchain](/docs/performance/graalvm/configuration#provision-the-toolchain).

### Improvements

- **Silent DEB/RPM self-update packaging** (#457) — `nucleus-update-helper` ships in the package
  payload so `dpkg -S` / `rpm -qf` attribute it; afterInstall only installs polkit; detached
  `*.asc` uploaded next to packages. See
  [Passwordless updates on Linux](/docs/packaging/auto-update#set-up-passwordless-updates-on-linux).
- **AppImage post-update relaunch** (#465 / #178) — replace-in-place while the old mount holds,
  clean environment on restart (`APPDIR` / `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` unset). See
  [Supported formats](/docs/packaging/auto-update#supported-formats).
- **Linux portal global hotkeys** (#455 / #264) — stable `shortcut_id` from modifiers+keyCode,
  debounced `BindShortcuts`, `GlobalHotKeyManager.commitRegistrations()` and `portalShortcutId`.
  See [Linux portal registrations](/docs/os/global-hotkey#linux-portal-registrations).
- **Unresolvable cleanup metadata reporting** (#461 / #439) — `cleanupGraalvmMetadata` reports
  types that resolve nowhere; optional
  `-Pnucleus.graalvm.cleanup.removeUnresolvable=true`. See
  [Clean up manual entries](/docs/performance/graalvm/automatic-metadata#clean-up-manual-entries).
- **Metadata dirs as `nativeImageCompile` inputs** (#459 / #431) — editing reachability metadata
  invalidates the native image task instead of serving a stale binary.
- **`mlProfileInference = false` gated on Oracle** (#458 / #452) — community toolchains skip
  `-H:-MLProfileInference` (unrecognized) with a warning. See
  [graalvm { } reference](/docs/performance/graalvm/configuration#graalvm---reference).

### Bug fixes

- **Outbound OS drag freezes the Tao host** (#434) — Windows, macOS, and Linux keep the render
  loop alive during `DoDragDrop` / AppKit / GTK drag via a shared `DragPump`. See
  [Drag and drop](/docs/input/drag-and-drop).
- **Wayland resize flash / shift** (#462 / #444) — paint at last drawable size until
  `wl_egl_window_resize` applies on the next present. See [Wayland](/docs/windows/linux-wayland).
- **Linux Compose subsurface opaque region** (#447 / #446) — `wl_surface.set_opaque_region`
  with transparent corners preserved for the CSD shadow.
- **Linux jpackage SIGSEGV on long classpaths** (#456 / #454) — after `jpackage`, multi-entry
  `app.classpath` is collapsed into a pathing jar (JDK-8380085 workaround).
- **FSEvents roots reached through a symlink** (#448 / #442) — macOS temp dirs under `/var` →
  `/private/var` deliver events again. See [Filesystem watcher](/docs/lifecycle/fs-watcher).
- **SLF4J no longer forced to build-time init** (#450 / #443) — avoids image-heap failures with
  run-time SLF4J 2.x backends; opt in via `buildArgs` if you want build-time init. See
  [Set build arguments](/docs/performance/graalvm/configuration#set-build-arguments).
- **`runWithNativeAgent` toolchain mismatch** (#451 / #437) — forks through `JavaLauncher`
  instead of a conflicting `executable` property.
- **Linux popup / tray panel EGL neutrality** (TextureView series / #350) — popup layers and
  tray panels no longer break the window EGL binding; Wayland popups offset by CSD content origin.

### Samples

- **mediafoundation-demo**, **avfoundation-demo**, **gstreamer-demo** — end-to-end video into
  `TextureView` on Windows, macOS, and Linux (native-image builds for the GStreamer sample).

## v2.2.0

**Released: 2026-08-03**

### Highlights

- **Window scaffold and chrome primitives.** Full-window layouts without giving up native drag, caption zones, or traffic-light insets. Compose content through `WindowScaffold` with `TitleBarPlacement.Docked` or `Overlay`, and rebuild chrome from public APIs: `Modifier.windowDragArea` / `noWindowDrag`, `WindowControls`, macOS `windowGlassRegion`, Windows 11 `WindowsBackdrop` (Mica / Acrylic / MicaAlt), `WindowBackground`, and `WindowAppearance`. See [Window scaffold](/docs/windows/window-scaffold), [chrome primitives](/docs/windows/window-scaffold#build-a-custom-title-bar), and [platform materials](/docs/windows/window-scaffold#match-the-window-to-the-app-theme).
- **GraalVM tasks mirror the JVM pipeline.** `runGraalvmNative` is the fast dev loop (`-Ob` quick-build); full optimization lives on `runGraalvmNativeDistributable`. New `createGraalvmNativeDistributable` and `packageGraalvmNativeDistributionForCurrentOS` match `createDistributable` / `packageDistributionForCurrentOS`. The native app folder lands under `compose/binaries/<app>/graalvm-app`. See [Tasks & CI — public surface](/docs/performance/graalvm/tasks-ci#gradle-tasks) and [output locations](/docs/performance/graalvm/tasks-ci#output-layout).
- **Type-safe garbage collector selection.** `garbageCollector = GarbageCollector.Z` on the JVM path and `graalvm { garbageCollector = NativeImageGarbageCollector.G1 }` for native images. G1 is Oracle GraalVM + Linux only and degrades with a warning elsewhere. Heap-percent flags follow the selected collector. See [Choose a garbage collector](/docs/performance/graalvm/configuration#choose-a-garbage-collector) and the [Gradle DSL](/docs/reference/gradle-dsl#application----jvmapplication).

### New features

- **`WindowScaffold` + `TitleBarPlacement`** (#412, #129) — design-system-agnostic chrome host. `Docked` keeps the classic bar-above-content layout; `Overlay` fills content to the full window height and hands the measured bar height back as top `PaddingValues`. Optional `autoHideInFullscreen` and `passThroughToContent` on `Overlay` for immersive and hit-test-through title bars (#423). See [title bar placement](/docs/windows/window-scaffold#place-the-title-bar).
- **Chrome primitives for custom title bars** (#412) — `Modifier.windowDragArea` / `noWindowDrag`, `WindowControls` + `WindowControlsRenderer`, `WindowDoubleClickAction`, and `LocalWindowChromeInsets` so toolbars can place content around traffic lights and KDE edge padding. See [chrome primitives](/docs/windows/window-scaffold#build-a-custom-title-bar), [drag areas](/docs/windows/window-scaffold#add-drag-areas), and [window controls](/docs/windows/window-scaffold#place-the-window-controls).
- **Platform materials** (#412) — `Modifier.windowGlassRegion` (macOS System Settings-style sidebar/content/inspector panes), `WindowsBackdrop` (DWM Mica / Acrylic / MicaAlt with tier pin), `WindowBackground` (clear colour from inside the content tree), `WindowAppearance` (force light/dark on native surfaces). See [platform materials](/docs/windows/window-scaffold#match-the-window-to-the-app-theme), [macOS glass](/docs/windows/window-scaffold#add-a-macos-glass-region), and [Windows 11 backdrops](/docs/windows/window-scaffold#add-a-windows-11-backdrop).
- **`DecoratedWindow(transparent = true)` on Tao** (#419) — full-window transparency for ghost overlays. Pair with `undecorated = true` for borderless see-through windows. AWT is out of scope; call the Tao `DecoratedWindow` (e.g. via `taoApplication`). See [transparent overlays](/docs/windows/window-scaffold#make-a-transparent-borderless-window) and [DecoratedWindow on Tao](/docs/windows/window-scaffold).
- **Native GTK CSD drop shadow** (#422) — Linux client-side decorations use the hidden-titlebar pattern so the shadow tracks the window correctly, including during interactive moves. See [DecoratedWindow notes](/docs/windows#notes).
- **AccessKit on Windows** (#420) — Windows accessibility now shares the AccessKit wire path with Linux (UIA provider). AccessKit crates bumped across both platforms; Linux AT-SPI probes match Windows severity. See [Accessibility](/docs/input/accessibility).
- **`garbageCollector` on the JVM and native DSL** (#408) — `GarbageCollector` (`SERIAL`, `PARALLEL`, `G1`, `Z`, `SHENANDOAH`, `EPSILON`) for HotSpot; `NativeImageGarbageCollector` (`SERIAL`, `G1`, `EPSILON`) for `--gc=`. Unset keeps JVM ergonomics / native-image Serial. See [Choose a garbage collector](/docs/performance/graalvm/configuration#choose-a-garbage-collector) and [Gradle DSL — GraalVM](/docs/reference/gradle-dsl#graalvm--graalvmsettings).
- **`NucleusApplicationScope` implements Compose `ApplicationScope`** (#372) — libraries scoped to plain `ApplicationScope` (for example ComposeNativeTray) resolve inside `nucleusApplication { }` without a separate overload set. See [DecoratedWindow notes](/docs/windows#notes).

### Ecosystem (separate repos)

Published around the 2.2 line; versioned independently of Nucleus:

- **[compose-macos-26-ui](https://github.com/NucleusFramework/compose-macos-26-ui)** — macOS 26 design system + `MacosDecoratedWindow`. Docs: [macOS toolkit](/docs/toolkits/macos).
- **[compose-fluent-ui](https://github.com/NucleusFramework/compose-fluent-ui)** — Fluent Design + `FluentDecoratedWindow`. Docs: [Fluent toolkit](/docs/toolkits/fluent).
- **[yaru-compose-ui](https://github.com/NucleusFramework/yaru-compose-ui)** — Yaru / GNOME design system + `YaruDecoratedWindow`. Docs: [Yaru toolkit](/docs/toolkits/yaru).

### Improvements

- **macOS `.app` bundle name consistency** (#409) — every artifact (DMG, ZIP, …) ships the same bundle name derived from `appName`, so auto-update no longer deletes one path and fails to open another when `appName != packageName`.
- **Glitch-free Windows fullscreen toggle** and macOS fullscreen transition ramp parity (#412 / #413).
- **macOS display-scale follow** when the window hops between displays (#412). See [Per-monitor HiDPI](/docs/windows/hidpi).

### Bug fixes

- **NsView `setBounds` / resize on layout changes** (#421) — embedded macOS native views update their frames when Compose layout changes. See [Native views](/docs/native-content/native-views).
- **Scheme-only deep link URIs** (#425 / #414) — `DeepLinkHandler` accepts opaque forms such as `myapp:?query=…` (common from `xdg-open`), not only `scheme://` authority forms. Windows drive paths are still rejected. See [Deep links — how it works](/docs/lifecycle/deep-links).
- **Hot-reload gate matches the published Tao artifact name** (#424 / #415).

## v2.1.10

**Released: 2026-07-26**

### Bug fixes

- **Resolve JDK library jars on JMOD-less JDKs** (#407) — ProGuard release packaging failed on JDKs that ship without a `jmods` directory (Temurin 25+ after JEP 493). The task falls back to extracting the run-time image with `jimage extract` and passes one class root per module. JDKs that still ship `jmods` keep the previous path.
- **Stop CSD shadow tracing while the window is dragged** (#393 / #383) — the Linux client-side-decoration shadow no longer leaves a trail during interactive window moves.

## v2.1.9

**Released: 2026-07-26**

### Bug fixes

- **Survive obfuscation for all JNI bridges and coroutines** (#405) — with `obfuscate = true` on by default since 2.1.6, release builds crashed at runtime. The module-by-module JNI keep list is replaced by generic rules that keep the names of any `dev.nucleusframework` class declaring native methods plus `*Bridge`/`*Jni` objects whole, fixing `UnsatisfiedLinkError` in the modules the list missed (autolaunch, launcher-linux, notification-linux/macos, service-management-macos, system-info, taskbar-progress, graalvm-runtime). Dropping `allowoptimization` from the `kotlinx.**` safety rules fixes a `VerifyError` in `ChannelsKt.trySendBlocking`; shrinking stays fully active. The system-color and media-control native builds now invoke `build.bat` by absolute path like every other module.

### CI

- **Microsoft JDK on Windows, Temurin elsewhere** (#406) — replaces JBR as the `setup-nucleus` JDK. The Microsoft Build of OpenJDK is the only mainstream distribution shipping GA windows-aarch64 builds for current LTS majors, and `decorated-window-jbr` needs no JBR at build time since the JBR API comes from the `org.jetbrains.runtime:jbr-api` artifact.

---

## v2.1.8

**Released: 2026-07-26**

### New features

- **`aotCache { }` configuration block** (#404) — exposes the AOT cache portability trade-off: `compatibility = NATIVE` restores the JDK default for locally-built or fleet-homogeneous deployments, and `extraTrainingJvmArgs` is an escape hatch for the training run. `enableAotCache` keeps working as a shorthand.

### Bug fixes

- **CPU-portable AOT cache by default** (#404) — the JDK 25+ AOT cache also stores machine code (i2c/c2i adapter blobs) emitted for the training machine's CPU features, and HotSpot records no ISA information for that region before JDK 27, so a cache built on a CI runner died with `EXCEPTION_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION`/`SIGILL` on a narrower CPU. The cache now defaults to metadata only (`-XX:-AOTAdapterCaching` on both the training run and the shipped launcher), keeping the class loading and linking gains and leaving the JIT untouched at runtime. `compatibility = NATIVE` warns at build time when the bundled runtime predates the CPU-feature validation added after JDK 26.

---

## v2.1.7

**Released: 2026-07-26**

### Breaking changes

- **GraalVM Community Edition is now the default toolchain** (#403) — the auto-provisioned toolchain was Oracle GraalVM, governed by the GraalVM Free Terms and Conditions. The GFTC only allows redistributing the Program provided you do not charge your licensees any fees associated with such distribution or use, and the plugin copies GraalVM runtime libraries next to the packaged executable — so that clause silently reached every app built with Nucleus. GraalVM CE (GPLv2 + Classpath Exception) carries no such restriction and is now the default via `GraalvmDistribution.COMMUNITY`. Oracle GraalVM stays available behind an explicit opt-in that logs a licensing warning. `-O3`, `--pgo` and `-H:AdvancedObfuscation` degrade to a warning under a community toolchain, and `runWithPgoInstrument` is not registered at all. The distribution is embedded in the install directory and the CI cache key so an existing Oracle download is never reused, and a `GRAALVM_HOME` whose distribution disagrees with the DSL is ignored.

### Improvements

- **Lazy toolchain provisioning** (#403) — every toolchain provider now resolves in `doFirst`, so an IDE sync or `gradlew tasks` no longer downloads a JDK.

### Bug fixes

- **Survive GitHub API rate limits when resolving Community Edition** (#403) — a pinned version (`"25.0.2"`) now constructs the download URL directly instead of listing releases, making the documented pin-a-version workaround work offline; the native-image build steps pass `GITHUB_TOKEN` so the releases API call is authenticated. Floating versions (`"25"`, `"25i1"`) still need the API.
- **Decode Mach-O `cpu_type` in the file's own byte order** (#402) — `MH_CIGAM_64` is the byte-swapped magic that every little-endian macOS dylib starts with on disk, so `cpu_type` was read swapped and every thin dylib reported `arch=UNKNOWN`. Cross-checked against `lipo` on 57 real dylibs: 44 decoded wrong before, all 57 are correct now. Also recognizes `FAT_MAGIC_64` alongside `FAT_MAGIC`, and hoists the path-plus-header merge into `NativeLibArchDetector.detectEntry` so the strip transform shares it.
- **Extract the target-arch native lib, not the first match** (#401) — native libs whose JAR path carries an arch but no OS token were extracted for the wrong architecture: `detectInfo` discarded the path-detected arch whenever the OS was `UNKNOWN`, and the 64-byte header buffer was too small to reach the PE machine field. An ARM64 DLL could therefore win the flattening race on an x64 target and fail to load. `detectInfo` now merges path and header information field by field and reads 4096 header bytes. Fixes #399.

---

## v2.1.6

**Released: 2026-07-23**

### New features

- **Advanced obfuscation for native images** (#389) — `graalvm { advancedObfuscation = true }` passes `-H:AdvancedObfuscation=` (Oracle GraalVM only, gated on the resolved toolchain and warning otherwise) so the symbol names baked into the binary — stack traces, heap dumps, `Class#getName`, strings — are obfuscated. Reflection and JNI names from the reachability metadata are preserved automatically, so it is JNI-safe by construction. `-H:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions` is passed alongside it, and `--enable-sbom=export` keeps the SBOM as a build artifact instead of embedding it and re-leaking the dependency list obfuscation hides.
- **Obfuscate-safe ProGuard rules** (#389) — when `proguard { obfuscate = true }`, a bundled `nucleus-obfuscation-safety-rules.pro` is injected automatically to preserve framework names (`androidx.**`, `kotlinx.**`) while still allowing shrinking and optimization, so the Compose and Kotlin runtimes survive renaming and only the app's own packages get obfuscated. Prevents `ClassNotFoundException: androidx.compose.runtime.Composer`. Not injected when obfuscation is off.
- **Desktop-appropriate default max heap for native images** (#390) — native-image's Serial GC defaults the max heap to 80% of physical RAM, far above a desktop app's norm. Nucleus now bakes `-R:MaximumHeapSizePercent=25` for parity with HotSpot's `MaxRAMPercentage`, configurable via `graalvm { maxHeapSizePercent = N }` or an absolute `graalvm { maxHeapSize = "2g" }` (which takes precedence). Both are defaults only, still overridable at runtime with `-Xmx`.
- **`--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED` baked into native images** (#390) — native modules call `System.loadLibrary` from the unnamed module, which since JDK 24 (JEP 472) emits a restricted-method warning and will be blocked in a future release. The JVM run path already passed the flag; the native binary now starts clean too.
- **Pause the render loop while the window is minimized** (#384) — each platform scene host gates its frame body on `window.isMinimized` before the frame-clock tick, so Compose animations park instead of recording and presenting into a hidden surface. This matters most on Windows, where ANGLE's flip-model swapchain never reports occlusion and there is no vsync back-pressure while minimized; restore re-kicks a redraw explicitly.
- **Jewel 0.39 and IntelliJ icons 262** (#395) — bumps Jewel to `0.39.1-262.9437.29`, adds the `intellij-icons-api`/`impl` dependencies that Jewel 0.39's `IntUiTheme` needs, and registers the build-time initialization and reflection entries required to avoid a `Method.invoke` segfault under SVM.

### Bug fixes

- **Scope JNI local refs on permanently-attached upcall threads** (#387) — object-creating upcalls on permanently attached threads never had their local frame popped, leaking local refs for the life of the process. The touch path was the worst: `dispatch_touch` allocated three `long[]` per event, so a sustained touch drag grew the JNI local reference table until it overflowed and aborted the JVM. Each such upcall body is now wrapped in `env.with_local_frame(...)`, covering the Linux touch and drop paths, macOS deep links, and the macOS/Windows accessibility action trampolines.
- **Clear pending JNI exceptions after accessibility and deep-link upcalls** (#385) — the accessibility and deep-link native-to-JVM callbacks invoked `NativeTaoBridge.dispatch*` without `exception_check`/`exception_clear`, unlike every other dispatch path. A throwing Kotlin handler left the exception pending on the long-lived callback thread (AT-SPI/zbus, UIA, AppKit), making the next JNI call on that thread undefined behavior and, under `panic = "abort"`, a process abort with an unrelated-looking crash site. The guard is now applied to all 18 upcall sites.
- **Migrate `-H:IncludeResources` to reachability-metadata globs** (#389) — the deprecated option warned at build time; the resource inclusion patterns moved into the module's `reachability-metadata.json` with identical semantics. The blanket font and icon globs are deliberately kept: they cover resources bundled inside library JARs, such as Jewel's SVG icons, which per-root `autoIncludeResources` does not reach.

### Improvements

- **Shared scene drag-and-drop extracted into `TaoSceneDnD`** (#386) — deduplicates the three platform scene hosts into one shared file, preserving the Linux-specific behavior where `has_files` reflects the presence of a `text/uri-list` target.
- **Jewel-specific native-image metadata moved into `decorated-window-jewel`** (#395) — the Jewel build-time initialization and reflection entries ship only with Jewel consumers; `graalvm-runtime` keeps only the generic slf4j build-time init.

---
